title: D'Andre Swift on fumbles: That's not me
summary: Bears running back D'Andre Swift fumbled four times in his first 33 games with the team, but he's been a little less adept at holding onto the ball in the early stages of this season.
full_text: Bears running back D'Andre Swift fumbled four times in his first 33 games with the team, but he's been a little less adept at holding onto the ball in the early stages of this season. Swift has fumbled twice, including one in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over the Jets. Head coach Ben Johnson called it "egregious" because of the way Swift was holding the ball and Swift was benched in favor of Kyle Monangai for the rest of the game. Swift said there was no big conversation about the benching, but said he understands what happens when you turn the ball over and "I’ll take whatever comes with that." Swift also vowed to make sure it won't happen again in the future. “I know that’s not me ,” Swift said, via Dan Wiederer of TheAthletic.com. “That’s not a part of my game. It hasn’t been. So I’m not about to make it one. That’s over with now.” The Bears haven't revealed their running back plans for this Sunday's game against the Packers, but injury could factor into it. Monangai has not practiced this week due to thumb and toe injuries, so Swift could get the chance to show he's cleaned things up by default.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jalon Daniels: Fast start gave us confidence we could win the game
summary: Quarterback Jalon Daniels and the Buccaneers came into Dallas as big underdogs on Thursday night and the first Cowboys possession of the night did little to suggest oddsmakers had it wrong.
full_text: ' Quarterback Jalon Daniels and the Buccaneers came into Dallas as big underdogs on Thursday night and the first Cowboys possession of the night did little to suggest oddsmakers had it wrong. They rolled 70 yards in four minutes for a touchdown, but the Bucs came up with an answer that foreshadowed the way the game would actually play out. Daniels went 8-of-8 while leading a 10:58 drive that ended with a five-yard touchdown pass to running back Bucky Irving. It was the second-longest scoring drive in Buccaneers history and Daniels said after the game that it gave the Bucs belief that they could win for the first time this season. "That offense is a very high-scoring offense," Daniels said, via Jenna Laine of ESPN.com. "So, the more you're able to keep those playmakers off the field, the more you're able to go out there and get closer and closer to being able to get a win. And the fact that we were able to start the game that way and be able to gain confidence also for the rest of the game, I think that's where it catapulted from." Daniels finished the night 19-of-25 for 189 yards while Irving ran 21 times for 165 yards and another score. The Bucs also won the turnover battle 3-0 and that kind of efficient play made the undrafted rookie quarterback a winner for the first time in the NFL. With Baker Mayfield still recovering from a dislocated thumb, Daniels will likely have at least one more chance to show that he belongs in the league.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dak Prescott did not appreciate stadium worker calling Cowboys' loss "embarrassing"
summary: "Feel free to speak your mind. Just speak it. Don't coward away from the reaction that you're going to get," Prescott said of his exchange with the worker in the tunnel after the game.
full_text: ' As Dak Prescott walked through the AT&T Stadium tunnel to the Cowboys' locker room after Thursday night's loss to the Buccaneers, a stadium worker had one word for him. " Embarrassing ," the worker said as Prescott walked by. Prescott looked at him, kept walking, and then said to a Cowboys employee, "Tough guy. Get his ass out of here." The Cowboys employee walked toward the stadium worker, who appeared to have left the area by the time the Cowboys employee got there. PFT is told the worker was a driver employed by a third-party contractor. Prescott was asked about it after the game and made clear he didn't appreciate it. "When he said it I just happened to look at him, and at that point he looked away, didn't look, and when I turned my head back, he said something else," Prescott said. "So that's the part that, just as a man or a person, feel free to speak your mind. Just speak it. Don't coward away from the reaction that you're going to get. If you're saying it's embarrassing, say it's embarrassing. If you're saying it to me, say it to me. Don't go back on it. That's all it was. I hate that it's even being talked about, to be honest with you." Prescott said he has too much respect for the Buccaneers to use the word "embarrassing" to describe the loss, but he acknowledged it was a game the Cowboys were supposed to win, and said head coach Brian Schottenheimer told the team that. "To use the word 'embarrassing,' it's tough," Prescott said. "I feel like I'm discrediting the NFL if I use that, in particular the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the great Todd Bowles coach, defensive-coached team. The guy's been a winning coach for a long time and whether he's been a head coach or a defensive coordinator. The plan, what they did tonight, is the reason for that. To say 'embarrassing,' I think I'd be discrediting them. But we were definitely supposed to win this game. It was a game we were supposed to have on paper. I think Schotty said it best in the locker room. in this league You've got to win the games you're supposed to win, and when a winless team comes into your home stadium on a Thursday night, prime time game, yeah, we're supposed to win that. It sucks, right up close to embarrassing, but I don't know if I would say that." And Prescott was not happy with the guy who did say that.
author: Michael David Smith

title: After Jalon Daniels leads Bucs over Cowboys, NFL teams are 8-4 when starting a backup QB
summary: Injuries to starting quarterbacks have not derailed teams this season.
full_text: Jalon Daniels, the Buccaneers' undrafted rookie backup quarterback, played surprisingly well on Thursday night in an upset win over the Cowboys. But maybe it shouldn't have been so surprising. Daniels continued a notable trend of this early NFL season, with teams winning more than they lose when starting a backup quarterback. After Daniels and the Bucs won on Thursday night, NFL teams are now 8-4 in the 12 games started by backup quarterbacks this season. In addition to the Bucs going 1-1 with Daniels, teams that have won games with their backups this year are the Giants (2-0 with Jameis Winston), the Bears (2-0 with Case Keenum), the Vikings (1-0 with Carson Wentz), the Seahawks (1-0 with Drew Lock) and the Commanders (1-1 with Marcus Mariota). The Falcons drag the record down by going 0-2 with their third-string quarterback, Cooper Rush, who looked like a third-string quarterback when Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa were both injured for the first two games of the season. Atlanta is the only team that has started a backup quarterback and failed to win at least one game with him. No team wants to lose its starting quarterback, but the results this season show that losing a starter doesn't have to be a disaster. Teams can and do win games with backup quarterbacks. This season, they've won twice as many games as they've lost.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bengals' Jordan Battle: Malik Willis taps the ball before he throws, we can key on that
summary: NFL players and coaches spend many hours studying film of their upcoming opponents to find tendencies that can give them an advantage on Sunday.
full_text: NFL players and coaches spend many hours studying film of their upcoming opponents to find tendencies that can give them an advantage on Sunday. Bengals safety Jordan Battle found such a tendency with Sunday's opponent, Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis. For some reason, Battle decided to tell the press about it before the game, giving Willis and the Dolphins an opportunity to fix it before Sunday. Battle told reporters in the Bengals' locker room that Willis has a tell that lets the defense know when he's about to throw the ball, so Battle and his fellow defensive backs can break on the ball a split-second earlier. Or at least they can if Willis doesn't fix it, now that Battle blabbed. “He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle said. "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that that gives the read the break. He's obviously dangerous with his feet. We know we've got to be alert for that. Third and longs, they will run quarterback draws, and in the passing game, he will extend plays. So we've got to be good downfield. DBs are plastering, so we got to be alert for that. He will take chances. We just got to be on, be alert on guys where they line up.” Battle and the Bengals made a good observation in their film study. Battle's coaches and teammates may be asking him why on earth he thought it was a good idea to broadcast that observation to the public before the game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jerry Jones expresses confidence in Christian Parker
summary: Dan Quinn left as the Cowboys' defense coordinator after the 2023 season to become the Commanders' head coach.
full_text: Dan Quinn left as the Cowboys' defense coordinator after the 2023 season to become the Commanders' head coach. Mike Zimmer and Matt Eberflus each lasted one season after Quinn's departure. The Cowboys ranked 31st in points and 28th in yards in 2024 under Zimmer and 32nd in points and 30th in yards in 2025 under Eberflus. They hired Christian Parker, the Eagles' passing game coordinator and secondary coach, as their defensive coordinator to fix what was broken. The Cowboys, though, entered Thursday night ranked 30th in total defense, including 31st against the run, and 28th in points allowed. The Cowboys allowed 419 yards, including 241 rushing yards, in a 24-16 loss to the previous winless Bucs who were starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones conceded it was a missed opportunity. "That's a question that I think we all, if you're a Cowboy fan, realize that patience really may not be the proper term here. . . . I like a lot about what we've got. We missed a chance here to improve, and we didn't improve." That prompted questions about Parker's job security. "Premature," Jones said. Jones said he still has confidence in Parker. "I do. Yes, I do," Jones said. "He's sitting there taking it on the shoulders, which goes with the territory, but I feel that he's competent, and the things that he's trying to do, I'm going to say it one more time: The thing that probably bothers me the most tonight is how they ran between the tackles so to speak and we're able to have that running game up in there, where we have a lot of strength. That's something that we've got to really look at and will." Cowboys defensive backs coach and passing game coordinator Derrick Ansley is the only assistant on staff who has previously served as a defensive coordinator. Ansley was the Chargers' defensive coordinator in 2023. Thus, the Cowboys likely will ride with Parker until at least the end of the season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Tony Romo was disqualified from a golf tournament, on the same day CBS announced his exit
summary: Last Friday was a very strange day for Tony Romo.
full_text: Last Friday was a very strange day for Tony Romo. It started with CBS and Romo announcing that he had parted ways with the network where he had served as the top NFL game analyst. It ended with Romo being disqualified from a golf tournament for submitting an erroneous scorecard. Via Chris Cwik of Yahoo Sports, the disqualification happened in the final round of a Korn Ferry pre-qualifier, as Romo was attempting to make the cut for the Korn Ferry tour. Romo put himself down for a four on the 16th hole and a four on the 17th hole. As it turned out, Romo had a five and a five. Romo took responsibility for the mistake, which may have resulted from the fact that Romo's trio had been placed on a clock due to slow play. Even with the incorrect score, it wouldn't have been enough to get Romo onto the Korn Ferry tour. Romo's broadcasting future is cloudy, to say the least. Until he makes his next move, he'll presumably be working to further hone his golf game.
author: Mike Florio

title: Thursday Night Football: Bucs upset Cowboys 24-16
summary: The Bucs ran for 241 yards, including 165 by Bucky Irving.
full_text: The Cowboys suffered one of their most humiliating defeats with Dak Prescott as their quarterback. They lost 24-16 at home to a previously winless team starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. Dallas is 2-3 and Tampa Bay 1-4. The Buccaneers, who trailed 10-7 at halftime, dominated the third quarter by outscoring the Cowboys 17-0 and outgaining them 197 to 59. The Cowboys got a break when Todd Bowles decided to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the Dallas 1 with 8:36 remaining. Sean Tucker was stopped for no gain by Jaishawn Barham, giving the Cowboys hope. Dallas went 99 yards in 10 plays, and George Pickens' 18-yard touchdown reception pulled the Cowboys within 24-16 after a missed 2-point conversion. The Cowboys drove to the Tampa Bay 24 with a chance to tie it, but a Prescott pass bounced off the hands of Jake Ferguson and Alex Anzalone intercepted the carom with 1:16 left. The Bucs gained 419 yards with 241 coming on the ground. Bucky Irving rushed for 165 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries and caught two passes for 10 yards and a touchdown. Jalon Daniels, making a second start in place of Baker Mayfield, was 19-of-25 for 189 yards and a touchdown. The Cowboys gained 366 yards with Prescott going 24-of-42 for 316 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Pickens caught nine passes for 130 yards and a touchdown. The Cowboys lost wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (quad) and left tackle Tyler Guyton (back) in the fourth quarter, but they will have a mini-bye week to get rested and healed before facing the Packers on Oct. 18.
author: Charean Williams

title: As trade rumors intensify, Marvin Harrison Jr. hires agents
summary: Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. says he's paying "no mind" to intensifying trade rumors.
full_text: Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. says he's paying " no mind " to intensifying trade rumors. He apparently has delegated that task to his new agents. Via ESPN, Harrison — who previously represented himself — has hired Todd France and Tory Dandy of Athletes First. The move happened on September 23, after Harrison had one catch for 33 yards in a Week 1 win over the Chargers and no catches on one target in a Week 2 loss to the Seahawks. Because Harrison has yet to complete his third regular season, there's no immediate contractual reason to have representation. He won't be eligible for a second deal until the current campaign ends. And so it's reasonable to think that Harrison made the move to have representation in place as he navigates the possibility of landing with a new team before the trade window closes on the Tuesday after Week 9. Under the new coaching staff in Arizona, Harrison has become largely forgotten in the Cardinals' offense. His agents can handle any and all conversations that would precede making the best decision about a new destination, in the hopes of unlocking Harrison's career. In his rookie year, Harrison had 62 catches for 885 yards and eight touchdowns. In 2025, he caught 41 passes for 608 yards and four touchdowns. So far in 2026, Harrison has five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown, on 13 total targets.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys close to within 24-16 on George Pickens' TD as CeeDee Lamb is questionable to return
summary: The Cowboys are without wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who is questionable to return with a quad injury.
full_text: ' The Cowboys are without wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who is questionable to return with a quad injury. They still have George Pickens, though. His 17-yard touchdown reception has drawn the Cowboys to within one score of the Bucs. Dallas went for 2 points and Dak Prescott's pass was incomplete, leaving the Cowboys trailing 24-16 with 5:26 left. The Cowboys got a break when Todd Bowles decided to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the Dallas 1 with 8:36 remaining. Sean Tucker was stopped for no gain by Jaishawn Barham, giving the Cowboys hope. They then drove 99 yards in 10 plays. The Bucs list left tackle Tristan Wirfs questionable to return with cramps.
author: Charean Williams

title: Colts-Commanders on Sunday morning had less than five million viewers
summary: The European games have created a new NFL viewing window on Sunday mornings.
full_text: The European games have created a new NFL viewing window on Sunday mornings. And while the numbers aren't shabby, they're nothing close to what NFL games do in the more traditional windows. Via Nielsen, the Week 4 Colts-Commanders game from London averaged 4.987 million viewers on NFL Network. In 2025, the six Sunday morning international games on NFLN averaged 6.2 million viewers . That next chance to improve the international performance comes on Sunday, when the Eagles face the Jaguars at 9:30 a.m. ET. In Week 6, it'll be Texans-Jaguars in London. The next week, the Steelers meet the Saints for the NFL's first-ever game in Paris. Two weeks later, it's Falcons-Bengals in Madrid. The European series ends in Week 10, with the Patriots and Lions in Germany. The NFL wants to expand the maximum number of international games from 10 to 16. That would mean even more Sunday morning games. And while the numbers aren't great in comparison to other standalone windows, it's bonus viewership in comparison to the usual cluster of Sunday afternoon games.
author: Mike Florio

title: Lions-Panthers slips under 20 million viewers on Sunday night
summary: The Lions don't seem to be the draw they've become in recent years.
full_text: The Lions don't seem to be the draw they've become in recent years. And the Panthers are still struggling to find national footing. Sunday night's game between Detroit and Carolina averaged 19.5 million viewers for NBC, per Nielsen. The first four NBC games of the 2026 season had exceeded 20 million viewers, with the Week 3 Rams-Broncos game attracting 20.8 million viewers. Sunday night's game was up against an MLB playoff game between the Atlanta Braves and L.A. Dodgers. The baseball game siphoned 3.33 million viewers away from football. Regardless, the number for Lions-Panthers suggests that the bloom is off the rose as to the resurgence of Detroit, which became much more of a national attraction in 2023. But Detroit has slipped back toward a middle-of-the-pack team in 2026, and the lack of an intense following seems to reflect that.
author: Mike Florio

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. says he is paying trade rumors "no mind"
summary: The NFL trade deadline is still a month away, but Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is one of the NFL players who could find a new home in the coming weeks.
full_text: The NFL trade deadline is still a month away, but Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is one of the NFL players who could find a new home in the coming weeks. He finally hired representation, recently signing with agents Todd France and Tory Dandy after previously representing himself. That has increased speculation that Harrison expects to be dealt. Harrison said Thursday isn't listening to the trade rumors. "Truthfully, I pay it no mind ," Harrison said, via ESPN. "I'm only focused on Detroit, helping the Cardinals win football games at the moment. So whatever rumors you're talking about, I don't pay it no mind." ESPN reports that the Cardinals are not shopping Harrison, but other teams are doing their due diligence. The Colts are among those teams. Harrison's father, Marvin Harrison Sr., became a Hall of Famer in Indianapolis. Harrison has five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown, with his 12 targets ranking fifth on the team. Coach Mike LaFleur again expressed confidence in Harrison, but Harrison has yet to live up to being the fourth overall pick in 2024.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bucky Irving gives Bucs 21-10 lead
summary: Bucky Irving has 122 rushing yards, and his second touchdown of the night has given the Buccaneers a 21-10 lead.
full_text: ' Bucky Irving has 122 rushing yards, and his second touchdown of the night has given the Buccaneers a 21-10 lead. The winless Bucs have dominated the second half with scoring drives of 86 and 75 yards on only five plays. Jalon Daniels hit a wide-open Tyler Johnson for 64 yards for the big play on the second drive of the half. Daniels is 13-of-17 for 155 yards and a touchdown. The Bucs have 315 yards to the Cowboys' 171.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bucs need only two plays to take the second-half lead
summary: The Bucs' first possession of Thursday night's game was a 15-play, 73-yard touchdown drive that ate 10:58 off the clock.
full_text: ' The Bucs' first possession of Thursday night's game was a 15-play, 73-yard touchdown drive that ate 10:58 off the clock. That was their only score of the first half. They opened the second with a two-play, 86-yard drive, needing only one minute to take a 14-10 lead over the Cowboys. Bucky Irving went 72 yards to the Dallas 14 before rookie safety Caleb Downs pushed the Bucs running back out of bounds. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka scored on a 14-yard run on the next play. Irving has 10 carries for 107 yards. Of the Bucs' 241 yards, 150 have come on the ground.
author: Charean Williams

title: Thursday Night Football: Cowboys lead Bucs 10-7 at halftime
summary: The Bucs have outgained the Cowboys 155 to 146 yards.
full_text: ' The Cowboys have had a long run with a game in Brazil on Sept. 27, followed by a trip to Houston for an early game Sunday and then tonight's game against the Buccaneers. The offense played 71 and 73 snaps against the Ravens and Texans, respectively. In the first half Thursday night, the Cowboys played like a jet-lagged team. They lead 10-7 despite an unimpressive half of football. The winless Buccaneers outgained the Cowboys 154-146. Dallas had the ball for only 10 minutes, 31 seconds and scored on only two of five possessions. Cowboys running back Javonte Williams scored on a 1-yard run following the opening kickoff, and Brandon Aubrey kicked a 41-yard field goal on the team's last series of the first half. Dak Prescott is 9-of-20 for 114 yards, while Williams has rushed for 32 yards on seven carries. CeeDee Lamb has only one catch for 4 yards and George Pickens three for 36. Jalon Daniels, starting a second consecutive game for the injured Baker Mayfield, threw a 5-yard touchdown to Bucky Irving. Daniels is 12-of-16 for 91 yards, with Chris Godwin catching three passes for 37 yards. Irving has nine carries for 35 yards. Chase McLaughlin kicked a 61-yard field goal in the second quarter, but officials waved it off, calling the Bucs for a delay of game. They punted.
author: Charean Williams

title: Brandon Staley pushes back against Troy Aikman's criticism: It's not true
summary: The ESPN analyst said Monday night: "Brandon Staley, he just simply doesn't have any answers, and I think he knew it when we talked to him coming in."
full_text: Saints defensive coordinator Brandon Staley pushed back at comments ESPN analyst Troy Aikman made during the Monday Night Football broadcast. With 2:43 remaining in the third quarter of the Saints' 45-24 loss, Aikman said Staley didn't have answers for the Falcons. Atlanta gained 420 yards, including 205 rushing yards, and the Falcons scored five rushing touchdowns. The Saints played without linebacker Kaden Elliss and edge rushers Carl Granderson and Andernee Jennings. "Brandon Staley, he just simply doesn't have any answers, and I think he knew it when we talked to him coming in," Aikman said Monday night. "I think he knew. He didn't tell us, but the guys that are out — their big edge rushers and guys who can play the run and set the edge — they're not on the field, and they just don't have that star defender that can erase mistakes for other people. "This was a matchup issue coming into this game, and it's proven true." Staley heard the comments and said he has "no idea" what Aikman was talking about. "It was a tough night for us, and certainly, I’m responsible . I'm calling the defense, but we've got a great group of guys," Staley said, via Katherine Terrell of ESPN. "No one defended that runner [Bijan Robinson] last year better than us. He's a hell of a player. But our group defended him twice last year better than anyone through his time in the NFL. "We're focusing on Minnesota, learning the tough lessons from the other night. We've got the right guys to bounce back." Staley admitted the comments bothered him "because they're not true." He also defended his players' effort after Aikman commented that some of the Saints were "standing around watching the play, missed tackles, just bad football" on the fifth rushing touchdown. "Our guys have played the right way," Staley said. "And mainly that's assignment, technique, effort, all in one. I think the other night, we were missing two out of the three. Our effort was there."
author: Charean Williams

title: Bucs score on first drive to tie Cowboys 7-7
summary: The Buccaneers' opening drive was as impressive as the Cowboys'.
full_text: ' The Buccaneers' opening drive was as impressive as the Cowboys'. Jalon Daniels led Tampa Bay on a 15-play, 73-yard drive that ate 10:58 off the clock. Bucky Irving caught a 5-yard touchdown pass from Daniels to tie the Bucs with the Cowboys 7-7. Daniels, the undrafted rookie who is making his second start in place of the injured Baker Mayfield, completed 8 of 8 passes for 49 yards and a touchdown. He also ran for 11 yards on two carries. The Cowboys had three defensive penalties on the drive, including a defensive holding penalty on DaRon Bland that negated a sack of Daniels by Shemar James on third down.
author: Charean Williams

title: Cowboys take 7-0 lead on opening drive
summary: The Cowboys have been virtually unstoppable in the red zone this season.
full_text: ' The Cowboys have been virtually unstoppable in the red zone this season. They kept it going on their first drive Thursday. Dallas, which entered the game with 13 touchdowns in 16 red-zone drives this year, scored on Javonte Williams' 1-yard run with 10:51 remaining in the first half. They drove 70 yards in nine plays after taking the opening kickoff. The Bucs had two red zone penalties, including a defensive pass interference penalty on Alex Anzalone in the end zone. Anzalone was covering Jake Ferguson. Dak Prescott went 3-of-5 for 37 yards on the drive, including two completions to George Pickens for 29 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers WR Mike Evans did not practice Thursday
summary: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans did not practice on Thursday after being a limited participant a day earlier.
full_text: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans did not practice on Thursday after being a limited participant a day earlier. He played through an injury to his ribs, catching five passes for 76 yards, and is expected to play Sunday against the Seahawks. Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee/calf), fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee), safety Marques Sigle (ankle) and defensive tackle James Thompson (ankle) also did not practice. Bosa has missed the past two games and is not expected to play this week. "I don't think he's far from playing, so hopefully, it’ll be sooner than later ," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said in his weekly radio show on KNBR, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "We would love to get him out there before our bye week, so hopefully, we can do that, but still too early to tell." Cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder) returned to practice in limited fashion after sitting out Wednesday's session. Defensive end Mykel Williams remained limited as he works his way back from the ACL tear that ended his 2025 season. He is expected to be activated from active/PUP before Sunday's game. "It's been his second week back, so he had a good week last week—even better this week," Shanahan said. "So, should be good to go for Sunday."
author: Charean Williams

title: Thursday Night Football: Cowboys LG Tyler Smith is active
summary: Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was a late scratch due to an illness.
full_text: ' Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was a late scratch due to an illness. They will, however, have left guard Tyler Smith, who will make his 2026 debut in Thursday Night Football. Smith underwent surgery on Sept. 8 to repair a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his left thumb and missed four games on injured reserve. The Cowboys' other inactives besides Porter are linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring), outside linebacker James Houston, offensive lineman Ajani Cornelius, offensive lineman Drew Shelton (hamstring) and wide receiver Camden Brown. The Bucs' inactives are quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb), safety Antoine Winfield (rib), cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad), linebacker SirVoce Dennis (ankle/foot), defensive lineman DeMonte Capehart, offensive guard Billy Schrauth and offensive guard Luke Haggard.
author: Charean Williams

title: Tyler Shough back to full participation, Alvin Kamara and Chris Olave limited
summary: Saints quarterback Tyler Shough downplayed his inclusion as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report and Thursday's update on his participation supported that lack of concern.
full_text: Saints quarterback Tyler Shough downplayed his inclusion as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report and Thursday's update on his participation supported that lack of concern. Shough, who hurt his left hand in Monday night's loss to the Falcons, is listed as a full participant. That should put him on track to play against the Vikings this weekend. Running back Alvin Kamara (back) and wide receiver Chris Olave (rest, knee) also took steps in the right direction. Both players were limited participants after being listed as non-participants on Wednesday. Linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf), defensive lineman Damon Godchaux (rest, groin), linebacker Anfernee Jennings (knee), and cornerback Jayden Price (personal) missed practice. Safety Julian Blackmon (shoulder), wide receiver Barion Brown (thigh), tight end Noah Fant (abdomen), linebacker Carl Granderson (ankle), and guard Jeremiah Wright (concussion) were limited participants. Linebacker Jaylan Ford (ankle), safety Mike Reid (ankle), and safety Lorenzo Styles (calf) were the team's full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Thursday Night Football: Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. ruled out with an illness
summary: The Cowboys acquired Porter in a trade with the Steelers last week, and he played 25 snaps in his 2026 debut on Sunday.
full_text: ' Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. played 25 snaps against the Texans on Sunday. He was expected to play a bigger role tonight, but instead, won't play at all. The Cowboys ruled out Porter with an illness. The team announced Porter's status 10 minutes before inactives were due. Porter has not allowed a touchdown in his last 1,685 coverage snaps, per Pro Football Focus. The Cowboys acquired him in a trade with the Steelers last week. He was inactive for the three games he was with Pittsburgh, unhappy that he didn't get a long-term contract extension before the start of the season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ashton Jeanty downgraded to limited practice on Thursday
summary: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty took a step in the wrong direction on Thursday's injury report.
full_text: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty took a step in the wrong direction on Thursday's injury report. Jeanty was listed as a limited participant due to ankle and foot issues. He was a full participant on Wednesday and the team will issue any injury designation for their Week 5 game against the Patriots on Friday. Tight end Brock Bowers (knee), defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (shoulder), and guard Jackson Powers-Johnson (groin) all moved the other direction by going from limited to full participation. Wide receiver Jalen Nailor (concussion) was the only Raider out of practice. Guard Spencer Burford (knee), wide receiver Cody White (ankle), and guard Trey Zuhn (knee) were limited while linebacker Segun Olubi (wrist), wide receiver Dont'e Thornton (hamstring), and wide receiver Dareke Young (shoulder) were full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: RB Chris Brooks out of practice, Packers sign Pierre Strong to 53-man roster
summary: The Packers were missing a running back at Thursday's practice and they signed another one to the active roster ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.
full_text: The Packers were missing a running back at Thursday's practice and they signed another one to the active roster ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears. title: As Skydance keeps growing, the CBS-NFL deal still hasn't been renegotiated
summary: Given the recent merger of Paramount and Warner Bros.
full_text: Given the recent merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, it's perhaps easier to list the major media outlets that Skydance doesn't own than the ones it does. Regardless, Skydance holds the CBS contract with the NFL, and that deal will likely expire after the 2029 season (absent an extension). Appearing Thursday on CNBC, Skydance Chair & CEO David Ellison said that his company anticipates " being in business with the NFL for the foreseeable future ," via Sports Business Journal . Ellison used the same phrase back in March. That's an inherently vague term, especially at a time when there's general concern that the clock on humanity is ticking toward Threat Level Midnight, thanks to Super Intelligence. Ellison also said Paramount has a "great relationship with the NFL," citing a “record-setting season” in 2025. The only record the NFL will want to set in 2030 (or sooner) is the amount of money received for the right to televise its games. Early this year, it seemed inevitable that, before the start of the 2026 season, CBS would agree to increase its current rate from $2.1 billion per year to $3 billion. That hasn't happened. Last week, Gerry Cardinale of RedBird Capital (which owns a large piece of SkyDance) said he expects CBS and the NFL to have a new deal " in a few years when the contract comes up ." “We have a tremendous respect for them,” Cardinale said, regarding the NFL. “They’re absolutely critical to our future and there will be a negotiation.” It was believed that negotiations were coming, if they hadn't already begun. Skydance's purchase of Paramount/CBS triggered a change-in-control clause that gave the NFL the right to redo the existing deal or pull the plug by August 2027. So why hasn't it happened? It could be as simple as this: Once the NFL met significant resistance from Fox (and perhaps others) regarding the prospect of paying more now for contract rights that are settled through 2029, CBS didn't want to be the only broadcast partner paying more. Either way, it's not as if the NFL will forget that it wanted more now and didn't get it. The next wave of contracts quite possibly will include as of 2030 and beyond every extra dollar that wasn't secured through new deals to cover 2026, 2027, 2028, and 2029.

title: Mike McDaniel: Calls for my firing come with the territory
summary: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said this week that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job is not in jeopardy, but the former Dolphins head coach knows that won't necessarily stop people from pleading with Harbaugh to change his mind.
full_text: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said this week that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job is not in jeopardy , but the former Dolphins head coach knows that won't necessarily stop people from pleading with Harbaugh to change his mind. The Chargers are 0-4 after entering the season with high expectations for what the tandem of McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert would be able to do on offense. They've fallen well short of those expectations while averaging 16.8 points per game and Herbert is only ahead of Jameis Winston in passer rating among qualified quarterbacks. On Thursday, McDaniel said that he understands calls for him to be fired come "with the territory of the job" but said his focus is only on how the team can get better results on the field. "When you have high expectations and you're getting the results we're getting and you're 0-4, that's pretty standard operating procedure," McDaniel said, via Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. "I would be foolish, or I would feel entitled, if I didn't expect there to be disappointment. And so, if you want things to change and you want narratives to change, you have to change them through action collectively. If our results are better, that's the only thing that matters. So it's pretty easy for me to focus on what I need to focus on." McDaniel said he thought Herbert played "the best, most competitive football that I've been around him for" late in last Sunday's loss to the Seahawks, but that success was mitigated by a pair of interceptions and five punts in the first half of the game that the Seahawks led by as many as 21 points. If the calls for major changes are going to end, it's going to take more than late, inconsequential flurries of good play.

title: Ernest Jones IV: Meeting of defensive players is needed "just once" per season
summary: The Seahawks' defensive players held a meeting this week, after a game on Sunday that included too many penalties.
full_text: The Seahawks' defensive players held a meeting this week , after a game on Sunday that included too many penalties. Linebacker Ernest Jones IV made it clear that they won't need to do it again this year. "Just once," Jones told reporters when asked how often such meetings occur per season. "You address that and you address other things in the same situation, so you don’t have to get to it later. Just once." He said that some of the players addressed the penalty issue, but that penalties weren't the only topic. "I had other things that I wanted to focus on," Jones said. "We got through to each other. We talked, we had man-to-man conversations in that room. We have an understanding of what we have to do and what we need to do." So why could it mean more to have that message coming from players and not coaches? "We’re the ones going out there doing it," Jones said. "Putting our bodies on the line so we don’t want to be doing it and costing the team. I don’t think it means more coming from one person, but having your brothers speak to you and come to you, it may do a little difference.” Despite the penalties, the Seahawks won the game. Still, absent a correction, it could cost them against a more capable opponent. This weekend, they'll be facing one in the 49ers.

title: Ranking all 32 NFL teams into tiers: 49ers among the elite, but some teams not as good as they seem
summary: Plus, the Rams still sit among the NFL's best despite slow start, and two squads sit at the very bottom of the barrel
full_text:
We're just about a quarter of the way through the NFL season, and we've learned quite a bit about every team in the league. There's plenty of time for teams to either continue as they've been or surprise us by reversing course. But we have enough information to start making educated guesses about who is good and who is not, and who is probably just average.
That's what we're here to do today. We're sorting all 32 NFL teams into the following tiers: The dregs of the league, the teams that are probably not that good, the teams that are probably average, the teams that are probably pretty good and the teams that look like inner-circle contenders. Let's take a look.
Note: Teams within each tier are listed in alphabetical order.
These two teams are really, really bad. They're not the only 0-4 teams, but they're clearly the ones with the least amount of hope.
These teams range from 0-4 to 1-3 to 2-2 to even 3-1, but the underlying performance and/or schedule they've faced indicates that they're probably not going to be legitimate contenders. Some of them may make the playoffs, but they're not likely to make much noise, if any.
Arizona scored an at-the-time surprising victory over the Chargers in Week 1, but it has since gone 0-3, including a loss to the Jameis Winston-led Giants last week. Cleveland is 3-1, but each victory has required a game-winning score in the final five minutes, and the Browns have only out-gained their opponents once. Green Bay's defense without Micah Parsons is eminently beatable, and its offensive line looks like a disaster. That's probably untenable unless Parsons drastically changes the Packers' defensive fortunes when he returns.
Houston is 0-4, and its defense does not look as good as expected. The passing offense has been good when Nico Collins has been active, but the Texans can't run the ball at all. The Colts have scored back-to-back victories, but their offense has looked nothing like it did last year as Daniel Jones works his way back from injury and the defense remains too friendly for them to be considered a good team just yet. The Chargers are the NFL's most disappointing team, and the less said about them, the better.
New Orleans can seemingly only move the ball in garbage time, and the Saints' defense has been unable to consistently generate stops. The Giants are 3-1, but their last two wins with Winston at the helm have gone against the Titans and Cardinals, so we're not exactly buying into them being all that good. The Jets looked much more competent offensively until this past week against the Bears , and they've given up 381 and 492 yards to their last two opponents.
Pittsburgh has really only looked good for one game so far. Tampa hasn't looked good or even acceptable at all this season, and is dealing with a backup quarterback situation for the next several weeks. The Bucs could already be out of the picture by the time Baker Mayfield gets back — even in the NFC South. And the Commanders' defense is once again just not good enough for them to be a real factor.
The Falcons have been surprisingly good defensively thanks to the league's most surprising pass rush, and the offense has looked really good the last two weeks since Michael Penix returned. The only remaining questions are how real that offensive improvement is and whether they can actually keep up that pass-rush productivity. Carolina looks pretty good behind a resurgent Bryce Young , but defensive injuries could undermine the Panthers until their top two cornerbacks return.
Denver's offense has looked miserable so far, except in the second half against the Jaguars , and now the Broncos will be without key players like Patrick Surtain II and Pat Bryant for a while. Still, there is upside with Sean Payton and then Vance Joseph's defense. The Lions have an explosive offense and a decrepit defense. It's hard to know what to do with them because they simply can't get consistent stops, but most teams can't stop them, either.
The Raiders' only loss is to the Chiefs , and by just three points... but their three wins are against the Dolphins, Chargers and Saints, so we don't necessarily know how good they are just yet. We're waiting to see a little bit more before moving them up. The Pats haven't exactly lit the world on fire just yet, but they did just beat the Bills and looked good doing it. The Eagles have looked just as annoying as ever in both their wins and their losses, and they're hemorrhaging offensive linemen and skill-position players. The roster still has a lot of talent on defense, though, so if they can get things into gear on that end, they still have a chance to take the NFC East.
The Ravens have looked incredible whenever Zay Flowers has been on the field. So long as Lamar Jackson 's injury isn't long-term and doesn't hamper him when he returns, we feel pretty comfortable declaring them a good team. The same goes for the Bears, who have been able to run the ball on everyone except the Vikings and should get Caleb Williams back fairly soon. Their defense has also been surprisingly effective so far, even though much of that has been about their third-down performance.
We need to monitor the injuries to Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor), but we know how good Cincinnati's offense can be when all the principals are healthy, and the defense has looked better than it did last year. The Dallas defense looks as bad as ever, but the Cowboys have scored at a rate that would rank the best in the NFL since 2000 (3.39 points per drive). When your offense is that good, you can overcome a bad defense — at least during the regular season. Minnesota is the inverse of Dallas. The defense is so good that it can overcome an offense that looks less than ordinary.
Buffalo hit a snag in its game last week against the Patriots, but it has otherwise looked pretty excellent. While we need to keep an eye on Jim Leonhard 's defense, the offense should bounce back compared to how it looked a week ago. Aside from the aforementioned second half against Denver, Jacksonville has looked like one of the league's elite teams. We're willing to consider that the exception to the rule and keep them in this group.
Kansas City might need to find some help at wide receiver after injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton , but Kenneth Walker III has taken the offense to another level, and the defense under Steve Spagnuolo always rounds into playoff form eventually. The Rams have alternated looking ordinary (or worse) with looking much more like the team we expected coming into the season, but so long as they can make it through the season healthy, they have as high a two-way upside as any team in the NFL.
San Francisco and Seattle have looked like the two best teams in the league so far. The Niners cannot be stopped offensively, and despite a blip against Washington, the Seahawks still have arguably the NFL's best defense when healthy (it's them or the Vikings). Both of those teams should be a major factor all year long.

title: Joey Porter Jr. ruled out of Cowboys' Thursday night showdown with Buccaneers
summary: Porter was unable to play in his second game with Dallas after being traded from Pittsburgh
full_text:
After a solid debut with the Cowboys , there was considerable anticipation regarding Joey Porter Jr.'s participation in Thursday night's game against the Buccaneers .
Cowboys fans, however, will have to wait another week to see Porter again. He was inactive for Thursday's game due to illness.
"It's disappointing (he's not playing tonight), but we'll have to overcome it," Cowboys owner/GM Jerry Jones said prior to kickoff . "We got our work cut out for us."
Porter reportedly arrived at AT&T Stadium hoping to play, but he was sent home after being labeled as "very sick." It was also reported that Porter has a bad virus and has been vomiting.
Joey Porter Jr. is set to make his Cowboys home debut pic.twitter.com/bUOEkMhux7
Porter, who was traded from the Steelers just over a week ago, started and logged 24 snaps during the Cowboys' Week 3 win over the Texans . He was targeted one time and did not allow a reception.
Last Sunday was Porter's first game of the season. He was inactive for each of Pittsburgh's first three games, citing a back injury. The Steelers traded Porter after he claimed he suffered a setback in his back following practice. Shortly after he touched down in Dallas, Porter acknowledged that his back felt better.
Porter held out this summer, hoping to get a contract extension. He is still playing under his rookie contract.
Without Porter, the Steelers' defense struggled during their Week 4 loss to the Browns . The Steelers are currently dealing with injuries to cornerbacks Jamel Dean (ankle) and Jalen Ramsey (wrist).

title: Bengals' Jordan Battle reveals subtle Malik Willis tell ahead of Week 5 matchup against Dolphins
summary: Cincinnati might have a leg up on Miami thanks to this scouting revelation
full_text:
When the Cincinnati Bengals hit the road in Week 5 for their matchup against the Miami Dolphins , their defensive players will be on the lookout for a quirk in Malik Willis ' passing mechanics. The Dolphins quarterback purportedly has a tell in his delivery that Cincinnati could use to time up its coverage.
Bengals safety Jordan Battle detailed Willis' habit and what it means for the defensive backfield.
"He has a slight little tap before every throw, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle said after the Bengals' Thursday practice . "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that gives the read to break."
Revealing the tell before the game comes with its risks. If Willis and the Dolphins were not already keen on this tendency, they certainly are now. They may have already discovered it through self-scouting, however. And if not, three days may not be long enough to permanently eliminate the habit from Willis' mechanics.
If the tell persists on Sunday and the Bengals' safeties come up with an interception, it may not be a coincidence.
The Bengals would gladly use any advantage they can find in pass defense, considering their struggles across the first four weeks of the season. They rank in the bottom half of the league in the following metrics.
On paper, Willis presents a more manageable test for the Cincinnati defense than the quarterbacks they faced thus far: Trevor Lawrence , Aaron Rodgers , C.J. Stroud and Baker Mayfield . Willis' 712 passing yards are the fewest of any quarterback who has played four games. He also has the fourth-lowest passer rating among qualifiers.
Still, as a mobile signal-caller, Willis offers challenges to a unit that has not found much success in containing the pass.
"He's obviously dangerous with his feet," Battle said. "We know we gotta be alert for that. Third-and-longs, they will run quarterback draws. In the passing game, he will extend plays, so we gotta be good downfield, DBs plastering. So we gotta be alert for that. He will take chances. We just gotta be alert on guys, where they're lined up."

title: The hidden impact of George Pickens: How Cowboys WR is helping unlock CeeDee Lamb
summary: Pickens may not be leading the box score, but his ability to draw coverage and create explosive plays has become a key ingredient in Dallas' offensive success
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys ' (2-2) offense is once again humming through the first quarter of the 2026 season.
Their Dak Prescott-led attack 30.5 points per game, and the most points per drive (3.39) in the league. Naturally, Prescott's numbers are elite: he ranks fifth in the league in EPA per dropback (0.24), fourth in completion percentage (70%), seventh in passing yards (1,065), tied for seventh in passing touchdowns (eight) and tied for seventh in passer rating (105.0).
CeeDee Lamb has been on the receiving end of much of that production, leading the league in catches (37), receiving yards (498) and receiving first downs (28). Those 498 yards receiving are the most through the first four games of a season in Cowboys history. But what about George Pickens?
Pickens has been a statistical casualty of Dallas' defensive struggles leading to the Cowboys having a league-low 36 drives this season. In 2026, playing alongside a healthy Lamb, Pickens has 225 yards receiving and no touchdowns on 18 catches through four weeks while averaging a career-low 12.5 yards per reception at the moment. However, Pickens is as valuable as ever if you ask the Cowboys.
"I think if you look at George last year, I don't know, you guys can look it up. I don't think he was putting up the insane numbers even till week four, five, six, whatever it was, because I think it's when CeeDee kind of went out, but George is learning the system as well. George easily could have had three catches for 180 yards in that game [on Sunday in the 34-30 win at the Houston Texans]," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "He really could have. He caught one with his eyes covered, and he opens people up all the time."
Pickens' role in the 2026 Cowboys offense, often, is that of the sacrificial lamb (pun intended) or field stretcher to open things up in the intermediate areas of the field. Pickens has run 45 go routes this season, the second-highest frequency in the league behind only DK Metcalf's 47 per TruMedia. Despite his high number of vertical routes deep down the field, Prescott maintains they're not making Pickens play decoy over and over again, even though that's what it may look like to the naked eye.
"He's pulling two guys with him almost all the time, and I don't know if he's clearing guys out," Prescott said. "Those are all real routes, and if you want to leave one guy on them, I'm going to throw it to him. So that's just making the defense show us what they want to do. When we're sending them deep, as I said, if it's going to be one-on-one, I'm going to throw it down there [to Pickens]. If not, you've got to take another guy with him. and that gives us numbers advantage."
Prescott was true to his word on Sunday when Pickens finished with 75 yards receiving on two catches. His first catch of the day came deep down the left middle portion of the field for a 53-yard gain with 10:43 in the third quarter. The big play moved Dallas' offense from their own 36 to the Texans ' 11. Nine plays later, Javonte Williams was in the end zone for one of his three rushing touchdowns that cut the Houston lead down to three, 23-20.
GEORGE PICKENS ‼️ 📺: #DALvsHOU on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/uA4UXgByqn
When Dallas acquired Pickens in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers , many viewed him as temperamental after he appeared exasperated about not getting the football as the Steelers rotated through a revolving door of passers. His attitude has been anything but temperamental in Dallas. Some of that has to do with the knowledge that the Cowboys are trying to get him the football. Schottenheimer admitted he had a double move called for Pickens in which he was the No. 1 option on a play, but Prescott was hit in the pocket and couldn't get the throw downfield to him at that moment. What did Pickens do? He laughed it off. Only receiving three targets to Lamb's 21 on Sunday also didn't bother him because that happened to be Dallas' path to victory.
"It'd be different if we weren't giving him the opportunities or trying to, and if defenses weren't just respecting him and taking him away," Prescott said. "So he's a guy that's smart, understands the game of football and he knows when the defenses are playing him that way, the opportunity it gives other guys. So he's a hell of a teammate, and I've said that. ... That [Pickens' attitude] shows a guy that's celebrating everybody else's success who obviously wants success, but as long as the team wins and he's doing his job, he's happy. We can't be more thankful for guys like that and with guys with an attitude like that."
So, when will it be Pickens' turn? It could come as soon as tonight under the primetime lights at AT&T Stadium when the Cowboys host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-4) on "Thursday Night Football."
"What I'm going to say about George is, if you blink, you're going [have] put up 150 [on you]," Schottenheimer said. "There's no doubt about that one, but the greatest thing about George Pickens was no one was happier in that locker room after the win than George Pickens, no one. It tells you how much of a magnetic personality he has, how much he loves playing football."
author: Garrett Podell

title: Cowboys vs. Buccaneers prediction: Can Tampa Bay slow down CeeDee Lamb and high-powered Dallas offense?
summary: Dallas brings a historically efficient scoring attack into Thursday night against an 0-4 Tampa Bay squad turning to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels
full_text:
In the Week 5 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Dallas Cowboys play host to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Dallas rebounded last week from its heartbreaking loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro the week before, storming back from a double-digit deficit to defeat the Houston Texans with a furious fourth-quarter rally. The Cowboys have arguably the NFL's best offense through the first four weeks of the season, and it could get a lift here with the potential return of guard Tyler Smith . But the Cowboys also have arguably the league's worst defense, and that unit is still dealing with various injuries even after trading for Joey Porter Jr .
Tampa is coming off a dispiriting loss to the Green Bay Packers in the first game of the Jalon Daniels era. The Buccaneers have turned to Daniels in the wake of Baker Mayfield's thumb injury, and the offense sputtered in his first game under center, totaling just 275 yards while Daniels was intercepted twice. The Bucs are now 0-4 after that loss and already in danger of falling out of the playoff picture entirely just a month into the NFL season.
Will Dallas get over .500 for the first time, or will Tampa capture its first win of the season? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Bucs went fairly run-heavy against the Packers in Daniels' first start, with the undrafted rookie throwing 27 passes while the team totaled 31 rush attempts despite trailing for most of the afternoon. Daniels went 19 of 27 for just 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also rushing eight times for 55 yards. Six of those runs were scrambles, and he totaled 46 yards on those plays.
The Cowboys have faced mobile quarterbacks three times this year and given up a ton of rushing yards to them. Jaxson Dart ran 11 times for 54 yards, Jayden Daniels ran for 69 yards on seven carries in just one half and Lamar Jackson ran six times for 50 yards.
Dallas does not have a strong pass rush to begin with (the Cowboys are 21st in pressure rate and 29th in sack rate), and the Cowboys have also allowed the highest scramble rate in the NFL while yielding 9.1 yards per scramble, according to Tru Media. Daniels, if he can maintain his composure when he does see pressure (and he was pressured on 42.9% of his dropbacks last week), should have opportunities to take off.
Tampa's offensive line has surprisingly not played all that well this year. The Buccaneers check in 22nd in ESPN's pass-block win rate and 23rd in run-block win rate. The team's running backs (mostly Bucky Irving ) have averaged just 1.07 yards before contact per attempt, indicating that the line isn't getting much push up front. And that's despite the fact that they've run into eight-man boxes at the second-lowest rate in football.
The Cowboys, of course, have gotten clocked on the ground, yielding 4.8 yards per carry to enemy backs. They check in 24th in yards before contact per attempt with 25th in yards after contact, per Tru Media. Irving should have room to run here if the Bucs can get their line in order.
The questions for Tampa's attack center on the passing game, where it's unclear whether Daniels can lead a competent attack. The Cowboys have gotten lit up through the air so far this season. Porter should help on that front, and he can probably follow Emeka Egbuka around the formation here and force Daniels to work the passing game through his other targets, but the Dallas secondary outside of him is eminently burnable right now.
Daniels didn't look like a player who could push the ball downfield with any degree of consistency against a subpar Green Bay defense, though, and there are still questions about whether he'll be able to do it even against this decrepit Cowboys unit.
So far this season, the Cowboys have an offense that is not just one of the best in the league but one of the best in recent memory. Consider this: Dallas has run the fewest drives of any team in the NFL (36), yet still ranks tied for second in points (122), just five behind the league leader (the Buffalo Bills at 127).
That's because the Cowboys have been historically efficient, averaging 3.39 points per drive. According to Tru Media, that makes them the sixth-most efficient offense through four weeks since the 2000 season. (The full-season record for points per drive during that span was just 3.19 by the 2007 Patriots .) When Dak Prescott called this unit the Greatest Offense There Is during the preseason, it's possible that he was not lying.
It's been Prescott himself doing the lion's share of the work, too, because the running game has yet to really get untracked. Javonte Williams has five rushing touchdowns, but he's averaged only 3.7 yards per carry and gained five-plus yards on his runs at the fifth-lowest rate among the 26 backs with at least 50 carries so far this season, per Tru Media. Rather than Williams getting consistent gains, it's just been Prescott methodically working the ball downfield with short and intermediate passes and then occasionally hitting defenses over the top with a shot to CeeDee Lamb or, more occasionally, George Pickens .
Tampa's defense has done an excellent job of stopping the run (opponents have averaged 3.2 yards per carry, the second-worst mark in the NFL), largely because that's what Todd Bowles tends to focus on. Those efforts have been successful, but the Bucs have been somewhat less successful against the pass, and they'll be shorthanded here thanks to the absence of Antoine Winfield Jr . They'll get Rueben Bain Jr . back to help the pass rush here; he hasn't been particularly effective so far, but Terence Steele has been friendly to opposing linemen who rush off the left side of the defensive line, so it's possible he could get going on Thursday night.
The Bucs probably don't have anybody who can deal with Lamb, mostly because it seems like nobody can actually guard Lamb when he's healthy. It's easy to forget what he did the last time he was full strength and had Prescott for a full season: he was a First Team All-Pro and totaled 135 catches for 1,749 yards and 12 touchdowns. He leads the league in both receptions (37) and yards (498) so far this year.
Pickens, by comparison, has yet to really make an impact, but that is probably coming soon enough given that defenses will presumably begin paying even more attention to Lamb. Pickens could have a significant size advantage against Tampa's corners on Thursday, and this could be the game where he gets loose.
Dallas' offense is too much for Tampa — or anyone else — to handle. Perhaps if the Buccaneers still had Mayfield under center, they could win a shootout, but even the version of Mayfield that was out there to start this season would have made that pretty unlikely. I suppose it's possible the Bucs could muscle and run their way to a win, but given how the offensive line has started the season, I don't see it happening in this one. Pick: Cowboys 34, Buccaneers 17
author: Jared Dubin

title: Cowboys should be afraid of this one nightmare stat heading into Week 5 Thursday night game with Buccaneers
summary: Everything appears to favor Dallas on Thursday night, but the Buccaneers fit the profile of a desperate winless team that has historically been primed for a breakthrough
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are a huge favorite going into Thursday night's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , which isn't all that surprising. After all, the Buccaneers have exactly zero wins and they have to hit the road on a short week to play in a city where they almost never win.
The Cowboys are 13-2 all-time at home against the Buccaneers, which is the second-best winning percentage for any team at home against one opponent (minimum 15 games played). In those 15 games, the Buccaneers averaged just 13.2 points per game, the second-worst mark since the 1970 merger for a road team in a single city.
And let's not forget that the Bucs are 1-9 in their past 10 primetime games dating back to the start of the 2023 season. Also, the Bucs will have an undrafted rookie at quarterback in Jalon Daniels , who will be making his first career start on the road.
The deck certainly seems to be stacked against Tampa Bay, but there is one stat that should have the Cowboys worried. Going into this season, there had been 10 teams in NFL history that:
Those 10 teams combined to go 9-1 in Week 5. The Buccaneers are now the 11th team to meet those qualifications. Yes, they're 0-4, but all four losses have come in close games that were decided by seven points or fewer.
Week 1: Bengals 33-27 over Buccaneers Week 2: Browns 23-19 over Buccaneers Week 3: Vikings 23-16 over Buccaneers Week 4: Packers 17-14 over Buccaneers
The Bucs have been close in each game. They just haven't been able to get over the hump to pick up their first win. Overall, they've been outscored by just 20 points in those four games combined.
Of the previous 10 teams to start 0-4 while being outscored by 21 points or less, six of them went on to win by at least a touchdown in Week 5.
1952 Steelers (Road): Pittsburgh 34-28 over Chicago Cardinals 1961 Steelers (Home): Pittsburgh 20-0 over Washington 1974 Lions (Home): Detroit 17-13 over San Francisco 1991 Buccaneers (Road): Detroit 31-3 over Tampa Bay 1998 Bears (Home): Chicago 31-27 over Detroit 2000 Patriots (Road): New England 28-19 over Denver 2005 Packers (Home): Green Bay 52-3 over New Orleans 2011 Vikings (Home) : Minnesota 34-10 over Arizona 2012 Saints (Home): New Orleans 31-24 over San Diego Chargers 2017 Chargers (Road): Los Angeles 27-22 over Giants
Not only are the 10 teams 9-1, but they're also 3-1 on the road, where the Bucs will be on Thursday night.
So why is this happening? It's hard to say for sure, but when you're losing close games, that gives you confidence that you can play with anyone and if you combine that with the desperation that comes with being 0-4, it sets the stage for an upset.
Of course, as you can see, the only 0-4 team in this situation that didn't win was the 1991 Buccaneers, so Tampa Bay knows first-hand that a win on Thursday night isn't a lock. As a matter of fact, it would be a total surprise if the Bucs won, but if they do pull off the upset, don't say we didn't warn you.
