title: It wouldn't shock me IF ... NFL Week 5: Nick Sirianni's seat heats up, Sean Payton takes back playcalling
summary: Could the 49ers plant their flag as the Super Bowl favorites? Will Jacoby Brissett be the latest QB to light up the Lions?
full_text:
When you step outside in the morning, you'll notice that chill in the air. It's a reminder that the fall months have arrived, and that typically means the action across the NFL is ramping up. Now that the first month is in the rearview mirror, teams are rounding into form, and we should start to see some significant separation between the contenders and pretenders over these next few weeks.
This is also the time when we begin to see if some early-season struggles or even hot starts are legit or mere flashes in the pan. For the former, that could create some awkward situations, particularly as we continue to gauge the temperature of the head coach's hot seat or coordinator duties.
Both of those could be at the forefront of the headlines by the time we wrap up Week 5 in the NFL, which we discuss in depth below, along with other storylines that could sprout out of the upcoming slate.
The Philadelphia Eagles might be on the verge of blowing it up. The club is off to a teetering 2-2 start to the regular season, has been dealt with an onslaught of injuries, and saw Lane Johnson retire this week. That said, the biggest indicator that something may be afoot is that they just shipped away starting interior lineman Cam Jurgens to the Ravens . For a team still trying to be in the Super Bowl conversation, it's a bit striking to see them trade someone of Jurgens' caliber, even if there are solid reasons for Howie Roseman to make such a move .
And that brings us to this weekend, when Philadelphia will be in London taking on the Jacksonville Jaguars . In my eyes, this has the makings of a Jags blowout win . Jacksonville is essentially the polar opposite of the Eagles right now offensively. They have the third-best third-down conversion rate (51.1%) in the NFL entering Week 5, the second-best red zone touchdown rate (81.8%), and Trevor Lawrence has the second-highest passer rating in the NFL (min. 100 pass attempts). If they keep that up, the Eagles offense, which hasn't converted a third down in its last 17 attempts, could be lapped.
Philadelphia would fall under .500, and Nick Sirianni would be 5-8 since Week 12 of last season (including playoffs). The head coach's seat would be as hot as it's arguably ever been, and this Eagles ownership hasn't been shy about making bold decisions if they believe it's in the best interest of the team.
The Chargers are in dire straits right now, as they enter Week 5 at 0-4 and have been lifeless on the offensive side of the ball. Justin Herbert has thrown more interceptions (6) than touchdowns (4) and has been the second-most pressured quarterback (46.5%) in the NFL. Herbert's 12 sacks taken are also tied for the second-most in the league.
With injuries to the offensive line, this sets the stage for him to be under siege more than he's been all year. L.A. already knows it'll be without starting left tackle Rashawn Slater , who will miss time due to a high ankle sprain. On top of Slater, starting right tackle Joe Alt is also not expected to play on Sunday due to a neck injury. Alt was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's opening injury report. Even with those two, the Chargers' offensive line was surrendering loads of pressure onto Herbert, and that's only going to get worse with them out of the picture and the Chargers squaring off against the Broncos .
Denver's pass rush isn't as prolific as it was last season, but it is still 11th in the NFL in pressure rate (38.9%). Over the last two seasons combined, it has piled up the most sacks (76) in the NFL.
Through four weeks, the most Herbert had been sacked in a game was four, which came last week against Seattle. At SoFi Stadium on Sunday, the Chargers QB will endure a new season high in sacks with the Broncos tagging him at least five times, just as they did the last time they faced him in Week 3 of last season.
The Lions defense is unquestionably the worst in the NFL right now. Their secondary is coming off a Week 4 showing where they were demolished by Bryce Young , who threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns. Detroit is giving up the second-most points per game in the NFL (31.8) and the most total yards (423.8) per game this season. The Lions' 1,216 total passing yards allowed are also the most in the league, while their 110.4 passer rating allowed is the fourth-highest. No matter which way you slice it, it's putrid.
That should be music to Jacoby Brissett's ears as he's eager to rebound from a three-interception performance against the Giants last week. Judging by the opponent he's facing, he's primed to throw it all over the yard.
So far this season, Brissett's high in passing yards is 280, which came back in Week 3 against the San Francisco 49ers . However, if you go back to last season when he became the starter in Arizona, he's had several eye-popping yardage totals. Brissett went over 300 yards four times and even had a 452-yard passing game thrown in there as well. I believe we get an aerial avalanche from Brissett, which gets him to 350 passing yards on Sunday.
Arizona has the weapons for Brissett to pile up yardage, particularly Trey McBride and Michael Wilson . McBride could go berserk as the Lions are giving up the most receptions and receiving touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season, and the second-most receiving yards. Meanwhile, Michael Wilson could follow in Tetairoa McMillan's shoes, who torched the Lions last Sunday to the tune of 14 catches, 192 yards and two touchdowns.
Because the Cardinals are the fourth-worst scoring defense (29.3 points per game allowed) in the NFL this season, Brissett could be forced even more into a pass-heavy game script.
Gambling nugget to note : Jacoby Brissett's O/U passing yard prop is set at 269.5 yards (-111 to the Over). Brissett is +115 to reach 280 passing yards, +145 to reach 290 passing yards, +183 to reach 300 passing yards, and +567 to reach 350 passing yards (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
The leash is getting shorter and shorter for Broncos offensive coordinator David Webb and his ability to call the plays in Denver. The Broncos are 2-2 on the season, which finds them in third place in the AFC West. Part of the reason for their .500 mark through the first month has been their sluggish starts on offense. Denver is scoring the fewest first-half points (13 total points) in the NFL this season and has only stayed afloat because their 61 total second-half points scored are the fifth-highest in the league.
So far this season, the Broncos (with Webb calling the plays) are averaging 18.5 points per game, which ranks 26th in the NFL. Last year, when Joe Lombardi was the OC and Sean Payton was calling the plays, Denver averaged 23.6 points per game, which ranked 14th.
Meanwhile, Bo Nix appears to be regressing under this new leadership. Over the first two years of his career, Nix's air yards per pass attempt were 7.3. This year, it's down to 5.4. The former first-round quarterback's yards per attempt this season (6.1), completion percentage (60%), and passer rating (80.4) are all on pace for career lows. His turnover-worthy throw rate of 3.7% is also on pace for a career-high.
Even if Denver wins on Sunday to improve to 3-2, it's on the table that Sean Payton takes back the play sheet from Webb if the offense continues to sputter, particularly entering a short week where they'll host the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football. Moreover, if the Broncos are upset by the Chargers and the offense is a key reason for the defeat, it'll be curtains for Webb's days as the play caller.
Despite a shaky 2-2 start to the season, the betting favorite to win Super Bowl LXI remains the Los Angeles Rams . While it's certainly a long season and there's plenty of time to go before we kick off that championship matchup at SoFi Stadium, I'm surprised L.A. has held onto being the favorite this long. With that in mind, I think we see the odds flip this weekend with a new NFC West team claiming the top spot. The San Francisco 49ers —…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Broncos experiment ends in failure: Sean Payton to reclaim play-calling duties after just four weeks
summary: The Broncos are making a significant adjustment as Payton looks to jump-start a struggling attack
full_text:
Davis Webb went into the 2026 season as the play-caller for the Denver Broncos , but after just four weeks, he has officially been replaced. Sean Payton has decided to reclaim his role as the team's play-caller.
The Broncos' head coach shared the news during his press conference on Thursday .
"We'll make a change offensively," Payton said. "I'll call the plays."
It's not a total surprise that Payton has decided to go this route. The Broncos' offense has struggled at times this season, especially early in the game.
The offense has gotten off to a slow start in all four games Denver has played. The Broncos only scored a total of 13 first-half points through four weeks, which is the fewest in the NFL. Even the hapless Dolphins (0-4) have had more first-half points (19) than the Broncos this year. The Broncos and Dolphins are the only two teams in the league that have scored under 20 total first-half points this season (To put Denver's struggles in perspective, the Broncos had scored 58 first-half points at this point last season).
The Broncos also struggled to get their run game going. Through four weeks, they averaged just 81.3 yards per game, which ranks 29th in the league. The Broncos rank in the bottom 10 of the NFL in multiple categories, including points per game (27th overall), yards per game (27th overall), and yards per play (24th overall).
Earlier this week, Payton was asked if four games was a big enough sample size to assess Webb and his future as the team's play-caller. Payton didn't blame Webb for the team's struggles, but he didn't exactly give him a vote of confidence.
"I think our focus needs to be more on the specific and the detail of each play regardless [of who's calling the plays],'' Payton said Wednesday, via ESPN . "I think Davis is very fast, very quick and understands what we're doing. I think that the most important job I have is really evaluating the whys. I think collectively, we all, after a game, and after a four-game sample size, certainly, this isn't championship football, what we see. How quickly can we correct those things?''
The bottom line is that the offense has struggled through the first four weeks, and now, Payton will try to fix things starting with this week's game against the 0-4 Chargers.
Payton is in his 20th season as an NFL head coach, and for most of that span he has served as his team's offensive play-caller, but that changed this year. Back in February, Payton decided that he wanted to hand over the play-calling reins to Webb . At the time, the Broncos underwent some changes on their coaching staff. Denver fired last year's offensive coordinator, Joe Lombardi, in January , and Webb was promoted from quarterbacks coach.
In the months leading up to the promotion, Payton considered giving the play-calling duties to Webb and he ended up making that official during the offseason.
"It was something I kind of knew during the year. He and I visited on a handful of occasions. He's extremely talented. With regards to play-calling, I think he'll be really good at it," Payton said back in February.
Webb's first job as an NFL assistant coach came in 2023. When Payton was hired as the Broncos' coach, he brought on Webb as his QB coach, and the two had worked together for three seasons before Payton decided to give up play-calling duties so Webb could take over.
If the Broncos are going to turn things around on offense, this would be the week to do it. Denver is getting set to face a winless Chargers team that has surrendered an average of 26.5 points per game this season, which is the ninth most in the NFL. Although the Chargers have struggled this year, they'll likely enter this game with some confidence, as Jim Harbaugh has a 3-1 record against the Broncos since being hired as head coach in 2024.
This is a game that would sting for weeks if they lost it, so Payton likely wants to do everything in his power to make sure the Broncos' win.
Not only does Payton have to worry about facing the Chargers, but the Broncos have to turn around and face the Seahawks on Thursday night in Week 6. Seattle has one of the best defenses in the NFL and Payton will probably feel a lot more comfortable going into the game knowing that he'll be calling the plays while matching wits with Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald.
Going back to Payton certainly makes some sense. He has a long history as a successful play-caller and the Broncos will probably be better off with him calling the shots.
Denver didn't want to lose Webb to another team during the offseason, so it made sense to give him a shot. Although four games might not be a fair shot, this is the NFL, and, unfortunately for Webb, not everything is fair.
The only potential problem with making the change now is that if Payton can't fix the offense, then the Broncos could be in trouble, so it will certainly be interesting to see how this plays out over the next few weeks.
Although Webb won't be calling plays, Payton did have some high praise for his offensive coordinator on Thursday.
"I've done this long enough where I know when I have a future head coach and he's going to be one," Payton said.
If Webb does become a head coach, he'll get to decide who calls plays, but for now, that decision belongs to Payton and he's decided that he gives the Broncos the best chance to win.

title: Is Justin Herbert 'elite'? He is NOT even one of the 10 best quarterbacks in the NFL
summary: Upon further review, Herbert's top-10 QB credentials should be revoked
full_text:
Jim Harbaugh, who effusively praises Justin Herbert , said Herbert needs to " be better " last week. Perhaps the tough love was an attempt to spark a 0-3 team and a quarterback he recently predicted would be remembered as the greatest quarterback in NFL history. Or, maybe he really meant it.
Either way, it hasn't helped yet as the Chargers fell to 0-4 after a loss on Sunday in Seattle.
I realize the "elite" QB conversation is tired. Rightfully so — I'm not even really sure what qualifies as "elite". I just recall it used to be an exhausting conversation with the likes of Joe Flacco back in his Ravens days, and it's been passed on to quarterbacks like Jalen Hurts , Dak Prescott , and now maybe Justin Herbert.
Let's shift the focus to something concrete. Is Justin Herbert a top 10 quarterback in the NFL going forward? This is not based on his current performance, which has obviously been poor during this 0-4 start. This is based on his entire body of work and where we think he's headed.
It's past time we take a hard look at his credentials. Going into the year, he was a consensus top-10 quarterback in the NFL, whether you asked CBS Sports' NFL experts or polled NFL coaches, executives, and scouts .
Four games can't change that much, right? Well, we are constantly getting evaluated in "corporate America," so we don't really need an excuse to re-examine Herbert. In fact, this recent stretch motivated me to peel back more layers and dig deeper.
He may be one of the most talented QBs in the NFL who has put up video game numbers in the past, BUT he's never won a playoff game, his team is 0-4 this year and his resume is frankly average over the past five seasons. His resume is closer to Trevor Lawrence than a Matthew Stafford , Dak Prescott or Joe Burrow .
The crux of my case here is built on the metric EPA per dropback. It's the best advanced measure to value all of a quarterback's production. It looks at how he impacts his team's scoring chances on every play by moving the chains, avoiding negative plays and making big plays, all while considering the game situation, unlike passer rating.
Herbert deservedly drew a ton of praise early in his career, as he is immensely talented and had the most passing yards through three seasons in NFL history. However, look at his production year by year.
He peaked in his first two seasons, and he's been outside the top 10 in this efficiency rating ever since.
He's one of two qualified quarterbacks to rank outside the top 10 in each of the past five seasons, along with Geno Smith . Smith has been up and down in the last few years across his tenure with the Seahawks , Raiders , and now the Jets .
Let's drill this down a little further. He's one of two quarterbacks in the past 20 seasons with five straight seasons outside the top 10 in this metric after multiple seasons inside the top 10. The other is Jay Cutler. Not saying he is Cutler, although both were (are) uber-talented signal callers whose production tailed off.
I don't see how Herbert could be a top-10 quarterback anymore when he hasn't played like one for five seasons, never won a playoff game and the Chargers are off to a disastrous start this year.
His career is very similar to Trevor Lawrence, another all-world talent with an up-and-down career. The only difference is that Lawrence was not a consensus top-10 quarterback entering the year.
Their traditional numbers are nearly identical over the last five years, which aligns with Herbert's slight decline and Lawrence's career, excluding his rookie year with Urban Meyer, which was an outlier.
The advanced metrics paint a similar picture, too.
If there's a tiebreaker here, let's not forget Herbert's Chargers blew a 27-point playoff lead to Lawrence's Jaguars . Perhaps Lawrence is the top 10 quarterback instead of Herbert.
Finally, eyeball this list. This could be the fifth straight season Herbert is not top 10 in EPA per dropback and fails to win a playoff game.
If you look at the names (and their corresponding seasons on the list), how many do you think were still considered a top-10 QB during (or after) those runs? Maybe Eli Manning, based on his two Super Bowl MVPs, but in reality, he was not a top-10 QB, especially late in his career. Carson Palmer was not one across his Raiders and early Cardinals years. Russell Wilson was not across his final years with Seattle and tenure with the Broncos , Steelers and Giants .
Of course, this case can't be settled by numbers alone. The first thing the Justin Herbert supporter would say is "check the tape!" Yes, I get it, he has a lot of quality traits, including a rocket arm and some wheels.
You could also say, he's like Matthew Stafford in Detroit. Both had no playoff wins through 100 starts. Both had a GOAT in their division ( Aaron Rodgers vs. Patrick Mahomes ), and both had video game numbers early in their careers, such as a 5,000-yard season.
There's certainly been question marks about Herbert's supporting cast, like there were with Stafford, who had no run game and no defense on the Lions . Nobody could win with that. Well, Herbert has never had a 1,000-yard rusher in his career. He's had zero RB, WR or TE with an All-Pro selection during his tenure. He's the most sacked quarterback in the NFL since he was drafted in 2020 (237 times), and he had no protection last year when Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater were hurt.
The traditional numbers are very similar when comparing Stafford and Herbert's first 100 starts (Herbert makes his 100th on Sunday). Stafford was even throwing to Calvin Johnson.
So maybe it's just a matter of the right pieces around Herbert (with the Chargers or elsewhere) so he can do what Stafford has done with the Rams . This is a very reasonable argument and one that could come to pass over time.
I laid out what I felt was the important evidence. Now you can decide for yourself if Herbert still deserves top-10 quarterback status.
Until I see him turn into post-Lions Stafford 2.0, I'm trusting the evidence showing he has not only been outside the top 10 for a long time but has also wilted in the playoffs. If one were false, I could be convinced he's still a top-10 guy, but both are true.
Right now, I'm comfortable ranking all these quarterbacks ahead of Herbert — Josh Allen , Patrick Mahomes, Matthew Stafford, Lamar Jackson , Joe Burrow, Brock Purdy , Dak Prescott, Jared Goff , Jalen Hurts, Jordan Love and Drake Maye .

title: Cowboys get boost as Tyler Smith returns from injury for Week 5 showdown
summary: The Cowboys survived without Smith, but his return gives Dallas a boost against Tampa
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Three-time Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith is back with the Dallas Cowboys, just in time for "Thursday Night Football" against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Smith practiced as a limited participant in Monday's walkthrough and in Tuesday's practice before being a full participant in Wednesday's walkthrough. Smith has been activated and will play in Week 5 against Tampa, a team source confirmed.
"You just get a guy like that back, an enforcer, one of the best guards, if not the best guard in the league. It definitely helps," Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott said after practice on Tuesday.
Smith had yet to suit up this season after undergoing thumb surgery days before their season opener and some time on injured reserve.
"It was extremely difficult," Smith said after practice on Monday. "It was one of the hardest things I've gone through. ... "I couldn't grab, I couldn't punch. … I just couldn't do my job as an o-lineman. We hand fight. We see somebody every play. It's not like I'm in space or I'm dropping back or I'm tackling somebody. I have to block, and I have to manhandle somebody every play. So that was my biggest issue. If I could do all those things with no issues, then we don't have a problem."
The Cowboys gave Smith the ultimate decision on whether he wanted to wait another week after his practice window opened, but he gave the team the green light to line him up on Thursday night.
"If Tyler feels good that he can go play, then I have no problem," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "I've seen him, like I said, play football at a very high level. It's more of a comfort level for him than me. All Tyler's got to do is say, 'Hey Schotty, I feel good' and he'll be out there.'"
So what will materially change for a Cowboys offense that is already averaging the most points per drive (3.39) in the NFL, a figure that actually ranks as the fourth-most by any team through their first four games of a season in the 21st century, per CBS Sports Research?
The versatility in Dallas' run game, which ranks as the eighth-worst in the league, with an average of 89.5 rushing yards per game. Teams that face the Cowboys know they don't feel incredibly confident running the football to the left with undrafted veteran T.J. Bass at left guard. The Cowboys have run to the right side of the line at the ninth-highest rate in the NFL this season (35.9%) and to the left side of the line at the fourth-lowest rate (26.9%) without Smith this season. They're around league average in run-up-the-middle rate, at 20th (44.7%). Now that Smith is back, his return unlocks the ability to run the football to any and all locations along the line of scrimmage.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Would a Marvin Harrison Jr. trade unlock his potential? History offers hope, and a warning
summary: Harrison has just five catches through four games. Here's what his trade value could look like, what history says about a fresh start and three teams that could make a move
full_text:
When the Cardinals drafted Marvin Harrison Jr . fourth overall in 2024, he was all but anointed a future Hall of Famer. And after what he did at Ohio State, it didn't take much imagination to envision what his NFL career might look like. Thirty-three games later, we're having a very different conversation: Would Harrison be better off playing somewhere other than Arizona?
But trading for Harrison requires believing two things: that the Cardinals haven't gotten the most out of him, and that another team can do better. The first argument is getting easier to make. The second is where things get complicated, especially when you look at what's happened to other highly drafted receivers who fell short of expectations early in their careers.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching, that's worth examining.
In my recent story on Carnell Tate , the fourth pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , we looked at what teams should expect from receivers drafted in the top 10. The average rookie season over the last decade was 901 receiving yards. Harrison finished with 885 in 2024, a respectable start, even if it fell short of expectations.
But things haven't gotten better. Harrison managed 608 yards in 12 games last season, and through four games in 2026, he has five catches for 85 yards. For perspective, Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price , who played three games before landing on IR, has four receptions. This is the same Price who was targeted just 14 times over his final two seasons at Notre Dame. Harrison was targeted at least 13 times in four different games during his final season at Ohio State.
Through 33 NFL games , Harrison has 1,578 receiving yards. Amari Cooper , also drafted fourth overall, had 2,285 yards at the same point. Corey Davis , the fifth pick in 2017, had 1,503. Harrison's production looks much closer to Davis's than Cooper's.
Harrison vs. first-round receivers early in their careers
Yards after catch/reception
There are encouraging numbers here. Harrison's 13 touchdowns are more than Cooper (12) or CeeDee Lamb (11) had through their first 33 games. He's also ninth in explosive receptions per target. But he's near the bottom in catch rate and yards after the catch. The big plays are there; the consistent production isn't.
Perhaps the biggest concern isn't simply that Harrison has struggled. It's that he's becoming less involved in Arizona's offense, even while playing more.
Among 41 first-round receivers in their first four appearances of Year 3, Harrison ranks 39th in receiving yards and is tied for the fewest receptions.
Harrison's disappearing opportunities
Typical Year 3 1st-round WR
That last row tells the story. Harrison was targeted on roughly one of every five routes through his first 29 games. This season, it's fewer than one in 10. And that raises a fair question: Is Harrison struggling because he isn't getting opportunities, or is he not getting opportunities because he's struggling?
There's evidence for both. Harrison ran 17 go routes in the first two games , tied for sixth most in the league, and Jacoby Brissett took some responsibility after Harrison went without a catch. But we can't blame everything on the quarterback or scheme when Trey McBride and Michael Wilson have combined for 58 receptions through four games. Harrison has five.
Despite the social-media noise, I'd be careful about giving up on Harrison. Plenty of first-round receivers have needed time to develop, but there's a difference between becoming productive and becoming the player a team thought it was drafting.
Corey Davis, Mike Williams and DeVante Parker all improved after modest beginnings. Each had at least one season that justified some of that early optimism. The problem? None consistently produced like the elite receiver his draft position suggested. And Davis was drafted the highest of the three, at No. 5 overall, one spot after Harrison.
Then there's Lamb, who went from a good young player to one of the NFL's best. But he was already averaging more than 62 yards per game through 33 appearances, considerably better than Harrison's 47.8.
How other first-round WRs developed
Williams and Parker eventually had 1,000-yard seasons, and Davis nearly got there with 984 in 2020. Harrison is young enough to make a similar leap. But Cooper and Lamb were already much more productive at this stage. That's an important distinction.
So what happens when a first-round receiver gets a fresh start somewhere else?
Amari Cooper is the obvious success story. In 2018, Oakland traded him to Dallas, where his production jumped from 46.7 to 80.6 yards per game. He followed that with consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. Brandin Cooks also flourished after New England acquired him from New Orleans in 2017, producing 1,082 yards before adding 1,204 with the Rams the following year.
But here's the difference: Both Cooper and Cooks had already posted two 1,000-yard seasons before being traded. Their new teams weren't betting on production they'd never seen. They were building on what those receivers had already done.
The other historical comparisons aren't nearly as encouraging.
I looked at first-round receivers traded in Year 3 or Year 4, the same stage of Harrison's career. Some joined better offenses or played with better quarterbacks. Most never became the players their new teams hoped they would.
First-round WR trades in Years 3-4: Price and production
3rd + two 7ths; 5th sent with Dotson
1st + 3rd; 4th sent with Cooks
E.J. Gaines + 2nd; 6th sent with Watkins
Cooper is the clearest example of a receiver taking his game to another level. Cooks maintained his production, while Sammy Watkins remained useful without ever returning to his 1,000-yard form.
But Dorsett, Coleman, Reagor, Dotson and Harry? None became the player their original teams envisioned. Injuries played a role in some cases, but changing teams didn't solve the larger problem. And that's something any team considering Harrison should remember.
Of course, there's another reason Harrison could be appealing: his contract. An acquiring team would inherit his remaining 2026 salary and 2027 compensation, with the possibility to exercise his fifth-year option for 2028.
But what should it cost to acquire him?
The historical returns vary considerably. Dallas sent a first-rounder for Cooper. New England gave up a first and third for Cooks, getting a fourth back. Arizona surrendered a first for Hollywood Brown, with a third coming back. All three receivers had already proved themselves.
Meanwhile, Dotson cost a third and two sevenths, with a fifth going the other way. Harry and Coleman each brought back seventh-round picks.
Harrison falls somewhere in between. He won't fetch a first-rounder, and a third feels closer to his worth given his production and untapped potential. But remember, Pittsburgh got a 2028 second-round pick for Joey Porter Jr . when plenty of people thought a third was the best-case scenario.
Put another way: You never know. If one team believes it can unlock Harrison, a second-rounder might feel like a bargain. But at that price, the buyer better have a plan for how to use him.
Arizona doesn't have to trade him, either. The Cardinals could spend the rest of 2026 seeing whether Mike LaFleur can figure this out. If they do make Harrison available, though, here are three teams I think would be intriguing landing spots.
Yes, the Pats traded for A.J. Brown , and he's the unquestioned No. 1 when he returns. But we've seen this group struggle without him. Receivers can't get open, Drake Maye has looked frazzled, and while Romeo Doubs looked better against Buffalo, he's better suited as a No. 3. Harrison could slide in as the No. 2, getting plenty of looks with defenses focused on Brown, without the same pressure he's faced in Arizona.
Always bet on Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes . That's where the conversation starts. Injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton (who could be done for the season) have also raised…

title: Revamped defense plus Kenneth Walker III: How the Chiefs re-established themselves as a Super Bowl contender
summary: Kenneth Walker III's league-leading ground game and Steve Spagnuolo's revamped, pressure-heavy defense are taking the burden off Patrick Mahomes
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs had won the AFC West nine consecutive years before missing the playoffs last season. For the majority of the decade, they were a free space on the NFL's postseason Bingo card. But in 2025, for the first time in Patrick Mahomes ' career, the media stopped giving the franchise the benefit of the doubt regarding being one of the last teams standing.
After four weeks of this year's regular season, Kansas City looks like the formidable Kansas City teams of old. While legacy names such as tight end Travis Kelce and defensive tackle Chris Jones are still around, several newcomers, including a strong rookie defensive class, have inspired newfound confidence — and taken the burden off Mahomes to get the Chiefs back to Super Bowl contention.
Prized free agent running back acquisition Kenneth Walker III leads the NFL in rushing (537) yards as the league trends more run heavy , but it was a defensive overhaul that has been the biggest change for the Chiefs. Roughly 35% of defensive snaps this season have been played by those who were not on the roster a year ago.
In terms of defensive EPA per play, through four weeks, the Chiefs have their best mark (0.04) since winning the Super Bowl in 2024. The pass rush is a big reason for that improvement.
Kansas City is on pace for 259 pressures, according to TruMedia, which would be the team's highest total in a decade. Last season, it generated a higher team pressure rate (39.2%), but that effort required more blitzes. Steve Spagnuolo's defense is impacting the opposing quarterback without sending five-plus rushers as often, which takes some pressure off an entirely revamped secondary. The problem thus far has been finishing plays. Despite the uptick in pressure, Kansas City has just four sacks on the year, tied for the second-lowest in the NFL.
The reason for elevated success up front has been improved play from stalwarts Felix Anudike-Uzomah and George Karlaftis , as well as working rookies R Mason Thomas and Peter Woods — both of whom were taken top-40 overall — into the rotation. The former is third on the team with 10 pressures.
Upon trading Trent McDuffie and allowing cornerback Jaylen Watson and safety Bryan Cook to depart in free agency, the franchise countered by drafting LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane No. 6 overall. It also signed veteran safety Alohi Gilman and brought back cornerback L'Jarius Sneed , whom they had traded to the Titans in 2024. Second-year cornerback Nohl Williams is more than halfway to last season's total snaps played.
Although inexperienced at this level, Williams and Delane have shown enough to suggest they could be even better than some of the duos Kansas City has employed in recent years. Spagnuolo requires his defensive backs to play the run and tackle. Delane has shown a willingness to play downhill,but has room for improvement in coming to balance in space and finishing tackles.
The team saved money by moving McDuffie and not signing the aforementioned veterans from last year's team. The savings were funneled toward the addition of Walker and others — a redistribution of resources. Opposing quarterbacks have the fourth-lowest passer rating against the Chiefs this season. The re-made secondary is doing its job.
The Chiefs' pass attack is still not where it needs to be, especially given injuries, but establishing the run game has made the franchise less one-dimensional. They have more answers than simply requiring Mahomes to be Superman. An injury to Tyquan Thornton may lead the organization to pursue its options, which are expanded to include former Chief Tyreek Hill and the Browns ' Jerry Jeudy .
Aside from Kelce, the team's primary outlets in the pass game are Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy . Jalen Royal's three receptions are the only other contributions from the receiver room.
The offensive line has also not gone according to plan, but I have already written extensively about the unit , particularly undrafted free-agent left tackle Kahlil Benson .
The early-season schedule has not been overly stimulating, but the path ahead is not littered with obstacles either. Enjoying a bye this week and embracing an early-season chance to get healthy, the team returns to action next week against the floundering Chargers . As one of three undefeated teams, the Chiefs are well on the way to a postseason return.

title: NFL trade deadline: 10 candidates who could be on the move and teams that could be buyers, sellers
summary: Big-name pass rushers and struggling former first-round wideouts could be on the trading block. Plus, potential landing spots for top targets ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline
full_text:
Now that we are in October, we are officially just one month away from a significant date on the NFL's calendar: the trade deadline.
Once 4 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 10, passes, all NFL teams are prohibited from trading players away. Last year's trade deadline was rather dramatic, as the New York Jets shipped off a couple of star players in cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . The Jacksonville Jaguars made a vital addition in wide receiver Jakobi Meyers , and the Seattle Seahawks added a key returner in Rashid Shaheed , who contributed to their Super Bowl run.
This year, we've already seen the Baltimore Ravens acquire a new center in Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles , the Dallas Cowboys trade two draft picks for former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , and the New York Giants send a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for J.J. McCarthy in the wake of the Jaxson Dart injury. Who could be next?
Below, we will break down 10 players who could potentially be on the trade block, plus a handful of teams that could be buyers or sellers over the next month.
Given how this season has started, it's fair to list former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr . as a potential trade target. The Arizona Cardinals wideout has never averaged more than 52 yards per game in any of his three seasons, and his production is trending the wrong way. Through four games, Harrison has caught just five passes for 85 yards and one touchdown. During Sunday's loss to the Giants, he played 65.2% of snaps on offense.
He's looked slow running routes and has struggled with drops, too. Last year, Harrison had to fight through a myriad of injuries, including an appendectomy and a foot issue. One could speculate that some of his struggles have been mental, so a change of scenery would make sense. However, the Cardinals aren't just going to punt on their former No. 4 overall pick.
The Athletic has reported that the Cardinals are not desperate to deal Harrison — at least not yet. That could change if a team is willing to offer considerable compensation, but what kind of compensation would Arizona want, and would any team actually meet that price? Harrison is under contract for 2027, but his team will have to decide on his fifth-year option this upcoming offseason.
Potential landing spot : Indianapolis Colts
ESPN mentioned Los Angeles Chargers pass rusher Khalil Mack as a trade candidate this past week . This is a 35-year-old player on an expiring deal, playing for a team that's arguably the biggest disappointment in the NFL this season. He should be helping a team that's contending.
Mack has actually recorded three sacks in four games for the lowly Chargers this season to go along with 14 tackles and 13 pressures. The former No. 5 overall pick was named Defensive Player of the Year in 2016 and is only three years removed from his last double-digit sack season, recording a career-high 17 QB takedowns in 2023. Wouldn't it be something if he returned to Chicago, where he spent 2018-2021?
Potential landing spot : Chicago Bears
Let's talk about another Cardinal. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that pass rusher Josh Sweat has been a trade target for some time now. It makes sense. He reunited with his former defensive coordinator, Jonathan Gannon, in 2025, signing a four-year, $76.4 million deal with the Cardinals prior to the 2025 season. He recorded a career-high 12 sacks for the 3-14 Cardinals, and then his coach was fired.
The Super Bowl champion is in his age-29 season and has played 50% of defensive snaps this year. Maybe reuniting him with Gannon again in Green Bay is a possibility, but what about returning to the team that drafted him in the fourth round back in 2018?
Potential landing spot : Philadelphia Eagles
Brian Thomas Jr . hit the ground running in the NFL, catching 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie in 2024. He was the fourth rookie since 1970 to cross 1,200 yards receiving and double-digit touchdowns, joining an elite list that includes Randy Moss, Odell Beckham Jr . and Ja'Marr Chase . However, his production has since fallen off, and his role has diminished.
BTJ caught 48 passes for 707 yards and just two touchdowns in 2025, while dropping 10 passes — tied for second-most in the NFL. This season, Thomas has caught nine passes for 105 yards and one touchdown in four games. He's played under 63% of offensive snaps in each game this year, and is averaging just 26.3 yards per game. It felt like his play forced the Jaguars to go out and pick up Jakobi Meyers at last year's trade deadline, who came in and led the team in targets (61), receptions (42) and receiving yards (483) from the day he was acquired to the end of the regular season.
If the Jags trust rookie Josh Cameron will continue to ascend, could Jacksonville entertain offers for Thomas?
Potential landing spot : Las Vegas Raiders
Walker Little has been mentioned as a trade candidate for several months now for a couple of different reasons. One, Little has been benched for Cole Van Lanen , but he has also played snaps at every position along the offensive line, minus center. He's made 39 starts in 74 games played, and should receive interest if he were available.
The Jaguars wouldn't want to part ways with their swing tackle for no reason, so any interested team better have an offer worth considering. We've seen the Jaguars trade offensive tackles at the deadline before, as they shipped Cam Robinson to the Vikings in October 2024. Granted, Robinson was on an expiring deal. That is not true for Little.
Potential landing spot : Green Bay Packers
The top two running backs for the Tennessee Titans are on expiring deals, and one could be moved if the right team comes calling. Tony Pollard is averaging 55.3 rushing yards per game this season with one touchdown, but he and Derrick Henry are actually the only players to have reached 1,000 yards rushing in each of the last four seasons. He recorded a career-high 1,082 rushing yards in 2025.
As for Tyjae Spears , he's a playmaker who just hasn't had the impact the Titans thought he would when he was selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft . He reached 800 scrimmage yards as a rookie but hasn't crossed 550 yards in a single season since, and he missed nine games over the last two years due to injury. I thought the Packers could have traded for one of these players instead of Kaleb Johnson before the regular season. Could Green Bay double-dip in the RB trade market if it receives bad news regarding Josh Jacobs ' situation?
Potential landing spot : Green Bay Packers or Philadelphia Eagles
The former Patriot spent last year with the Eagles and then signed a one-year deal with the Miami Dolphins . He's recorded 17 tackles and one sack with four QB hits over the first four games of the season, and really stood out on the defensive front during Sunday's loss to the Vikings. With Josh Uche being four years older than former first-round pick Chop Robinson , he may be the player that's easier to acquire for a contender looking for pass-rush help. PFF ranks Uche 27th among 108 qualified edge defenders this season.
Potential landing spot : Baltimore Ravens
Kayvon Thibodeaux was expected to step up with Brian Burns ' season-ending injury, but he recorded just two combined tackles and zero sacks playing 95.5% of defensive snaps vs. the Cardinals on Sunday. He's had just one quarterback hurry in four games played. The former No. 5 overall pick out of Oregon recorded 11.5 sacks in 2023 but has had just eight since.
Thibodeaux has been the subject of trade rumors for quite some time now. It remains to be seen if the Giants would want to move him for a Day 3 pick, but why not if Joe Schoen/John Harbaugh have no interest in signing him to a new deal? A change of scenery could give him a boost.
Potential landing spot : Cleveland Browns

title: Super Bowl stock report for NFL Week 5: Jaguars enter peak form, Eagles trend toward rebuild
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 4 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
The NFL International Series rolls on in Week 5 with the second of three games in London, and it marks the first of two consecutive contests in England for the Jacksonville Jaguars . Liam Coen's team returns to its "home away from home" across the Atlantic Ocean for a matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles : A contest between two teams trending in opposite directions.
If the Eagles are to save their season and return to Super Bowl contention after back-to-back losses, this is an ideal spot to prove they can beat one of the best teams in the league. If the Jaguars handle their business as favorites, they will extend their winning streak to three games and improve to above .500 all-time in games held in London.
That is not the only impactful showdown on the road to the Super Bowl this week. In fact, even more seismic collisions occur on the West Coast with an NFC West battle between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks and a meeting between the two Super Bowl favorites in the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills .
Here is a look inside the Super Bowl race entering Week 5.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
The next time the Jaguars play on American soil will be in November. Each of their next two games come in London as they become the first NFL team to play consecutive home regular-season games in an international market. For most teams, the departure from the friendly confines of their domestic home stadium to spend two weeks abroad could be seen as a hindrance. For the Jaguars, games in England are nothing new. They should have a logistical advantage over the Eagles and Texans , and they are simply the better team in both matchups, too.
Trevor Lawrence last week finally got a Joe Burrow-sized monkey off his back, as the Jaguars defeated the Bengals 22-17 for Lawrence's first head-to-head win over Burrow in four tries. Jacksonville now has two consecutive victories under its belt in response to its Week 2 loss and might be in the early stages of another extended winning streak. It will be favored in each of its next three games.
Lawrence is easily a top-10 quarterback , but most impressive during the 3-1 start has been the defense. The Jaguars rank second in scoring defense at just 13.3 points allowed per game. The unit stands fifth in EPA per pass despite having to match up against Burrow's high-octane aerial assault and the reigning MVP runner-up, Drake Maye , in consecutive weeks. This squad is more well-rounded than ever and looks poised to avenge last year's 35-7 loss in London with a pair of overseas wins.
The odds of Nick Sirianni bringing a second Super Bowl to the City of Brotherly Love in three years are nearly twice as long now as they were heading into Week 4. That is the product of a miserable offensive showing in which the Eagles set a franchise record with 12 third downs without a conversion en route to a 24-20 loss to the Rams. They squandered a 10-point lead in the final four minutes and have now lost two in a row after opening at 2-0. And those two wins to begin the season were hairy, one-score outcomes against bad teams.
This season is heading in the wrong direction for Sirianni. Not all of that is his fault, but he now has work to do in order to save his job , because the pressure is officially on in Philadelphia.
The Eagles closed Week 4 without 10 key players. Injuries to Saquon Barkley , DeVonta Smith , Zack Baun and numerous other starters ravaged their roster. Further depleting the squad, Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL, and Philadelphia traded Cam Jurgens in an overhaul of what used to be a stout offensive line. That trade might signal that the Eagles are already prepared to pack things up and move on to next year.
With the 12-longest odds to win the Super Bowl, the market might not have caught up to the Falcons quite yet. This is no championship frontrunner, but it is a completely different team with Michael Penix Jr . running the offense, and it is one that at least deserves the respect of a division favorite .
When Cooper Rush was under center, the Falcons lost their first two games, scored a combined 16 points and coughed up seven turnovers. In the two games with Penix at quarterback, the offense racked up 80 points, managed nearly twice as many yards and turned the ball over just once. Atlanta went from 0-2 to 2-2 at the flip of a switch. Now that there is a signal-caller in the lineup capable of feeding the ball to Drake London , Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts , a unit that stands among the NFL's most talented collection of skill players can excel.
It is not just the offense that is getting the job done now, too. The Falcons also rank third in the league with a 43.6% pressure rate and boast the NFL's stingiest run defense by a hefty margin, having allowed just 48.3 yards per game. All of that is without Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr . on a defensive front that was supposed to sputter in their absences.
Monday, 8:15 p.m., ABC, stream on Fubo
With respect to the Australia game between the Rams and 49ers, Week 5 presents the biggest showdown of the year thus far. Los Angeles hosts the Bills in what may be a Super Bowl preview. These two teams hold the best odds to hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy. Both star-studded squads need a momentum-building win in this spot because the Rams did not appear nearly as strong as expected in their 2-2 start and the Bills seek to avoid a two-game losing streak on the heels of their first loss of the year.
Sunday, 4:25 p.m., Fox, stream on Fubo
The 49ers are already the top team in the NFC West with a 4-0 record and two wins in divisional play, but they can take complete command of football's best division with a win in Week 5. They already topped the Rams in their season-opening blowout, so to defeat the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks on the road would be the second statement win over a divisional foe in the first quarter of the season. Seattle's defense let off the gas over the last two weeks and needs to get right in this big spot, because the next four games are a gauntlet.
Sunday, 9:30 a.m., NFL Network, stream on Fubo
A loss in England would not end the Eagles' season, but it might create the kind of downward spiral that derails the rest of the campaign. A three-game losing streak amid the onslaught of injuries and coaching scrutiny Philadelphia faces at this juncture would be awful for momentum. On the flip side, this is where the Jaguars need to pounce. Squaring off against a downtrodden team, they have a chance to build early separation in a top-heavy AFC South and cement themselves as a top-tier conference championship contender.

title: NFL Week 5 upset alert: Why these five favorites could easily lose, including the Patriots
summary: After accurately identifying three major upsets last week, we examine five more for Week 5
full_text:
No favorite appears to be safe these days in the NFL , as underdogs have come on strong over the first month of the regular season.
In the past two weeks, a total of 23 games have been decided by one score, which is tied for the most in a two-week span in NFL history. Naturally, those coin-flip games have produced quite a bit of upsets, and we've largely been on the scent with them. In last week's upset alert, we accurately identified the Texans , Lions , and Saints as favorites ripe to fall short, with the Cowboys , Panthers , and Falcons each pulling off upsets.
Now, we turn our focus to Week 5, where there are several home underdogs, which always put our antenna up. Three of which you can find below, as they could stun the road favorites this weekend, along with two AFC East favorites possibly on shaky ground at home.
All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
New England is coming off its biggest win of the season after going up to Buffalo and upsetting the Bills to get to 2-2 on the year. After it felt like the sky was falling in Foxborough, that win -- at least for the moment -- stabilized things. That said, this does feel like a possible letdown spot for the Patriots after such a monumental victory. They host a Raiders team that saw its undefeated 3-0 start get snapped by the Kansas City Chiefs last week, but Las Vegas largely hung in there. The defeat didn't expose them as fool's gold. Rather, I expect them to go into Gillette Stadium and make the Patriots sweat.
Vegas ranks sixth in the NFL in pressure rate (42.5%) and fifth in sack rate (8.7%). Drake Maye was much improved against Buffalo's pressure last week, but he's still struggled overall when under duress and has had a propensity to turn the ball over. If that rears its head here, Kirk Cousins -- who is tied for the league lead in passing touchdowns (11) -- should be able to take advantage.
I don't think it's hyperbole to call this a make-or-break game for Green Bay. A loss at home to Chicago would drop them to 2-3 on the season and, more importantly for tiebreaker situations, 0-2 in the NFC North. That's the makings of a hole that'll soon be too big to claw out of, no matter if Micah Parsons and/or Josh Jacobs return. So, with that in mind, I think the Packers -- who are admittedly flawed -- could throw the kitchen sink at a Bears team that is still dinged up.
On top of Caleb Williams (hamstring) still being out and Tyson Bagent set to start at quarterback, Kyle Monangi (thumb) and D'Andre Swift (knee, hip) did not practice on Wednesday. They both could play in Week 5, but if they are limited in any way, that takes away/deminishes the identity of what this offense has been. Coming into Week 5, the Bears lead the NFL with 196.3 rushing yards per game.
It's also worth noting that the Ben Johnson-led Bears have struggled against the NFC North. Against the division, Chicago is 2-5, while they are 12-2 against everyone else.
What if the Browns are just good? Cleveland is coming off a marquee win over the Steelers in Week 4, and will have the rest advantage over the Jets after playing last Thursday. After a season opener where it looked like the Browns were going to sink to the bottom of the league, they've ripped off three straight, and Deshaun Watson has looked solid. In fact, he's been clutch. Over this winning streak, he's orchestrated three game-winning drives and has completed 15-of-20 passes, averaged 6.9 yards per attempt, and has two passing touchdowns with no interceptions in those drives.
Watson and the Browns now face a Jets team that has gone in the opposite direction from them. After winning its first game of the year, New York has lost three straight. As it relates to this matchup, it's the Jets defense that should be of central focus and possibly the reason for an upset. Sure, they got an interception last week, but the unit has struggled in the two games prior to Week 5. The Jets' defense ranks last in the NFL in yards per game allowed at 436.5. Watson also won't have to deal with a ton of pressure as New York ranks 28th in the NFL in pressure rate this season.
New York is 0-12 in its last 12 games against above-.500 teams.
The Saints were embarrassed on Monday night in a 45-24 loss to their division rival, the Atlanta Falcons, at home in primetime. Typically, a team playing on a short week might be at a disadvantage, but I'd guess New Orleans is foaming at the mouth to get back out there to get rid of the sour taste of that defeat.
Minnesota is 4-0 on the year, but that undefeated record has come despite some questionable play on offense. They've registered the third-fewest yards per game (262.8) during a 4-0 start to a season by any team since 1940. Meanwhile, Kyler Murray hasn't looked like the second coming of Sam Darnold by any stretch of the imagination to this point. Of the 28 quarterbacks who've thrown at least 70 pass attempts this year, Murray is 24th in passer rating, 25th in yards per attempt, and 27th in EPA per dropback.
Really, it's been the play of the Vikings defense that has spearheaded this undefeated start. Brian Flores' unit has allowed the fewest points per game (12.8) in the NFL this season and has by far the highest blitz rate (71%) in the league. Against the blitz this season, Saints quarterback Tyler Shough has a 105.8 passer rating (11th among QBs) and five passing touchdowns (tied for third-most in the NFL), so he has been solid in the face of added pressure.
If he can find some success against this Vikings blitz, that could be enough to pull out the win, especially if the Murray-led offense continues to struggle to get off the ground.
The Detroit Lions simply cannot be trusted as a road favorite with their current defense. They just let Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers torch them for 32 points and 329 passing yards, despite it largely just being a two-man show between Young and wideout Tetairoa McMillan (14 catches, 192 yards, and two touchdowns). Detroit's secondary is giving up a league-worst 423.8 total yards per game, and their 31.8 points per game allowed is the second-worst in the NFL.
While the Cardinals won't be mistaken for a Super Bowl contender, they have enough playmakers on offense to take advantage of the Lions' poor defense. Jacoby Brissett is coming off his worst statistical game of the season, tossing three interceptions against the Giants , but he is capable of bouncing back and throwing it around the yard, especially with the likes of Trey McBride and Michael Wilson at his disposal.

title: Cardinals work out four defensive backs
summary: This week, the Arizona Cardinals brought in four defensive backs for a workout and physical. Oftentimes, GM Monti Ossenfort will bring in a handful of players just to update his player profile lists in the event that a player will become injured. But this tryout had a specific focus: find some capable cornerbacks and safeties […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 25: Coby Bryant #8 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates with d'Anthony Bell #23 during an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 25, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, the Arizona Cardinals brought in four defensive backs for a workout and physical. Oftentimes, GM Monti Ossenfort will bring in a handful of players just to update his player profile lists in the event that a player will become injured. But this tryout had a specific focus: find some capable cornerbacks and safeties to help out. RELATED: BEAKS & GEEKS AGAINST THE GIANTS Before the season began, the defensive back group was viewed as one of the strengths of the roster. And held true until CB Will Johnson became injured and was lost for the year. Apparently, Johnson was the glue that held this room together, because the entire group has had coverage issues. To be fair, the inability of the defensive line to put good pressure on their opponents when dropping back to pass has amplified what is wrong with the defensive backfield. They can’t cover a guy forever, and without a decent pass rush, opposing pass catchers will run their routes, then break off and attempt to find open spots. This has been giving the other team’s quarterback plenty of time to survey the field and find the open guy. The four defensive backs are all safeties: D’Anthony Bell, Dan Jackson, Mark Perry, and Nate Valcarcel. Bell (6’-1”, 211 pounds) won a National Championship at the D-2 level with the University of West Florida, went undrafted, and signed with the Cleveland Browns. He played in 50 games with seven starts for Cleveland and got a name for himself on punt and kickoff coverage teams. During free agency, he signed with the Carolina Panthers for one year and finally with the Seattle Seahawks. He has 76 total tackles, 0.5 sacks, 3 QB hits, 2 interceptions, 4 pass defenses, 1 forced fumble, and 3 pressures. He runs a 4.51. Jackson (6’-1”, 195 pounds) played for Georgia and participated in two National Championships, then received a Senior Bowl invite. The Detroit Lions selected him in Round 7 of the 2025 NFL Draft and he has yet to appear in a regular-season game. He runs a 4.46. Perry (6’0”, 211 pounds) played for Colorado and TCU. He went undrafted in 2024 and signed with the Miami Dolphins but was cut on the final cutdown. He has been signed to the practice squad of five NFL teams. He has played in zero NFL contests and runs a 4.42. Valcarcel (6’-1”, 194 pounds) went undrafted in 2025 out of Northern Illinois. He signed with the Los Angeles Rams, was waived, and signed to the practice squad, where he remained for all of 2025. During the offseason, he inked a reserves/future contract and had a good training camp, but was waived on the final cutdown. He has played in zero games and runs a 4.53. Out of all the safeties who worked out, Bell was the only one with a lot of game action, as he has played in 64 total NFL games. After the tryouts, the Cardinals inked Perry and placed him on the practice squad.

full_text: A new week is underway, as the Atlanta Falcons and Baltimore Ravens prepare to face off on Sunday evening. The Falcons have now won back-to-back primetime games, and they look to make it a third. For that, they’re going to need some of their currently banged up players to get healthy. Let’s take a look! Falcons injury report Full • OT Michael Jerrell (ankle) • DE Cam Thomas (shoulder) Limited • LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) • DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring) • LT Jake Matthews (groin) Did Not Practice • LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring) • DE Za’Darius Smith (concussion/neck) Ravens injury report Full • TE Mark Andrews (hand) • WR Rashod Bateman (shoulder) • S Kyle Hamilton (groin) • WR Chris Moore (ankle) • OT Ronnie Staley (toe, ankle) Limited • WR Zay Flowers (foot) • OL John Simpson (groin) • OL Andrew Vorhees (foot) Did Not Practice • LB Trey Hendrickson (finger) • CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring, calf) • QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) • C Cam Jurgens (concussion) Looking at the Falcons first, there are some notable names to keep an eye on heading into Friday. Za’Darius Smith, who has played well recently and had a scary injury against the New Orleans Saints last week, is currently in concussion protocol. His status for this weekend is unclear, but thankfully it sounds like he dodged a major injury, as at first that’s what it appeared like. Another big name to keep an eye on is Jake Matthews who also left the Saints game with a groin injury. Matthews currently holds the longest active streak for games started in the NFL with 200. The Ravens have a very large list of players who are dealing with injuries, with none as big as Lamar Jackson who has an ankle injury. Some reports have said that Jackson may miss multiple games, while some recently have said he may still suit up on Sunday night. If he’s unable to play, the Falcons will see Tyler Huntley in his stead.

title: What to know about Falcons – Ravens Week 5 on Sunday Night Football
summary: What a difference a couple of weeks can make. After the first two games of the season, the Atlanta Falcons were left for dead by analysts, pundits, and a significant portion of their own fanbase. They were 0-2, Cooper Rush had played like one of the worst quarterbacks in the league, and the entire operation […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST17: Baltimore Ravens running back Chris Collier (38) runs with the ball against Atlanta Falcons defensive tackle Brandon Dorlus (54) during the Atlanta Falcons pre season game versus the Baltimore Ravens on August 17, 2024 at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, MD. (Photo by Mark Goldman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images What a difference a couple of weeks can make. After the first two games of the season, the Atlanta Falcons were left for dead by analysts, pundits, and a significant portion of their own fanbase. They were 0-2, Cooper Rush had played like one of the worst quarterbacks in the league, and the entire operation outside of the defense looked sloppy and disjointed. Two weeks later, the Falcons are back at .500, the hottest offense and one of the hottest defenses in the league, and looking like a surging team to be reckoned with. If you had asked any of us in Week 2 whether the Falcons could win Sunday Night Football against the typically fearsome Baltimore Ravens, we would have laughed. Now I think it’s fair to suggest Atlanta should be the favorite . How did we get here? A combination of rapid progress, the return of Michael Penix Jr., a coaching staff settling in, and now some poor injury luck for Baltimore. Let’s talk about the matchup. Team rankings Team Record Points Scored Yardage Passing Yards Rushing Yards Points Against Yardage Against Passing Yards Against Rushing Yardage Against Turnovers Created Turnovers Surrendered Falcons 2-2 15 10 25 2 15 8 30 1 23 26 Ravens 3-1 7 5 13 4 19 10 16 10 12 3 Almost across the board, the Ravens are the better team thus far in 2026. They’ve gotten more turnovers, turned the ball over less frequently, passed effectively, defended effectively, and so forth. They just don’t have quite the same caliber of run game or run defense as the Falcons. For reasons we’ll discuss below, though, this isn’t quite the true measure of either team at this moment. As we all know, the Falcons’ awful start heavily tilted their offensive numbers and turnover numbers, and they don’t even look like the same team the past two weeks. The Ravens, meanwhile, are dealing with injuries that damage their short-term outlook. How the Ravens have changed in 2026 The biggest change, of course, is the departure of John Harbaugh. He had been Baltimore’s coach since 2008, winning a Super Bowl in 2012 and compiling a 180-113 record with the Ravens, but three frustrating playoff exits in a row and an 8-9 record in 2025 were enough to get him up out of there. Former Chargers defensive coordinator Jessie Minter took over as the team’s head coach this offseason. After nearly trading for Maxx Crosby before he failed a physical, the Ravens signed Trey Hendrickson, who is a mighty fine consolation prize. They added underrated former Falcons safety Jaylinn Hawkins, guard John Simpson, former Falcons center Jovaughn Gwyn, blocking tight end Durham Smythe, and center Danny Pinter. They should have had their center depth taken care of at that point, but due to some truly incredible injury luck, that would not hold. Guard Vega Ioane joined as their first round pick, and due to their dire center situation, will be making a start at the position against the Falcons. They had a ton of picks and added talented young wideouts Ja’Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt, defensive end Zion Young, tight end Matthew Hibner, and one of my favorite running backs of this past class in Adam Randall. An already talented roster got an infusion of youth, and it’s little surprise that Baltimore remains one of the most talented teams in the league despite injuries and a new coaching staff taking over. What to know about Week 5 A full-strength Ravens team is a very tough out. The Falcons have lost four of their past five games against Baltimore and last won in 2010, and their 2022 matchup was a slopfest where Atlanta was beaten 17-9. There’s a new coach for the Ravens, but aside from an inexplicable loss to the Saints, the Ravens have gone right back to winning football and stand 3-1. But this is far from a full-strength Ravens team. Their offensive line has been wracked by heavy injuries to center, where they’re set to start rookie Vega Ioane after centers Danny Pinter, Ethan Pocic, and Jovaughn Gwyn were all placed on injured reserve. Ioane may have a bright future at center, but he certainly wasn’t expected to play there this year, and the team won’t get new trade acquisition Cam Jurgens into the lineup until after this week. That presses Andrew Voorhees into starting duties at left guard, and his work in run blocking in particular has been shaky throughout his career. Promising rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane is out. Top-shelf pass rusher Trey Hendrickson may be out. Kick returner and receiver Chris Moore is banged up. Key blocking tight end Durham Smythe is out. And by far worst of all, Lamar Jackson is very likely to miss Week 5. That all adds up to a team well shy of full strength, one weak on the interior of their offensive line and with a backup quarterback who has not historically thrived under pressure. The Ravens are still a damn good team—they can bring Derrick Henry to bear on this run defense, Tyler Huntley moves well and limits mistakes at quarterback, and the defense is still very talented—but their specific weaknesses line up with some of Atlanta’s strengths. With Zay Flowers, Marlon Humphrey, Rashod Bateman, and even Voorhees banged up heading into the week, this could be a very diminished offense missing a couple of key defensive pieces. The danger is that the Ravens can still punish sloppiness and mistakes. Henry is, impossibly, still doing this at age 32 and has the 13th best success rate in the league and seven touchdowns already. Huntley has been around a long time now and is an assured passer at this stage of his career who can get the ball out quickly and escape from pressure, prolonging plays and giving this passing game a fighting chance. I think the Falcons underestimate him at their own peril. The receiving corps is roughed up, but if Flowers plays, he’s a major threat who has been one of the more efficient receivers in the league this year, with Rashod Bateman quietly finding his footing as well. If Atlanta can’t generate consistent pressure and can’t wrap up Henry, there’s game-changing big play potential still alive in this offense. If the defense looks like it has the past couple of weeks, though? That’ll do nicely. Offensively, Atlanta has to beware Kyle Hamilton but can pick on these safeties otherwise. Malaki Starks and Jaylinn Hawkins are both scuffling in coverage and will have the tall task of picking up Kyle Pitts and serving as insurance against Drake London and Bijan Robinson breaking big gains; the Ravens run defense has also been lackluster by their standards in 2026. This is still a group that can hurt you—there’s a healthy pass rush here even if Hendrickson is out or limited, and Hamilton is an all-world caliber safety—but it’s going to be tougher sledding than it has been in years past. If the Falcons stick with a run-first gameplan, they should be able to make plenty of headway. Special teams is solid enough in Baltimore, but their best kick returner Chris Moore (who is also a solid receiving option) is working his way back after missing last week. Tyler Loop has been nails from long distance but has missed two of his four kicks from 40-49 yards; that’s sort of the opposite problem Atlanta has with Nick Folk, who they don’t appear to trust from distance. Oh, and on top of all that, the Ravens are third in the NFL in penalties with 39 and second in penalty yardage at 329, with the second-highest false start total in the league working against an aggressive, attacking Falcons front. The circumstances here—the potent primetime Falcons, their hot play, being at home, the Ravens being so dinged up and minus Jackson—set this up for Atlanta to win if they can just seize the…
