title: Week 5 game preview: Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers
summary: Shifting expectations are difficult. For years, I dreaded when the Chicago Bears would face the Green Bay Packers. Even in the years when Chicago was good, it still felt like an uphill climb to beat the team up north. In the down years, of which there have been far too many, I was resigned to […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 4: Wide receiver Matthew Golden #0 of the Green Bay Packers completes the fourth and goal for the touchdown in the second quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Shifting expectations are difficult. For years, I dreaded when the Chicago Bears would face the Green Bay Packers. Even in the years when Chicago was good, it still felt like an uphill climb to beat the team up north. In the down years, of which there have been far too many, I was resigned to yet another humiliation at the hands of the green and gold, their smug quarterback and their young darling of a head coach. But the tide is turning. The shift started with the drafting of Caleb Williams but really hit last season with Ben Johnson. Johnson wasn’t afraid to come in and talk a little trash. He wasn’t afraid to embrace the rivalry, the recent one-sidedness of it and look at all that in the eye and say, ‘bring it.’ Now, Green Bay is off to a rough start. They’ve struggled just to be at .500. There are still years of pain deep in my gut, telling me not to be confident. Not to fall into a trap. As if perhaps Green Bay has purposely laid a 2-2 subpar start to the season just to set the Bears up, only to once again knock us down and laugh. But then I see the state of the rosters, the weaknesses, the strengths, the stats. I’ve said I won’t believe the tide has shifted in the series until the Bears can sweep the season series against the Packers. That can’t happen Sunday, but they can win their third straight, which is awfully close. I know Green Bay is going to give everything they can to beat Chicago Sunday. And they absolutely can do it. The NFL is truly an any-given-game-day league. But with Ben Johnson on our sideline, I like our odds and I’ll take my chances with him anytime we can get it. Green Bay Packers SB Nation site: Acme Packing Company Record: 2-2, third in the NFC North Last week: 17-14 win over the Buccaneers Game day, time, TV: Noon CT Sunday on FOX Spread: Bears -2.5 Bears all-time record against: 98-109-6, including 2-1 in the postseason Historical meetings: Week 5 of 2007. The 1-3 Bears traveled to Lambeau to face the 4-0 Packers. Green Bay scored first with DeShawn Wynn rushing for a two-yard touchdown. The Bears started by going three-and-out on their first three possessions. The Bears got the ball on two consecutive drives by Charles Tillman using his patented Peanut Punch on receiver James Jones. Finally, though, following a Green Bay three-and-out, the Bears put together a 12-play drive. The Bears committed an illegal formation on a Roobie Gould field goal attempt, giving the Bears fresh downs. Cedric Benson scored a 10-yard rushing TD two plays later.The Packers answered right back with a 41-yard Favre-to-Greg Jennings strike. Following some field goals, Brian Urlacher picked off Favre and Griese threw a 19-yard touchdown to Greg Olsen on the very next play. In the fourth quarter, it was more of the same until Griese put together one more drive and hit Desmond Clark for a 34-yard score to break the 20-20 tie. The Bears picked off Favre’s heave toward the endzone with 8 seconds left and won 27-20. Last meeting: In week 16, the Bears were down 16-6 with less than 2:15 to play. The Bears kicked a field goal, recovered an onside kick, scored a touchdown and went to overtime. They stopped the Packers on fourth down and scored a walk-off touchdown to DJ Moore. ROLL THE TAPE: Oh, wait, that was the last regular-season meeting. I’m so sorry. In the Wild Card round, the Bears trailed 21-3 at halftime. After two field goals cut it to 21-9, the Bears scored with D’Andre Swift to make it 21-16. But on the next drive, the Packers hit Matthew Golden for a 23-yard touchdown. But Caleb Williams hit Olamide Zaccheaus for an 8-yard score; the defense got the Bears the ball back and Williams hit D.J. Moore for a 25-yard touchdown pass to win, 31-27. ROLL THE TAPE! Injury report: The Packers list nine players as limited on their Wednesday report. Limited participation T Anthony Belton (knee) DT Anthony Campbell (ankle) EDGE Lukas Van Ness (shoulder) WR Savion Williams (ankle) DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle) Did not participate G Aaron Banks (knee/toe) RB Chris Brooks (ankle) C/G Jager Burton (back) C/G Jacob Monk (quadricep) Offense: The Packers come into the game ranked 28th in points and 20th in yards. Their passing offense ranks 11th and their rushing offense ranks 32nd. Jordan Love’s (56.5 pct. cmp./1,041 yds./8 TD/3 INT) numbers don’t match what they typically are, but it doesn’t seem like it’s all on him. Leading weapons are Christian Watson (20 rec./331 yds/4 TD), last year’s first-round pick Matthew Golden (18/274/2) and TE Tucker Kraft (15/148/1), who is back from his injury. Jonnu Smith (5/85/0), Skyy Moore (6/35/0) and Jayden Reed (4/24/0) also make some plays. The ground game is led by MarShawn Lloyd (30 att./81 yds/0 TD) and Kaleb Johnson (20/80/0). Johnson was acquired in a late-summer trade from Pittsburgh. Chris Brooks (15/70/0) also gets some totes. Lloyd (9 rec./49 yds.) gets the most passing targets. Defense: The Packers defense ranks 23rd in points and 14th in yards. Their passing defense ranks fourth and their rushing defense ranks 28th. Down both Micah Parsons and Ederrin Cooper, Lukas Van Ness (2.5 sk/6 TFL/3 QB hits) is the main pass-rushing threat now. He’s been good this year, but can he be a one-man show? Leading tacklers are S Evan Williams (34 tkl/2 TFL/1 INT/4 PD), Zaire Franklin (30 tkls/1 TFL/1 QB hits) and Keisean Nixon (25 tkls/3 PD/1 INT/2 TFL). In the secondary, Xavier McKinney (1 INT/1 PD/1 sk/17 tkl) and Javon Bullard (23 tkls/2 PD/3 TFL) are making plays. Key match-ups: Look at the run defense numbers for Green Bay. Ben Johnson is going to want to attack them on the ground in every which way. And Green Bay will likely sell out to try and stop it, to make Tyson Bagent beat them. If Bagent can keep the floaters to a minimum and keep the ball out of harm’s way, there will be play-action opportunities. Otherwise, a steady dose of D’Andre Swift (secure the ball!) and Kyle Monangai, as well as sweeps with Luther Burden or getting Roschon Johnson involved again. Whatever Ben feels like dialing up. On defense, the secondary is going to have to keep Watson and Golden contained. Getting pressure on Jordan Love with four would be ideal, but let’s be realistic. Dennis Allen will have to pick and choose when to blitz to not let Watson have deep opportunities. The interior of Green Bay’s line is bad, though, so getting pressure will hopefully be a little easier. Key stats The Packers have zero rushing touchdowns this season. The Bears have the second-most in the league with nine. Green Bay has the highest three-and-out rate in the league at 45.5 percent. Their third-down offense ranks last in the league, converting just 26.1 percent of the time. Their third-down defense isn’t much better; it ranks 29th, allowing 48.2 percent of their third downs to be converted. The Packers also have the worst-ranked red zone defense. Opponents are scoring 85.7 percent of the time inside the 20. Green Bay has six offensive turnovers this season already. They had 13 in the entire 2025 season. The Bears rank first in time of possession and average drive length in time. The Packers’ average drive length in time ranks 32nd Am I crazy for still sowing a bit of paranoia about the team up north? How are you feeling heading into Sunday’s game?

title: Bears’ Tyson Bagent looking to build on Jets’ performance against Packers
summary: The Chicago Bears will head to Green Bay this week without their starting quarterback, as Tyson Bagent is set to start in place of Caleb Williams, who continues to work through a hamstring injury. Bagent stepped in for Williams last week against the New York Jets, leading the Bears to a 23-12 victory. He completed […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears makes a pass during the first quarter of the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears will head to Green Bay this week without their starting quarterback, as Tyson Bagent is set to start in place of Caleb Williams, who continues to work through a hamstring injury. Bagent stepped in for Williams last week against the New York Jets, leading the Bears to a 23-12 victory. He completed 25 of 34 passes for 268 yards and one interception. Three other interceptions were wiped away by penalties. Despite the mistakes, Bagent gave the Bears enough at quarterback to come away with a win in his first game of the season. His performance also showed why the Bears can feel confident moving forward with him, while leaving room for improvement heading into a much tougher divisional matchup. QB Performances, Week 4 (pre-MNF) 1. Drake Maye 91.0 Total QBR 2. Bryce Young 85.4 3. Dak Prescott 85.3 4. Tyson Bagent 75.1 5. Kirk Cousins 72.7 pic.twitter.com/SErnq4kF4o — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) October 5, 2026 Ben Johnson pointed to a few areas where Bagent can still improve heading into Sunday’s matchup against the Packers: “There’s probably a couple plays last week where I thought our second-level throws were available to us, and we didn’t pull the trigger on them. That’s just one of those things, we just need to see it,” Johnson said. Bagent showed he can operate this offense effectively, but there are still opportunities for him to be more aggressive, particularly when plays develop down the field. Johnson also expressed wanting Bagent to trust his pass catchers and give them opportunities to make plays on the ball. “It would be encouraging from the coaching staff to him, you get the green light, man,” Johnson said. “[I] have a lot of confidence in how our pass catchers are playing right now. I thought they did a nice job going up for the ball when given the opportunity last week, and so we’re going to need more of that this week.” Johnson said the focus this week is on carrying over what worked in Bagent’s game last week while making the necessary adjustments ahead of his second. “We’re just looking to get better from his first start to his next start … he’s just gotta figure out what he did well, keep doing that, and then the things that we need to improve on, we’ll improve on.” Bagent won’t need to completely reinvent his game against the Packers. If he can build on what worked against the Jets, take advantage of opportunities downfield and lean on the run game, the Bears will look for him to keep the offense moving in Green Bay.

title: Bryan Cook doesn’t want to hurt the Bengals defense by playing injured
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-2, and while that record very much keeps them right in the thick of things at this point in the season, there are some reasons to worry. One of those reasons is the health of the team’s secondary. The Bengals were without starting safety Bryan Cook and backup safety Kyle Dugger […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-2, and while that record very much keeps them right in the thick of things at this point in the season, there are some reasons to worry. One of those reasons is the health of the team’s secondary. The Bengals were without starting safety Bryan Cook and backup safety Kyle Dugger last week, and Jordan Battle was limited throughout the week with a hamstring injury. With Battle’s struggles on the field and the lack of experience of the other safeties on the roster, it would be nice to know that Cook and Dugger will be good to go on Sunday. It’s still too early to tell, but Cook was very clear on Thursday that he wouldn’t play if he didn’t feel like he could pull his weight on the field. “You know how much I love my teammates, and I want to be playing, but I can’t be selfish in that aspect,” he said per Mike Petraglia. “But at the same time, I feel if I’m not being who they need me to be on the team, on the field, I’m hurting my teammates. So I never let that happen. “It’s always team first at the end of the day. So if I can be what I need to be for my team, I’ll be out there. And if I feel like I’m giving them less than myself, I’ll never let that happen. It’s always team first at the end of the day.” Cook injured his right ankle in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals are playing one of the winless teams remaining in the league, but winning on the road is tough, and the term “any given Sunday” exists for a reason. He did not practice on Wednesday, but he was a limited participant on Thursday, which is a step in the right direction. If Cook is able to play, he could help shore up a secondary in desperate need of a solid leader at the safety position. Going into the bye week with a losing record would be an absolute gut punch. After losing the last two games, largely due to their own mistakes, they’re in desperate need of a win. Then they can worry about health in their off week. full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will be riding a two-game losing streak to South Florida on Sunday when they take on the Miami Dolphins. Their last two games have been plagued by injuries, untimely turnovers, and a defense that has struggled to get off the field on third down. The team has been practicing and meeting all week to go over their plans against Malik Willis and the Dolphins’ offense, and on Thursday, Jordan Battle spoke to the media and revealed something that has surely been brought up in the meeting room. Take a look. Jordan Battle on Malik Willis: “He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball. He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that that gives the read the break. He's… pic.twitter.com/hI4hfjzm6t — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) October 8, 2026 Battle told reporters that Willis has. tell before he throws the ball, and the defense will look for that as a cue to attack. “He has a little slight little tap before every throw, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball. He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that that gives the read the break,” Battle said. That is a nice thing to notice on film, but maybe not something you let your opponent know you’ve noticed when they have time to get it corrected between now and Sunday. Battle also acknowledged Willis’ running ability and, hopefully, taking note of that will help the defense contain him to get off the field in the crucial moments that have hurt them over the last two weeks. “He’s obviously dangerous with his feet. We know we got to be alert for that. Third and longs, they will run quarterback draws, and in the passing game, he will extend plays. So we got to be good downfield. DBs are plastering, so we got to be alert for that. He will take chances. We just got to be on, be alert on guys where they line up, Battle continued. They have clearly had their eyes on the tape this week, and hopefully, Willis doesn’t adapt too much before Sunday, and the Bengals’ defense can capitalize on the tendencies they found.

title: Bengals News: Joe Burrow wants to stick with under-center offense
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have been trying to incorporate more offense from under the center. They made an effort all offseason to work out any kinks. full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) walks for the locker room after the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 4 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. The Bengals fell to 2-2 on the season with a 22-17 loss at home. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals have been trying to incorporate more offense from under the center. They made an effort all offseason to work out any kinks. Many wondered what would happen to it after they abandoned it against the Jacksonville Jaguars in their loss on Sunday. However, Burrow isn’t going to push to trash it . “We obviously have to be better at it,” Burrow said. “We’re still going to stick with it and keep getting reps invested in that. I think it’s very valuable, so we have to be able to do it. But we need to do better.” The ending the Jaguars game was a special situation with a mixture of circumstances. The biggest was they weren’t able to run the ball well at all. Second was them falling behind while the defense wasn’t going to be able to keep them off the scoreboard regularly enough since Cam Little would be able to convert those long field goals that may usually be punts. That meant Burrow and the offense needed to go to work. Safe to say that if the run was working we would have seen more from them. Bengals News Quick Hits | Rookie WR Colbie Young Gets Some Work While Joe Burrow Takes Some Extra Work This could be a big opportunity for Young. The Bengals may be down two of their top three options on Sunday, if not all three. There should be plenty of targets up for grabs. He could easily work his way into more snaps with a good game or two. ‘Perform On His Level’ – Bengals Pass-Catching Depth Aiming to Fill Star WR Absence Against Dolphins “We came off of two losses, and we really need to get that rebound. If we don’t have those big guys out there, we still need to be able to perform. So, being out there, having one of the best quarterbacks, we need to be able to perform on his level,” Young said. “That’s what I was hoping when I was coming into this league. I know that we got guys. It’s a long season, so there was always going to be a possibility there. So I’m happy that it’s coming sooner rather than later.” Young at least understands the reality of the situation. Battle whiffed on at least two big gains that converted 3rd-and-longs. Covering is one thing, but they truly can’t tackle them either. NFL News NFL QB rankings, Week 5: C.J. Stroud, Bryce Young vault into top 10 Burrow falling out the Top 10 based on Sunday is fair. Truly, it was a great performance outside of a couple of throws, but the late interception in the red zone was a hard one to get by. Those are the little things that can move you up and down in this list. Cam Heyward won’t ‘apologize’ for sideline outburst in Steelers’ loss to Browns The wheels are falling off a little bit off in Pittsburgh, which will make that Week 3 loss hurt that much more. Aarond Rodgers and TJ Watt also had outbursts during the game. There is just a clear lack of discipline among some veterans. title: Bengals Film Room: New defensive line additions doing their part
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals dropped to 2-2 after a frustrating loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. While players like Jordan Battle continue to struggle on defense, the new additions to that defensive line played really well once again. The trio of Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence, and Jonathan Allen combined for 12 pressures during the game on Sunday. […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals dropped to 2-2 after a frustrating loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. While players like Jordan Battle continue to struggle on defense, the new additions to that defensive line played really well once again. The trio of Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence, and Jonathan Allen combined for 12 pressures during the game on Sunday. Mafe and Lawrence each recorded a sack during the game. Jonathan Allen led the defense in pressures, recording five on Sunday. He was also the highest-graded player on the defense that game with an 80.7 overall grade. He finished with an 82.7 pass rush grade. While he was the only one of the trio of guys to not record a sack this week, he was an impact player all game long, rushing the passer. His pressure was part of the reason his teammates were able to come away with sacks during the game as well. He had notable pressure when Mafe and Murphy both had their sacks on Sunday. The three new defensive line additions have certainly been doing their part early in the season. pic.twitter.com/m4xSyVSAX2 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Myles Murphy running right through talented young left tackle Anton Harrison for the sack. pic.twitter.com/NYpeoUOHPg — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 It wasn’t just his pass-rushing ability that impressed this week either; it was what he was able to do against the run. While he finished with just three tackles, his presence was felt along that defensive line. He and Dexter Lawrence have quickly established a chemistry playing beside one another. Barrett Carter quickly closing off the running lane with Jonathan Allen getting there to finish off the tackle. pic.twitter.com/PEiA20T9Un — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Jonathan Allen with the tackle for loss pic.twitter.com/DJKMiXyKcO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Speaking of Dexter Lawrence, he was his usual dominant self again this week. Lawrence finished the game with three pressures, three tackles, and a sack during the game. It isn’t just the numbers on the stat sheet either, as Dexter is constantly freeing up the linebackers to make plays against the run. He also does a dang good job of making plays against the run himself. Knight and Carter in on another run stop, this time with some help from Dexter Lawrence. That was the best game the young linebackers have both played at the same time this season. pic.twitter.com/4zUb0LhGNh — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Dexter Lawrence, Myles Murphy, Boye Mafe, and the linebackers getting the stop on 3rd down. pic.twitter.com/DvuESVuemU — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Dexter Lawrence, Demetrius Knight, and others in on the gang tackle of Tuten late in the game. pic.twitter.com/1yLasVfi39 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Dexter is such a handful for teams to deal with. Oftentimes they will have a handful of jersey when trying to block him. His power just tossed Robert Hainsey out of the club on one play, with Hainsey having no choice but to get an obvious holding penalty to protect his quarterback. That play ended up helping lead to the Jaguars only coming away with a field goal, after initially having 1st and 10 inside of the five-yard line. 1st and goal around the 2 yard line for Jacksonville and the dominance of Dexter Lawrence draws a holding call to push them back. pic.twitter.com/9e3oMtf8ci — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Not only is Dexter Lawrence a sheer force of nature with his power, but he also is giving a ton of effort out there for a guy that is 350 pounds. Lawrence was able to get his sack by chasing down Trevor Lawrence from behind. That type of effort goes a long ways in setting the tone for your teammates on that defensive line. Boye Mafe with the pressure on Trevor Lawrence, and Dexter Lawrence with the hustle to chase him down. pic.twitter.com/6MnZFs2GfX — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Boye Mafe was highly impressive rushing the passer again this week for Cincinnati. He finished the game with four pressures and a sack. He started the game off with a bang by getting to Trevor Lawrence and knocking the ball up in the air. Myles Murphy was close to intercepting the ball. Mafe with the pressure, and look how close Murphy was to picking that ball off. Also, good lawd Jonathan Allen. pic.twitter.com/swH6eobpzX — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Mafe had another pressure during the game that led directly to a Kris Jenkins Jr. sack. Mafe beat talented left tackle Anton Harrison around the edge and was almost able to come up with a strip sack on the play. Boye Mafe with the pressure, and the sack is finished off by Kris Jenkins Jr. pic.twitter.com/E7jA1ceHdS — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Mafe was buzzing around during the final possession for the defense when they absolutely had to have a stop. He set the tone for getting one by combining with Jordan Battle for a tackle behind the line of scrimmage to start the possession. Mafe and Battle combining for the tackle for loss pic.twitter.com/TdvsoqzNhT — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 On a day with a frustrating loss, it is still very apparent just how much this defensive line has improved. If they can fix some of the issues in the secondary during the season, this defense should have a chance to finish the year in a much better place than they did last season. If they do, it will be because of guys like Lawrence, Mafe, and Allen getting the job done all season long up front.

title: Zac Taylor rising up NFL Hot Seat Rankings
summary: After a thrilling 2-0 start, the Cincinnati Bengals have dropped back-to-back games against the Steelers and Jaguars and are now 2-2 going into Week 5. The Bengals also lost Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins during the loss to Jacksonville and will be working through those injuries going into the next game. After two straight losses, […]
full_text: After a thrilling 2-0 start, the Cincinnati Bengals have dropped back-to-back games against the Steelers and Jaguars and are now 2-2 going into Week 5. The Bengals also lost Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins during the loss to Jacksonville and will be working through those injuries going into the next game. After two straight losses, head coach Zac Taylor is facing heat again, and Sports Illustrated has him back on the hot seat. Connor Orr now has Taylor ranked No. 5 in his latest NFL hot seat rankings. Taylor is still riding off the fumes of a surprise Super Bowl berth in 2021, which was followed by a conference title game appearance in 2022. Since that season, the Bengals have yet to make the playoffs. Last year, we ran up against a bizarre situation in which it was revealed that the Bengals quietly extended Taylor, though the team and the coach declined to address it. This is fair criticism considering the Bengals have no business being 2-2 with this roster, and the in-game management, game planning, and offensive playcalling are still frustrating to watch. Yes, the season is still incredibly early, but similar issues from the past few seasons are coming to the surface again, and winning is the biggest cure when that happens. One of the biggest issues right now is that Taylor’s offense is still incapable of establishing the run with a healthy Joe Burrow, and that created so many problems for this unit against Jacksonville. Burrow reassured everyone in his press conference that no one is panicking and the season is still incredibly early, but with these injuries stacking up and issues coming back around, it is fair for everyone to have concerns.

title: Browns keep adjusting on defense and finding success
summary: The Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 season uncertain but hopeful about the defensive side of the ball. With defensive end Myles Garrett in Los Angeles after an offseason trade and defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz at home after being passed over for the head coaching job, no one knew exactly what to expect. Things got off […]
full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 season uncertain but hopeful about the defensive side of the ball. With defensive end Myles Garrett in Los Angeles after an offseason trade and defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz at home after being passed over for the head coaching job, no one knew exactly what to expect. Things got off to a rocky start, to say the least, in Week 1 against Jacksonville as the Browns gave up 34 points as part of a four-touchdown day from Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence. Since then, the defense has found its footing and been a key part of the team’s current three-game winning streak: First, it was denying Tampa Bay on its final possession of the game in a four-point win in Week 2. In the home opener, they flummoxed Carolina’s high-flying offense as the only team to hold the Panthers under 30 points so far this season. Last week, it was about confusing and abusing Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers (two interceptions and five sacks) in a three-point win. So what has gotten into the defense since the opener? One of the big talking points coming out of the Jacksonville game was how Rutenberg had the defense play zone coverage on 80 percent of Lawrence’s pass attempts, the fourth-highest rate by a Cleveland defense since 2023, according to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi . Since then, the Browns have gotten back to what they do best and are now playing man coverage on 50 percent of opponents’ pass attempts, highlighted by playing man on almost 74 percent of Rodgers’ pass attempts last week, the highest rate by a team this season, according to Oyefusi . But it is more than just doing what the players are good at (and prefer). Rather, it is about looking at each game and coming up with the best plan possible, as Rutenberg explained on Thursday : “Not going to go too deep into what went into it, but as we’re all learning and progressing through the season, it is week to week to week to week in the NFL, and you guys know that. You guys have been covering the NFL. I’ll steal (Todd Monken’s) line that it’s constantly under construction. And the truth is each little week is a season, right? Because this thing is a marathon, it’s a grind. “And every week you’re trying to find that winning edge. You’re trying to find that winning margin. You’re trying to eliminate the things that can hurt you, build on the things that can help you, and week to week finding your players’ superpowers, finding what can make your players go, what can make your coaches go, and then building on that week to week and then having the humility to say, ‘oh, that didn’t go as we thought, let’s work it back to this way.’ And it’s a credit to our players for constantly trying to find those inches in their game.” It is certainly not a novel approach to hear that teams change their game plans each week based on the opponent. (Although it is a bit disconcerting that Rutenberg has to explain it during a press conference.) What is refreshing is Rutenberg being willing to recognize when things are going wrong and making the proper adjustments. Again, that may sound like coaching 101, but there have been plenty of coaches come through this town who were more focused on fitting the players to their system, no matter how bad that fit was, rather than adapting the system to the ability of the players. The Browns may not have liked what they saw on the field in Week 1 in Jacksonville, but Rutenberg and the defense deserve credit for not letting that poor performance turn into a multi-week issue. full_text: All offseason, Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry looked to upgrade the team’s defensive end position after trading away DE Myles Garrett . Berry brought in DE Tyus Bowser for a workout and passed. Former Cleveland DE Jadeveon Clowney returned for a visit , then signed with the Houston Texans . Same with DE Za’Darius Smith heading to the Atlanta Falcons . Recently, we’ve covered the rumor floating around about DE Khalil Mack , who, along with DE Josh Sweat , could be available before the NFL trade deadline. Mack and Sweat could help DE Jared Verse be more than a force multiplier for the Browns defense, but defensive end might not be the team’s biggest need. Cleveland has been getting a lot of pressure on the quarterback, despite the relatively low sack numbers: Browns 4th in pressure rate, 3rd in quick pressure rate, 10th in non blitz pressure rate and 9th in sack rate without Myles Garrett are promising stats to start the season. https://t.co/3Fh64gbMn2 — Colb (@___Colb___) October 6, 2026 Two of the late additions to the Browns roster have been getting a lot of pressure: Two late additions to the Browns’ EDGE rotation are paying dividends through four games. Derek Barnett and Sam Williams rank eighth and 24th, respectively, in pressure rate. (📸: @Browns ) pic.twitter.com/pdKtTCPqRR — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) October 6, 2026 As one of our commenters noted, defensive tackle is probably a bigger need for the Browns: A look at the Browns injury report to start Week 5 seems to confirm that, with DT Mason Graham expected to miss a few weeks and DT Mike Hall Jr. missing the first practice ahead of the New York Jets. DT Kalia Davis is not eligible to return from injured reserve , but has three weeks to do so, leaving only DTs Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington at the position on the team’s 53-man roster. Cleveland’s practice squad includes Sam Kamara (listed as a DT, plays more DE), Zion Logue , and Chris Williams at the defensive tackle position. The problem is that good defensive tackles are hard to find. ESPN listed Daron Payne as an option if the Washington Commanders continue to falter. CBS Sports had no defensive tackles on their Top 10 list. The Athletic added Grover Stewart to Payne , but the Indianapolis Colts are 2-2 and in second place in the AFC South. Pro Football Focus added A’Shawn Robinson and Zach Sieler as potential trade options as well. A look at the names on the list and the relatively short nature of the above list is an indicator of how hard it is to find good defensive tackles, much less ones that teams are willing to move on from. Big contracts tend to be dolled out for big guys in the middle of the defensive line, whether their performance on the field deserves the money. Can Berry work some magic and find a team willing to deal from a position of premium value with few, overall, options? Is defensive tackle a bigger need than defensive end? How soon would the Browns be willing to go more in on the 2026 season? What other positions should Berry and company be looking to replace, including slot cornerback? A lot of questions with over a month to go until the NFL trade deadline. Any of the defensive tackles listed above interest you for the Browns? title: Penalties are an epidemic for the NFL in 2026, not just the Browns; CLE stats are bad
summary: “No excuses, play like a champion.” – Wedding Crashers (and every NFL fan, ever) There are so many axioms when it comes to professional sports that they are hard to keep up with. The above quote, pulled from the comedic movie, has found its way into sports lore as well. Fans and media love the […]
full_text: “No excuses, play like a champion.” – Wedding Crashers (and every NFL fan, ever) There are so many axioms when it comes to professional sports that they are hard to keep up with. The above quote, pulled from the comedic movie, has found its way into sports lore as well. Fans and media love the idea that it doesn’t matter what happens; a player and/or team is expected to still perform. Last week, the Cleveland Browns could have lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers due to a blatantly missed pass interference call on WR Denzel Boston . Penalties and missed ones are a part of the game, but for the Browns, the story has been more about the myriad of ones that have been called on the team this season. Heading into Week 5, Cleveland leads the NFL with 43 penalties called against them . That is an average of almost 11 a game, a staggering number. Of those, 21 penalties were presnap, also the worst in the NFL. The Green Bay Packers (42), Baltimore Ravens (39), Los Angeles Chargers (38), and New York Jets (37) round out the top five. Not only are the Browns getting called for a lot of penalties, but they are not seeing a lot of penalties going their way, just 25, which is the bottom six in the NFL. Whether that is due to the players on the field or Cleveland’s reputation is up for interpretation. What isn’t up for interpretation is that the Browns penalty difference is tied for first in total number (-18) and tied for third worst in yardage (-97). Interestingly, penalties are an epidemic around the NFL as a whole as well: if you watched the NFL and thought something didn't feel right, you're not alone: #1 most flags in over a decade thru 4 weeks, refs are impacting the most CRITICAL moments of games most: #1 most red zone penalties per game by offenses in history #1 most penalties on 3rd/4th… — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) October 5, 2026 So, three things can be true: Officials are throwing more flags, the Browns are not getting the benefit of the calls, and Cleveland is playing undisciplined in receiving a ton of penalties. Yet, the Browns are 3-1 heading into Week 5, embodying the Wedding Crashers notion of “no excuses, play like a champion.” As the season churns on, Cleveland’s coaches and players need to figure out the penalty issue. If the Browns continue to win, hopefully the team will also start to get more calls as well. For now, refs are throwing way more flags, and Cleveland continues to scrape by despite all of their penalties. Playing like champions indeed. Are you surprised how bad the Browns have been with penalties? Surprised how many calls are being made throughout the league? title: Browns’ 3-1 start feels different
summary: Cleveland Browns fans have always been wary of fast starts. The history of this organization since its return in 1999 has not been very positive, so it is easy to be skeptical. A really exciting win can always be followed up with a challenging loss. While the season is still early, there are reasons to […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns fans have always been wary of fast starts. The history of this organization since its return in 1999 has not been very positive, so it is easy to be skeptical. A really exciting win can always be followed up with a challenging loss. While the season is still early, there are reasons to be excited about this fast start . After losing the opening game of the season, the Browns have not only won three straight games but have also shown fight and resilience in each of them. In Week 3’s matchup against the Carolina Panthers , not every drive was pretty, but the team fought hard to put themselves in a position to march down the field for a game-winning drive. All facets of the game had to work well to win this matchup. Cleveland had a similar experience in Week 4 versus the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Browns defense in particular has exceeded expectations thus far after losing Myles Garrett this offseason. From Denzel Ward to Mason Graham to Carson Schwesinger , every aspect of the defense is working together effectively. With the defense playing at this level of dominance and Deshaun Watson and the offense giving the team a chance to stay in games, confidence is only growing. The roster is also full of a lot of talented young players, which is helpful for fan-related hope. Considering Cleveland has one of the easiest schedules in the league, there is reason to feel like this season might be different. title: 3 things the Browns must do to defeat the Jets in Week 5
summary: The Cleveland Browns are at a pivotal juncture. Sitting at 3-1-0, they can either improve or implode. It happens. And not just with past Cleveland seasons, but across the league. Just gaze at the standings this year. Both the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans were playoff teams last year. The Texans were one game […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are at a pivotal juncture. Sitting at 3-1-0, they can either improve or implode. It happens. And not just with past Cleveland seasons, but across the league. Just gaze at the standings this year . Both the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans were playoff teams last year. The Texans were one game out of winning their third straight AFC South Division title. The Chargers had back-to-back 11-6-0 seasons. Yet now, both teams are 0-4-0. RELATED: BROWNS HAVE A CHANCE TO PROVE THEY BELONG Collapses happen frequently in the landscape of the NFL. And Browns fans realize this. Many expect it, while others assume it will happen at some point in the season. Up next, Cleveland travels to New Jersey to meet the New York Jets in the early game . The Jets are 1-3-0, but aren’t as bad as their record indicates. After defeating the hapless Tennessee Titans 23-10 in their opening game, they have lost two of three games by less than six points. Yes, the Chicago Bears took this roster to the woodshed in a 23-12 beatdown last week that was never close, but the Jets have been hampered by penalties, turnovers, and a lack of offense. What must the Browns do in order to defeat the Jets? Limit the penalties Okay, everyone knew this one would be front and center. The Browns are killing themselves with untimely penalties. Against the Pittsburgh Steelers, they had 14 accepted for 88 yards. There were other calls that the Steelers declined and took the yardage instead. In the first quarter alone, Cleveland had five penalties accepted, and two declined. Nine penalties in the first half. The Browns were flagged for 14 penalties, including declined flags, in their Week 3 win over the Panthers. It was the most in a game for Cleveland since a Week 6 win over the 49ers in the 2023 season. Cleveland's 34 total penalties are the second most in the NFL. — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) September 28, 2026 The term “shooting yourself in the foot” applies here. The Adin Huntington sack right before the half was wiped out by the hands-to-the-face call on Sam Williams. A third-and-eight during the first drive of the second half became a third-and-13. The pass interference call against the rookie S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was a fourth-down play that eventually became a touchdown. The nice strike to Jeudy with 1:11 left in the game was negated by a false start on LG Zion Johnson. Jared Verse’s encroachment gaffe on the one-foot line gave the Steelers offense some breathing room, and then Verse had an offside that set up the two-point conversion. In the win over the Carolina Panthers, the Browns had 12 penalties for 84 yards. Against Tampa Bay, six were accepted for 50 yards. And in the Week 1 loss to Jacksonville, Cleveland had 14 penalties for 88 yards. Fight like hell to get that fixed — Dennis Wells (@Dwellz90) September 28, 2026 For 2026, the Browns are ranked #1 in average penalties per game (10.8), #5 in penalty yards per game average (74.3), #1 in pre-snap penalties (21), #1 in penalties declined (6), and #1 in penalties accepted (43). Run the ball Head coach Todd Monken installed this new offense based on the short passing game and establishing the run. Except the Browns haven’t been a very good run team to date. Here’s the kicker: The Jets aren’t good against the run, ranking #25 in the league. That is their defensive weakness. Cleveland hasn’t used RB Quinshon Judkins that much so far in four games, as he is averaging fewer than 15 carries per game and only gets 3.0 yards per carry on average. Light him up and give him the ball against New York. Running backs still matter in this game. Judkins entered the season with Top-5 rusher expectations, but his average yards per carry and YAC numbers (94) just aren’t very good. The Jets’ rushing defense should allow Judkins an opportunity to pad his stats. Asked #Browns RB Quinshon Judkins if the first 2 opponents entering w/ statistical success in run defense played into the slow start. "It's more so about us…going into the season, what our game plan was, was to run the ball downhill at Jacksonville…the same as far as Tampa." pic.twitter.com/LhvOSd57nP — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) September 21, 2026 The Jets are in the bottom third of almost every rushing stat. They are allowing 4.3 yards per carry on average, which is respectable, and only one of 20+ yards. But they are not protecting the “A” and “B” gaps where teams are gaining their most yardage. New York is allowing a first-down run on 25% of defensive snaps. If Cleveland can wear down the Jets’ defensive front, the fourth quarter won’t provide much of a resistance. Defense must contain Jets playmakers It is no secret about WR Garrett Wilson and RB Breece Hall. They are exceptional players in this league. The Browns will need to focus on taking both guys out of the offensive game plan. The defensive focus should be to attempt to contain the Jets to 20 points or fewer. Hall hasn’t had a good year so far, with just 51 carries for 163 yards gained and a single touchdown. His best runs have been around the edge, where he has been able to cut upfield. In the trenches is where he has been turned away. That is a good plan for this talented running back. He has been nursing a quad injury since Week 3 and is currently week-to-week. Hall did not practice on Wednesday and could miss Sunday’s contest. Wilson has three 1,000-yard seasons, but he was injured last year with a knee sprain, which shut down his season. He remains a problem for every defensive backfield. Except for last year, he has always had good YAC numbers and is an explosive playmaker. Wilson is able to get good separation and is a shifty receiver. They can also change the narrative in a game. Browns DC Mike Rutenberg will need to come up with a plan so that neither of these players can control the game. Make other New York offensive players gather the spotlight, and if they produce and shine, so be it. But don’t allow both Hall and Garrett to get loose and do what they do best. What do you think is the key factor for the Browns to win in Week 5 versus the Jets? Join the conversation! full_text: (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken took a risk by opening the season with Deshaun Watson at quarterback. By now, everyone knows the story of Watson’s tenure in Cleveland, which has been marred by injuries and ineffective play on the field, and animosity from the fan base off the field. Monken could have taken the easy route and named second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders the starter. The PR boost would have been tangible given Sanders’ popularity, both in Cleveland and nationally, which would have pleased ownership. But there is little to no reason to believe the Browns would be in first place of the AFC North Division had Monken gone that route. It’s not that Watson has been lighting up opposing defenses, but since the Week 1 disaster he has been good enough when the Browns needed him, which is evident by the team’s current three-game winning streak built on a trio of fourth-quarter comebacks. While that has all been exciting – it is easy to forget how good it feels when the Browns win since they do it so rarely – Monken cautioned on Wednesday that there is still a long way to go : “We still have a marathon in the rest of the season to go, but up until this point, I think our guys have just done exactly what they’ve done since I’ve gotten here. And that’s just practice and work and believe, stay connected. So, we’ll just continue to push the envelope. They should have confidence in themselves as individual players, in their ability to make plays, and they’ve done that.” That confidence should only grow if the Browns take care of the New York Jets this week to set up a big home game against the Baltimore Ravens on October 18. But to get to that point, the Browns need practicing, working, and believing that they can make this a special season. Bucky Irving ran for a career-high 165 yards, including a 72-yard run to set up the touchdown that put Tampa Bay ahead for good while scoring twice himself, and the Buccaneers beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 on Thursday night for their first win of the season. He was deemed “questionable” to return to the game, according to Amazon’s sideline reporter Kaylee Hartung, when Dallas began a drive with 8:32 remaining in regulation. title: 3 things we learned from the Cowboys vs Buccaneers
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers just handed the Dallas Cowboys their worst loss of the season. Here are three things we learned about the Cowboys during the game. The Cowboys are untrustworthy Coming into this week, nearly the entire globe picked the Dallas Cowboys to win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a convincing fashion. Instead, […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tampa Bay Buccaneers just handed the Dallas Cowboys their worst loss of the season. Here are three things we learned about the Cowboys during the game. The Cowboys are untrustworthy Coming into this week, nearly the entire globe picked the Dallas Cowboys to win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a convincing fashion. Instead, the winless Buccaneers came into the Cowboys home and dominated them. The game took off fast for Dallas with a touchdown on the opening drive. And then we sat dazed and confused as the Cowboys offense would only put up another three points until 5:26 left in the fourth quarter. The offense that was self-coined as the “Greatest Offense There Is” looked woefully unprepared to deal with the Tampa Bay blitz. In this week’s pregame article we noted that the only viable path for the Buccaneers defense was to blitz Dak Prescott at a high rate. But that tactic would be a double-edged sword since Dak has been one of the league’s best in dealing with the blitz. The gamble paid off for Tampa Bay as the quarterback was under duress from free blitzers throughout the entire night. It affected him and the offense all night. Timings were thrown off, passes were tipped, and at times, Prescott struggled putting the ball where it needed to be. On the other side of the ball, we know the defense is bad. But they had been taking micro steps towards improvement each and every week. This week the defense held on for a while, but completely folded in the third quarter. Mistake after mistake added up, ranging from missed tackles to dropped interceptions. This unit just didn’t do much right in the second half. The finish isn’t there Late in the game, Dallas had a golden opportunity to tie it up and have a second life in overtime. DaRon Bland broke on a short pass at the sticks in prime Bland fashion, but allowed the ball to bounce right through his hands and onto the ground. That was an easy pick-six which would have put the score at 24-22. We’ve seen the veteran corner make that play with ease earlier in his career. But on a night where seemingly little went the Cowboys way, this was just one more thing to add to the list. Even after that drop, Dallas had the ball in Tampa Bay territory with another chance at a game-tying touchdown. After a drive where the offense went 99 yards to score, they were once again driving with ease. Dak looked like his normal self, George Pickens was making plays – even KaVontae Turpin and Jonathan Mingo got involved. But on a fateful second-and-one throw, Jake Ferguson popped a Dak Prescott dart into the air and into the arms of a defender, essentially sealing the win for the Buccaneers. “Of course” was the phrase uttered around Cowboys nation after the dropped pass. Regardless of what occurred during the first 52 minutes of the game, Dallas put together a game-changing goal line stand, a 99-yard touchdown drive, and had two clear chances at tying it up. Unfortunately, this team couldn’t make the plays when they mattered the most. Tyler Smith did not solve the run game When Dallas opened the game with a nine-play, 70-yard drive, the run game looked completely renewed. Javonte Williams had a huge gain of 21 yards and eventually would punch it in the endzone from the one. But through the remainder of the night, the Cowboys run game just about disappeared. Dallas would eventually abandon the run altogether, as they finished with 50 yards on 13 carries. At times, we saw push from the left side of the offensive line, but it was extremely inconsistent. There were too many negative run plays that put the Cowboys behind the sticks. Just as it impacted Prescott and the pass game, the Buccaneers blitz just didn’t allow much movement on the ground either. Expect Dallas’ rushing attack to improve as the offensive line grows and gels with Smith’s return. But for tonight, it was not close to where this offense needs it to be.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys vs. Buccaneers: 2 winners and 3 losers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys had the perfect opportunity to build on last week’s comeback victory in Houston. Instead, they were comprehensively outplayed at home by an 0-4 Tampa Bay team starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. The Cowboys looked unprepared for Tampa Bay’s pressure offensively and incapable of controlling the game defensively. There haven’t been many positives, […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys had the perfect opportunity to build on last week’s comeback victory in Houston. Instead, they were comprehensively outplayed at home by an 0-4 Tampa Bay team starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. The Cowboys looked unprepared for Tampa Bay’s pressure offensively and incapable of controlling the game defensively. There haven’t been many positives, but a couple of players have still managed to stand out in tonight’s embarrassing defeat. Winner: George Pickens George Pickens has been one of the few Cowboys offensive players capable of creating anything consistently. He made seven catches for 114 yards, including a 27-yard reception along with the fourth quarter touchdown, and he gave Dallas a threat further downfield while the rest of the passing game struggled. The frustrating part is Dallas wasn’t able to get him involved enough. With Tampa Bay attacking Prescott and disrupting the timing of the offense, Pickens frequently left waiting for opportunities. When the football did reach him, though, he has looked like one of the few Dallas players capable of changing the game. Winner: Malachi Lawrence We’re stretching our winners in that game, but the Cowboys desperately needed somebody from their pass rush to make some plays, and rookie Malachi Lawrence answered. Lawrence got to Jalon Daniels for an 11-yard sack during the third quarter, producing one of the few occasions where Dallas genuinely made Tampa Bay’s rookie quarterback uncomfortable. After entering the game with only 42 pass-rush snaps through four weeks despite owning the team’s best pass-rush win rate, Lawrence made another argument for receiving more playing time. He also recorded a pass defensed when he knocked down a ball at the line of scrimmage, and one TFL. With the Cowboys struggling badly to generate sacks through the opening month, the rookie is increasingly showing why Dallas needs to find him more snaps. Loser: Brian Schottenheimer This was one of Brian Schottenheimer’s worst offensive performances of the young season. Tampa Bay’s intentions were clear and Todd Bowles’ aggressive defensive style meant Dallas knew pressure and blitzes were coming. However, the Cowboys appeared completely unprepared for these tactics. Prescott has been hurried into decisions, receivers haven’t consistently had time to develop routes, and Dallas never found enough quick answers to punish Tampa Bay for sending extra defenders. That’s where the criticism falls on Schottenheimer. Dallas entered the game averaging 31 points per game and had just produced 28 second-half points in Houston. Against Tampa Bay, the Cowboys managed only 16 points and there was 51 minutes between Dallas scoring its first touchdown of the game, to their second touchdown scored by George Pickens in the fourth quarter, simply abysmal. When the Buccaneers changed the game with pressure, Dallas never produced a convincing counterpunch, that’s down to game planning, which falls at the feet of Schottenheimer. Loser: Dak Prescott Dak Prescott looked nothing like the quarterback who engineered last week’s comeback. Prescott went 24-of-42 for 316 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Several throws were simply inaccurate, but his response to pressure was the bigger concern. Tampa Bay sped up his internal clock and too often made Prescott hurry even before the rush actually reached him. Some responsibility belongs to the protection and the play calling, but Prescott is the veteran quarterback being trusted to identify pressure and find the correct answer. Against a defense that entered the night with only six sacks in four games, Dallas shouldn’t have looked this uncomfortable. Tampa Bay dictated the terms, and Prescott struggled to change them. Loser: Christian Parker Where to even begin with this as Christian Parker couldn’t have asked for a more favourable quarterback matchup. Tampa Bay arrived at AT&T Stadium winless, without Baker Mayfield, and with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels making only the second start of his NFL career. Rather than forcing the rookie to carry the Buccaneers offense, Dallas allowed Tampa Bay to protect him with the running game and some extremely poor tackling, with missed tackles coming in bunches at all levels of the field all night long. Bucky Irving exploded for 165 yards on 21 carries averaging nearly eight yards per carry, and that also included a 72-yard run. Tampa Bay controlled possession for more than twice as long as Dallas with a total of 37 minutes thanks to their ground game and Parker had no answer for it. Daniels, meanwhile, completed 19 of 25 passes and never turned the football over. Dallas entered Thursday ranked 31st against the run, and nothing about this performance suggests Parker has found an answer. That’s the biggest indictment. Against a rookie quarterback, the plan should have been simple, stop the run and make Daniels beat you. Dallas did the exact opposite. Instead of exposing Tampa Bay’s rookie quarterback, Parker’s defense allowed the Buccaneers to hide him behind the running game and control the football. Parker is dealing with injuries and a new scheme, but by now they should look better than they do.

title: Cowboys vs Buccaneers recap: Dallas drops a game they had no business losing
summary: The Dallas Cowboys just did what almost no one thought they would do. They were an 8.5-point favorite going against a winless team, a team playing without its starting QB, instead playing an undrafted rookie at QB in his second-ever start. They lost to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 24-16. Going into a mini-bye, the Cowboys […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys just did what almost no one thought they would do. They were an 8.5-point favorite going against a winless team, a team playing without its starting QB, instead playing an undrafted rookie at QB in his second-ever start. They lost to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 24-16. Going into a mini-bye, the Cowboys needed this game for momentum, stacking wins, and putting a turbulent early season behind them. Instead, they just raised more questions, and lost a lot of goodwill among the fanbase. The rest of the NFC East can celebrate as the Cowboys lose a game they should have won if they want to be contenders. They do not look like contenders. Brian Schottenheimer’s hot second half from last week didn’t carry over as the coach will come under more fire. Dak Prescott also struggled for large portions of the game Dallas tried to make it interesting at the end by staging a comeback, but it fell short. A deserving end for a team that certainly didn’t play winning football. Dallas is now 2-3 and stuck in a rut of not playing up to form when needed. The Texans game was a nice reprieve, but more often Dallas has just not been good enough this year. What do you think will happen in Dallas now? A recap of the action by quarter, starting from the end. Go to the bottom for the start of the game. Fourth quarter Bucs ball On 3rd-and-13, the Bucs got a pass interference penalty as Revel grabbed a receiver. Another 3rd and double-digits converted by the Bucs. Then QB Daniels used his legs to get another first down as the Cowboys defense disintegrated. From there, the Bucs just ran the ball and ground down the clock, while Daniels used his legs for more missed tackles. Finally they tried for the the kill shot on fourth down at the goal line, but were stopped. Dallas took over. Cowboys ball The Cowboys got off their goal line with a pass to Flournoy. Then Turpin and Pickens moved the ball toward midfield on completions. Pickens then provided another big play. Dallas got a first down just inside the red zone, then Pickens hit the touchdown. Dallas attempted a two-pointer but failed. 24-16. Bucs ball The Bucs start at the 35-yard line. On first down, Jaishawn Barham got hurt. The Cowboys forced a 3rd-and-9, which the Bucs almost gifted the Cowboys a pick-six, but Bland dropped it. Still the Bucs punted. Cowboys ball The Cowboys get moving with a big Flournoy reception and run, but then get hit with a holding penalty on Tyler Booker. A Jonathan Mingo catch set them up close, but once again, disaster. Prescott hit Ferguson who just missed it, popping it up for an interception. Bucs ball The Bucs get a first down on the ground, and the game is over. Dallas loses 24-16. Third quarter Bucs ball The Bucs started the second half with the ball. On their first play, a run play the Cowboys had bottled up at the line, Bucky Irving found a crease and ran all the way to the Cowboys 14-yard line. 72 yards. Then a sweep took it the rest of the way on the following play and the Bucs lead 14-10. Cowboys ball The Cowboys took over and a big play to Pickens converted a third down and picked up 26 yards. But then disaster struck as a Prescott pass was tipped and bobbled by Flournoy, bounced off two people and was intercepted. The Cowboys drive comes up empty. Bucs ball Tampa started at their own 25-yard line and immediately picked up a holding penalty. Then more disaster for Dallas, a busted coverage as Bland fell down and the pass was complete setting up the Bucs at the 15-yard line in the redzone. From there, the Bucs just bulldozed it into the endzone. 21-10 lead and the Cowboys are in big trouble. Cowboys ball Nope, not Cowboys ball. Turpin fumbled the kickoff and the Bucs took over. Bucs ball The Cowboys got a sack on first down to push the Bucs back to midfield. On third down, 3rd-and-21, the Cowboys defense gave it up. Easily. Without much fuss. The defensive secondary is broken. Also Shavon Revel got hurt in this series. The Bucs couldn’t totally capitalize after Ezeiruaku made a good play on a screen, and settled for a field goal to extend their lead to 24-10. Cowboys ball The Cowboys can’t move the ball effectively as pressure from the Bucs defense is throwing Dak off his game. The Cowboys roll the dice and go for it on fourth down, and miss. Schottenheimer is getting outclassed and Prescott is not shredding pressure like he usually does. Bucs ball Tampa took over at the Cowboys 42-yard line, almost in field goal range. A holding call backed them up leading to a 3rd and 13. Second quarter Bucs ball The Bucs had a second down at the Cowboys ten-yard line after Jaishawn Barham made a tackle at the line of scrimmage to end the first quarter. But a Rashan Gary offsides moved the Bucs to the five-yard line. Bucky Irving covered the rest of the distance on a short pass to tie the game at 7-7. Cowboys penalties really hurt on that drive. Cowboys ball KaVontae Turpin got a short pass for a first down, but after that the Cowboys faced a 3rd-and-long, and a big blitz forced a a throw into coverage that was broken up. Bryan Anger nailed a punt inside the Bucs five-yard line. Bucs ball The Cowboys defense held strong by getting pressure on Daniels, and rallying to a tackle on a wide receiver screen on third down. They got the ball back, after being assessed a holding penalty on the punt, at their own 41-yard line. Cowboys ball Williams got them going with a nine-yard pass reception, then picked up the first on a short run. Two incompletions to CeeDee Lamb brought up third down. Pressure forced Dak Prescott to scramble and throw a poor pass and the Cowboys punt. Bucs Ball An Otitio Ogbonnia facemask gave the Bucs 15 yards to their own 27-yard line. The Bucs then converted a short third down to move to their 41-yard line. Bucky Irving then broke off a 12-yard run, but the drive stalled and they ended up punting after a couple of penalties. Cowboys ball Starting at their own 12-yard line, Dallas got 10 yards on a penalty, but then did nothing again. Another punt. Bucs ball After the punt the Bucs started in good field position at their own 48-yard line. Quinnen Williams forced a holding call after breaking through the line. On third down, Markquese Bell made a great pass break up to force a punt. Cowboys ball Dallas start the drive at their own 13-yard line. Ryan Flournoy made an explosive play with a 48-yard catch. Pickens added a catch, then an offsides gave Dallas a new set of downs. After a Jake Ferguson drop on first down, pressure forced a fourth down and Brandon Aubrey nailed a short kick. Bucs ball The Bucs were unable to really move the ball to end the half. Cowboys lead 10-7 at halftime. First quarter The Cowboys entered the game already down a man. CB Joey Porter Jr. was ruled out with an illness and was sent home from the facility. Cowboys ball The Cowboys started with the ball and got a decent return. George Pickens converted a third down, then Javonte Williams hit a big run behind Tyler Smith. Another big play to Pickens put them in the redzone. They capped it after Jake Ferguson created a pass interference call in the end zone with a Williams touchdown run. A very efficient drive helped along with a few penalties. Tyler Smith being back is already making a difference. Bucs ball Bucs QB Jalon Daniels used his legs to convert a third down, then hit Cade Otton for another first down. Otton, on a short pass, converted another third down, putting the Bucs past midfield. A Shemar James coverage sack on third down was undone by a DaRon Bland holding call. Malachi Lawrence forced a holding call after he used an inside move and was closing on the QB. The Cowboys pass rush is causing havoc, but another holding call, this time on Shavon Revel, provided another first down. Dallas was doing well against the run, but couldn’t get off the field. Chris Godwin got involved on a couple of passes moving them into…

title: Keys before kickoff: Cowboys vs Buccaneers Week 5
summary: The 2-2 Dallas Cowboys host the struggling 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers this week. Here are the keys to the game. Win fast or win slow? George Pickens. CeeDee Lamb. Which one do you attempt to remove from the game? Tampa Bay is faced with the impossible task of picking exactly how they’d like to lose […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Tim Heitman-Imagn Images The 2-2 Dallas Cowboys host the struggling 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers this week. Here are the keys to the game. Win fast or win slow? George Pickens. CeeDee Lamb. Which one do you attempt to remove from the game? Tampa Bay is faced with the impossible task of picking exactly how they’d like to lose against one of the league’s most dynamic receiving rooms. Last week, Houston decided to limit big plays with deep zones. But by doing so allowed Dallas to methodically destroy them underneath. CeeDee Lamb exploded for 189 yards on 17 receptions, thriving on the short-medium game. He also scored the game-winning touchdown when the Texans chose to double Jake Ferguson in the endzone instead of the receiver that had already put the offense on his shoulders throughout the day. It’s unlikely that Tampa Bay will play a blanket coverage like we saw the Texans do last Sunday. The Buccaneers currently possess the fourth highest blitz rate on defense, according to Sumer Sports. They also are going to be without defensive backs Antoine Winfield Jr. and Benjamin Morrison. The only viable path towards success for their defense is to pressure Dak Prescott throughout the night. But if they choose to do so by sending extra men on the blitz, they’ll be playing with fire. Prescott is one of the league’s best quarterbacks when blitzed, and he has the weapons on the outside to make defenses pay. Whether Prescott and the offense are able to open the field up for explosive plays will be determined by what kind of defense Tampa Bay rolls out. If the Buccaneers refuse to allow Lamb to beat them underneath, this could be time for George Pickens to make his presence felt. But either way you cut it, Dallas has more than enough ability to win fast on offense or to score on methodical, clock chewing drives versus this defense. Turnover time? The Dallas defense is the only team in the NFL to not record a single interception this season. It’s possible they will not have a clearer path to forcing turnovers this season than they will against the Buccaneers. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels heads to Dallas on a short week for the second start of his career. He’s coming off of a one touchdown, two interception loss against the Packers. The young quarterback demonstrates a quality that has plagued Dallas this season – mobility. It will be key for Dallas to not only rush the passer, but also to contain him and force him to make decisions from inside the pocket. This defense has not demonstrated the ability to do that so far this season, ranking last in rushing yards allowed to opposing quarterbacks. If the Cowboys are able to fluster the rookie, we should expect to see mistakes made, potentially leading to turnovers. If Daniels is allowed to utilize his legs throughout the night, however, this game could end up being closer than many anticipate. Joey Porter Jr. arrives on the scene We’ve yet to see exactly how defensive coordinator Christian Parker will utilize newly acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr. But judging by what we saw in his limited snaps last week, it appears that he will be allowed to thrive in what makes him special – press man coverage. You simply don’t make a big trade for a player to force him into a scheme that won’t utilize his talents. With that in mind, Porter Jr. should be matched up against Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin for much of the night. Egbuka leads the Tampa Bay receiver room in receiving yards through four weeks and has been a highlight machine. Godwin has a remarkable 88.9% reception rate, catching 16 passes on 18 targets. The hope is that Porter Jr. is able to erase the man he’s covering, taking away one of those two options for the rookie quarterback each time he drops back. If that is the case, it should also provide the pass rush extra time to get home, something they’ve rarely accomplished this season. Separation Prevented & On Ball Grade when in single coverage pic.twitter.com/Dvzq5kJeMi — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) October 6, 2026 While Porter Jr. should be able to limit things to his side, Dallas still has to be concerned about the other cornerbacks. DaRon Bland has struggled through four weeks in finishing plays. The veteran cornerback hasn’t necessarily been lost in coverage, he just has not been able to get his hands on the ball to force pass breakups. His separation rating is in line with all-stars Christian Gonzalez and Trent McDuffie. Bland just needs to complete the process and finish plays. This week, against an undrafted rookie free agent quarterback, he’ll have the chance to do exactly that.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys vs Buccaneers: Score predictions for Week 5
summary: Dallas gets a short turnaround after its dramatic 34-30 comeback victory over Houston, but Thursday night brings a very winnable home matchup. Tampa Bay is still searching for its first victory and will again start undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels in place of the injured Baker Mayfield. The Buccaneers’ defense has kept games close, though, so […]
full_text: Dallas gets a short turnaround after its dramatic 34-30 comeback victory over Houston, but Thursday night brings a very winnable home matchup. Tampa Bay is still searching for its first victory and will again start undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels in place of the injured Baker Mayfield. The Buccaneers’ defense has kept games close, though, so Dallas cannot afford another slow start like the one it produced in Houston. When Tampa Bay has the ball Tampa Bay needs to make life as easy as possible for Daniels. In his first NFL start against Green Bay, he threw for only 148 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, but his 55 rushing yards showed how dangerous he can become when plays break down. The Buccaneers also ran for 141 yards as a team, so expect Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell and Daniels to be heavily involved on the ground. That approach makes sense against a Dallas defense that has struggled throughout the opening month and cannot afford to let another mobile quarterback extend drives with his legs. The clearest opportunity for Dallas comes up front. Tampa Bay has allowed 16 sacks through four games and currently owns the NFL’s highest sack rate per passing play. That should be an invitation for Quinnen Williams, Rashan Gary and the rest of a Cowboys pass rush that has produced only four sacks itself. Dallas has been waiting for this group to take over a game, and facing a rookie quarterback behind struggling protection gives them perhaps their best opportunity yet. If Dallas can win early downs and make Daniels throw from obvious passing situations, turnovers could follow. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should continue putting the game in Dak Prescott’s hands. Prescott threw for 335 yards in Houston and repeatedly went back to CeeDee Lamb, who caught 17 passes for 189 yards and the winning touchdown. Lamb now leads the NFL in receptions and receiving yards, and Tampa Bay will have to find a way of slowing him down without leaving George Pickens isolated elsewhere. That is easier said than done, particularly with safety Antoine Winfield Jr. and cornerback Benjamin Morrison both expected to miss this game. Javonte Williams also deserves to remain a central part of the plan after scoring three rushing touchdowns against Houston, but this is not the week to stubbornly force the run. Tampa Bay has been one of the NFL’s better run defenses, so Brian Schottenheimer should use Williams to maintain balance before attacking through the air. Playing at AT&T Stadium also removes most concerns about weather and field conditions, allowing Dallas to play fast on its familiar surface. The formula should be straightforward, protect Prescott, continue feeding Lamb and Pickens, make Tampa Bay’s rookie quarterback chase points and finally give the Cowboys pass rush an opportunity to attack. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Brandon Loree (3-1) As RJ Ochoa said this week: if the Dallas Cowboys are a serious football team, they have no business losing on Thursday night. But doesn’t it just feel like Jaylon Daniels is going to run for 102 yards, given Dallas can’t stop a mobile quarterback, and what do the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have to lose? Their 0-4 and desperate teams do weird things. I still like Dallas’ chances of winning this game, and it should be a fun one, but don’t count out the Bucs, who played better than expected against the Packers. Cowboys win 32-23. Dyllan Rivers (3-1) Dallas has the opportunity this week to face off against an undrafted rookie quarterback in just his second start. If the defense can’t come way with several sacks and forced errors on this struggling Buccaneers team, it’ll be disappointing to say the least. The Cowboys offense continues to roll and George Pickens get heavily involved. I’m uncomfortable with picking a blowout win, but if Dallas isn’t looking ahead at the extended rest, this should be a relatively easy game. Dallas wins 34-24. Tom Ryle (2-2) I’m like Dyllan, but I see it like this: Either the Cowboys win big, or their season will start circling the drain. A narrow win over a plucky opponent won’t cut it, and I refuse to even discuss what a loss would mean. Maybe I’m just not ready to write Dallas off, but I’ll take them 27-9 over Tampa Bay in a game where the foot comes off the gas pedal early. Matt Holleran (3-1) I think this game will be the first time in 2026 we see the Cowboys’ defense come to life. While Tampa still has some quality offensive weapons, quarterback Jalon Daniels, making just his second career start, should present an opportunity for Dallas’ defense to get right. On a short week I see the script flipping and Dallas’ defense being the stars on Thursday night. The Cowboys move to 3-2 in a low-scoring affair. Give me Dallas, 23-16. Mike Poland (2-2) Let’s pit each opposing offense’s stats against each other and see where they rank. Dallas total points scored- 2nd, Tampa Bay- 23rd. Dallas total offensive yards- 9th, Tampa Bay- 31st. Passing yards, Dallas ranks 7th, Tampa 31st. Rush yards, Dallas 14th, Tampa 28th. Third down conversion rate, Dallas 1st, Tampa 24th. And Tampa now have to come into Dallas on a short week with their starting quarterback, safety, cornerback, and rotational defenders expected to miss the game. Yea, give me Dallas taking this one 41-17.
