title: Will Terrance Ferguson pick up where he left off for Rams?
summary: Will Terrance Ferguson be able to make a big impact for the Los Angeles Rams when he comes off of Injured Reserve? The expectation is that Ferguson will be back after his IR time, but will he be back in full force? Or, will Ferguson continue to adjust at the NFL level? Before Ferguson was […]
full_text: Will Terrance Ferguson be able to make a big impact for the Los Angeles Rams when he comes off of Injured Reserve? The expectation is that Ferguson will be back after his IR time, but will he be back in full force? Or, will Ferguson continue to adjust at the NFL level? Before Ferguson was placed on Injured Reserve, he had a bit of the breakout game against the New York Giants with a touchdown reception and some big time catch and runs. He also had a few drops, so you could see the room for improvement. Then, in Week 3, Ferguson was hurt seriously enough that he could not finish for the Los Angeles Rams against the Denver Broncos. He was then placed on a 4-Week Injured Reserve stint. Ferguson has shown the upside of why the Rams drafted him a couple years ago, he also hasn’t dominated in a way that says the Rams really got a “steal” when they selected him. This second-year player’s career and development have been interesting to watch with moments of awe, and moments of seeing why he wasn’t taken at the tippy top of his draft class. The Rams are hoping Ferguson can come back and make a difference. They are likely hoping the same for Myles Garrett too. Hope and reality don’t always mesh, but in this case, they just might for the Rams. Well, that’s the hope. Rams TE Terrance Ferguson will be ‘ready to go’ after 4-week IR stint (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams lost one of their top playmakers in Week 3 when tight end Terrance Ferguson suffered an ankle injury against the Denver Broncos . He was ruled out for Week 4 and subsequently placed on injured reserve , forcing him to miss a minimum of four games. That means the absolute earliest he’ll be able to return is Week 8 when the Rams host the Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Sean McVay gave an encouraging update on Ferguson’s timeline during the “ Coach McVay Show ” Monday, saying he’ll be “ready to go” after four weeks.“ Xavier Smith signs with Rams rival after being cut (ramswire) “The Rams surprisingly cut Smith last Friday after he endured some early-season struggles on special teams, replacing him with Alex Bachman on punt and kickoff returns. The 49ers are banged up at wide receiver, especially after Dante Pettis injured his calf, so Smith could potentially help them on offense. He’s the latest wide receiver to join the 49ers after a stint with the Rams. Demarcus Robinson signed with the 49ers last offseason after the Rams let him walk, and Brandin Cooks signed to their practice squad this season.“ Los Angeles Rams vs. Buffalo Bills: How to watch, listen to and live stream Monday Night Football Week 5 (therams.com) “The Rams and the Bills last met in Week 14 of the 2024 season on Dec. 8, 2024, at SoFi Stadium where the Rams won 44-42. Quarterback Matthew Stafford had 320 passing yards and two touchdowns. Wide receiver Puka Nacua had 162 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown on 12 catches. Running Back Kyren Williams had 87 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns on 29 carries. Defensively, safety Kam Curl, inside linebacker Omar Speights and outside linebacker Byron Young all had four total tackles and defensive end Kobie Turner had one quarterback hit. Kickoff for Monday night’s game at SoFi Stadium is scheduled for 5:15 p.m. pacific time on ESPN and ABC.“ Pro Picks: Rams will edge the Bills on Monday night in potential Super Bowl preview (sports.yahoo) “Buffalo must fix its turnover issues after seven giveaways in the past two games. It’ll be a challenge for the Bills facing a tough Rams defense that’s still missing Myles Garrett. Aaron Donald and cornerback Jaylen Watson could return for this one. Puka Nacua was back last week and had a big day catching passes from Stafford. The Rams are 2 ½-point favorites. They’re just 4-6 against the spread in their past 10 games, but Pro Picks likes the home team in a close one.“ Multiple Doctors Believe Rams WR Puka Nacua Is at Risk of Re-Injury (si.com) “The question becomes whether the rest has allowed the weakness/strain in the affected area of the hip/groin to improve sufficiently to prevent a hernia from developing,” said Florio. “If it ever does, there’s only one way to fix it.” The one way to fix it would be surgery, and the Rams will hope it doesn’t come to that point. A typical recovery from a hernia surgery would be 4-6 weeks and Nacua would almost certainly land on injured reserve if that were to be the case. After resting Nacua for the past two weeks, the Rams are banking on that helping the issue long-term. However, there is some risk with Nacua, especially with his physical style of play. Toward the end of training camp, Nacua was h eld out due to a psoas injury in his groin. Following the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers, Nacua felt discomfort during the following week of practice and didn’t return until last week..“ Bills will wear all-white uniforms against Rams in Week 5 (wgrz) “The Bills announced Wednesday in a newsletter that they will be wearing their all-white uniform when they visit the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5. That game is scheduled to start at 8:15 p.m. Monday. Buffalo has worn its classic uniform — white helmet, blue jersey, white pants — twice this season, most recently during a Week 4 home loss against the New England Patriots. The team also wore its Nickel City uniforms during a Week 3 home win against the Los Angeles Chargers. “ Rams Make History Ahead of Monday Night Showdown With Bills (lasportsreport) “The Los Angeles Rams are set to make history on Monday, October 12th, as they play their fourth prime-time game in the first five games of the season, becoming the first team to do so. Rams primetime schedule The Rams started the season playing the San Francisco 49ers on a Friday in Australia, which was televised on Netflix.“ Howie Long reveals what Sean McVay must do to save Rams’ season (sports.yahoo) “Long said that he was a “bit disappointed last week,” and wants to see more production on third-down situations. “They don’t have a closer on third down, really a real closer — just a guy who throws the fear of God into you,” Long said. “And I think that impacts them.” McVay is only 40 years old but might be one of the most experienced coaches in the NFL, as he’s in the middle of his 10th season coaching in the NFL.“ Sean McVay gives update on 2 linemen who are now eligible to come off IR (ramswire) “Sean McVay shared an update on both players during his appearance on the “Coach McVay Show” Monday, saying that “That’s something that fortunately, we’ve been able to stay healthy up front,” McVay said. “Those are guys that we’re counting on that are going to be big-time depth guys for us. What does that really look like? Anytime you bring somebody back, usually there’s a coinciding move. Now, we’ve had some injuries where sometimes those things have a way of working themselves out, so we’ll look at that and that’s something that I’ll visit with Reggie and our group this week.” Rams Get Bad News About $100 Million Super Bowl Champion (heavy.com) “While it may have already essentially been off the table, the Los Angeles Rams have now officially missed out on another opportunity to reunite with Odell Beckham Jr. At least, in the sense that they can no longer add him on a trial basis via their practice squad. “BREAKING: Odell Beckham Jr. is signing with the #Vikings, per sources,” The Schultz Report’s Jordan Schultz reported on X on October 7. There are noteworthy Rams ties for Beckham in Minnesota.“ Comment of the Day: “I’ve warmed to the Simpson pick, I think he looked good in preseason and he can move when needed. Added mobility, a rarity in recent Rams QBs. Can’t tell for sure until he eventually takes over the QB reigns. Ask yourself though, if you had to pick between Simpson, Manning or Chamblis who would you take?” -LaRams&NyMets Feed Post of the Day:

title: Klint Kubiak’s accountability sound, without action, it’s empty words
summary: The divide between the AFC West-leading Kansas City Chiefs and the Las Vegas Raiders is still there, but the gap appears to be dwindling. Call it the Klint Kubiak Effect. The Silver & Black’s patience in wanting to interview and eventually hire the hotshot offensive-minded 39-year-old as its new head coach is paying dividends early […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The divide between the AFC West-leading Kansas City Chiefs and the Las Vegas Raiders is still there, but the gap appears to be dwindling. Call it the Klint Kubiak Effect. The Silver & Black’s patience in wanting to interview and eventually hire the hotshot offensive-minded 39-year-old as its new head coach is paying dividends early in the team’s 2026 campaign. “Ahead of schedule” is synonymous with this rendition of the Raiders who are in phase one of the rebuild with Kubiak and general manager John Spytek at the helm. Three straight wins gave way to a tough 30-27 defeat at the hands of the visiting Chiefs this past season — hence the lessening competitive gap between the two division foes. Kansas City narrowly escaped Las Vegas and Kubiak’s coaching and decision making played a part in that. To his credit, Kubiak was quick to own up to the shortcomings immediately after the game. “Wish we would’ve won the game but got a lot of really hardworking guys that care about winning and fell short tonight,” the rookie head coach said to begin the postgame press conference. “And obviously, there’s a point there where I took three points off the board, and we were going to be aggressive going into the game. I don’t regret it. I regret not getting it. “And at the end of the game, however, I’ve got to get the play in faster. We had an illegal shift, that’s on the play caller, not getting the play in fast enough.” “I don’t regret it.” Raiders coach Klint Kubiak on his decision making and “We’re going to win” statement at halftime after a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs. 🎥: By @Sean_Zittel pic.twitter.com/E3AGSrFGL9 — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) October 5, 2026 The accountability continued the following day during his media session on Monday. It’s becoming abundantly clear that while Kubiak and his coaching staff have done a marvelous job creating the eighth-ranked offense in points scored (115) and 11th-ranked defense in points allowed (84) through the initial phase of the season, a key element of the Silver & Black attack — the ground game — is lacking. We all knew about Kubiak’s affinity for running the football heading into Year 1 at the helm of the Raiders. And the 119 rushing attempts he’s dialed up ranks as fifth most amongst the 32 teams in the NFL is a testament to that. However, Las Vegas ranks 24th with 372 yards gained on the ground and with only one touchdown, are 28th in that department. And the paltry 3.1 yards per carry average is dead last in the league. Against the Chiefs this past Sunday, the Raiders were limited to 72 yards on 26 carries with starting tailback Ashton Jeanty pacing the team with 15 carries for 58 yards (3.9 yards per carry average) with a long run of 19 yards. Promising rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. garnered nine totes for 18 yards (2.0 yards per carry average) with a long carry of 11 yards. And fullback Connor Heyward finished with two carries for negative four yards. As such, Kubiak was asked about anything particular that stands out about what’s going on with the production — or lack thereof. “Yeah, there is. I put it on myself. I got to do a lot better job of putting us in better position,” Kubiak responded. “We’ve got solid backs, we’ve got a solid offensive line. And myself and the coaching staff, there’s plenty of things we can do better for our players.” “Scheme them up better,” is how Kubiak answered the follow up question looking for specifics on what he feels the team can do to improve the ground game. Again, Kubiak’s accountability is indeed sound. Admitting an issue and taking ownership of it is the first step into solving it. But true accountability requires tangible behavior for change and repair. It fails without action and true accountability is visible in future choices, such as fixing specific problems or change the environment that allowed it to happen. Without it, Kubiak’s words are empty. Can Kubiak make that happen? It’s difficult to say the head coach can’t. What’s wrong with the Raiders run game? pic.twitter.com/8EpocZGjGI — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) October 7, 2026 His team’s turnaround so far and holding a 3-1 overall record heading into Week 5 action. This rendition of the Raiders showed it can overcome in-game adversity and win ball games — that’s a considerable achievement considering prior versions of the Silver & Black routinely folded in the face of pressure. Thus, overachieved these Raiders have indeed done so far. But a defeat was certainly inevitable and how this team rebounds and responds will be intriguing. “We just got done meeting with them. They’re disappointed, and they’re a very mature group that wants to win. So, we’re fixing the corrections,” Kubiak said. “We’re trying to make ourselves better. Whether we win or whether we lose, we’re telling each other the truth and just seeing what we can do to be a better team moving forward.” And we’ll get to see soon if Kubiak continues to be all about that action — shout out to former Raiders running back Marshawn Lynch who frequently used that phrase, by the way — with the team headed East to take on the New England Patriots (2-2) for a 10 a.m. (Pacific Standard Time) Sunday matchup. The host Patriots rank 14th in rushing yards allowed in their four games (416 yards yielded) with the 4.4 yards per carry average ranking 21st. But overall, New England’s defense is sixth in both points allowed (77) and yards yielded (1,175). Which makes for a concerted effort from the Raiders coaching staff to scheme and adjust in-game and the players to execute in-game a must-do this coming Sunday. Kubiak and Co. embark on a grueling slate with the Patriots up first, followed by tilts with: Buffalo Bills (home) , October 18 Los Angeles Rams (home) , October 25 New York Jets (away) , November 1 San Francisco 49ers (away) , November 8 Seattle Seahawks (home) , November 15 Denver Broncos (away) , November 22 Cleveland Browns (away) , November 29 All those contests before a Week 13 bye where Las Vegas can take a true breather. And we’ll know a whole lot more about Kubiak’s accountability and action over that course of time and if the Raiders’ overall record heading into the bye week is reflective of that.

title: Maxx Crosby, Las Vegas Raiders’ pass rush must get to Drake Maye in Week 5 key matchups vs. New England Patriots
summary: It’s only Week 5, but the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and New England Patriots has a lot of early postseason implications on the line. The 3-1 Raiders are coming off a significant loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and head into Sunday as the sixth seed or second Wild Card in the AFC […]
full_text: (Photo by Barry Chin/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images It’s only Week 5, but the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and New England Patriots has a lot of early postseason implications on the line. The 3-1 Raiders are coming off a significant loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and head into Sunday as the sixth seed or second Wild Card in the AFC Playoff standings . Meanwhile, the 2-2 Patriots are coming off a huge win over the Buffalo Bills to hold the seventh seed or third Wild Card spot. For the second week in a row, the stakes are high for Las Vegas, adding importance to the three key matchups below. Raiders’ Pass Rush vs. Maye A year ago, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye finished second in MVP voting and earned a second-team All-Pro bid while leading the NFL in completion percentage ( 72.0% ) and tossing 4,394 yards with 31 touchdowns and eight interceptions. However, it’s been a different story in 2026 so far, as he’s completing just 62.4% of his passes for 854 yards and four touchdowns with seven interceptions (most in the NFL). A big reason for the statistical regression is that the third-year QB has been under pressure more frequently — 37.9% to 44.3%, according to Pro Football Focus — and is handling it worse than last season. PFF gave Maye a 65.2 grade under pressure during the 2025 regular season due to recording a 6.7% “big time throw” rate with just a 3.2% “turnover worthy play” rate. However, the same numbers sit at 36.2, 4.3% and 8.7%, respectively, over the last four weeks. So, it’s going to be important for the Raiders’ defensive line to get after the quarterback, starting with Maxx Crosby. With 25 pressures in four games, Crosby is on pace to log a career-high 106 pressures and post triple digits for just the second time in his career (101 in 2021). He’s also tied for fourth among edge rushers in the metric and ranks ninth with a 19.8% pass-rush win rate, his best percentage since 2021. Of course, Las Vegas will need other players to step up and support its top pass-rusher. The good news is the Silver and Black rank 12th in the NFL with a 37.9% pressure rate as a team while blitzing just 21.9% of the time (eighth-lowest) per Next Gen Stats . That’s a nod to defensive coordinator Rob Leonard, who has found creative ways to get pressure with just four rushers. Additionally, Malcolm Koonce is somewhat quietly having a good season. He has half as many pressures (12) as Crosby but has also rushed the passer 57 fewer times (136 to 79) and has a nearly identical win rate (18.9%), per PFF . The latter puts Koonce as the 11th-most successful edge rusher across the league (minimum 37 pass rushes). Circling back to Maye, he is coming off his best game of the season with 269 yards and three touchdowns to one interception against the Bills. A big reason for that is he handled pressure much better. Buffalo got to him on 47.6% of his dropbacks, but the 2025 MVP candidate had two “big-time throws” on 15 attempts (13.3%) under pressure and just one “turnover-worthy play” (4.5%), per PFF . So, Sunday will be a true test to see if Maye has turned the corner, as Crosby, Koonce and Leonard await. Mayer vs. Robert Spillane While Brock Bowers is the primary focus of the Raiders’ offense and typically draws opponents’ top cornerback, especially when a corner of Christian Gonzalez’s caliber is on the other sideline, Gonzalez didn’t play last week with a shoulder injury. His status for this Sunday is unknown at the time of writing, taking the air out of that one-on-one battle. Assuming Gonzalez isn’t available again, New England will likely turn to a committee approach when it comes to slowing down Bowers. To the Pats’ credit, they’ve been very stingy against tight ends so far this season, giving up just 104 yards over four games and have yet to yield a touchdown to the position, per StatMuse . The Bills’ duo (Dawson Knox and Dalton Kincaid) combined for just three catches and 20 yards last week. To be fair, Knox hasn’t been very productive this season. However, Kincaid came into the game leading all tight ends with 263 receiving yards , and was held to just one catch for seven yards against the Patriots. Former Raider linebacker Robert Spillane is part of the reason for New England’s success against tight ends, allowing just one catch for five yards to the position on the campaign, per PFF . Spillane isn’t the most dynamic athlete in space to prevent many completions, as he is yielding an 84.6% completion percentage (mostly against running backs and wide receivers) and hasn’t forced an incompletion yet this season. But he is good at rallying and tackling to make stops in coverage, recording five in four weeks without logging a missed tackle. That makes the linebacker good at limiting yards against checkdowns, which is where Raiders tight end Michael Mayer does most of his damage. All 20 of Mayer’s catches and his 167 yards this season have come either behind the line of scrimmage or in the zero-to-nine-yard range, per PFF . Additionally, his 91 yards after the catch are the 10th-most among tight ends, and his 12 first-down receptions are tied for third, proving to be a valuable safety net for quarterback Kirk Cousins. Additionally, the fourth-year pro is coming off one of the best games of his career with eight catches for 82 yards and five first downs. So, New England can’t spend too much of its attention on stopping Bowers because Las Vegas’ other tight end can hurt its defense on underneath routes. On top of all that, Spillane is traditionally known for what he brings as a run defender. He’s currently tied for 15th among linebackers in defensive stops (eight) and has a 2.8-yard average depth of tackle against the run, according to PFF . Meanwhile, Mayer is 17th at his position with a 66.1 PFF run-blocking grade . That sets up for a very intriguing battle in both phases of the game. Raiders’ OTs vs. Patriots EDGEs New England has been without its top two sack leaders from last year’s Super Bowl run — Harold Landry III ( 8.5 ) and K’Lavon Chaisson (7.5) — to begin the current campaign. Chaisson signed with the Washington Commanders in free agency, while Landry has been on the PUP list and doesn’t have a timeline to return. However, the defense is still getting good production from its edge rushers. Dre’Mont Jones was brought in during the offseason and has 12 pressures on 64 pass-rush reps in three games, per PFF (he missed the Week 3 bout with a shoulder injury). That’s incredibly efficient, and Jones’ 23.3% pass-rush win rate is second-best among edge-rushers. Meanwhile, the Patriots also have a pair of young edges who have stood out. Second-year pro Elijah Ponder leads the team with 2.5 sacks and has 13 pressures on 101 pass rushes in four games, and rookie second-round pick Gabe Jacas is second with 1.5 sacks and has 10 pressures on 88 rushes over the last month. Additionally, Jacas has been more efficient every week, highlighted by registering three pressures on just 14 opportunities in Buffalo. All three defenders will spend a good amount of snaps on both sides of the offensive line, adding extra importance to both Kolton Miller’s and DJ Glaze’s performances on Sunday. Miller is coming off a rough outing where he allowed six pressures to the Kansas City Chiefs and struggled to handle George Karlaftis’ ability to win with power. However, there’s reason to believe the nine-year veteran can bounce back quickly since he’s built a reputation as a quality blind-side protector and yielded just five pressures in the three weeks prior to the Chiefs game. Meanwhile, Glaze might be the most improved offensive tackle in the NFL so far this season. He went from giving up the second-most pressures ( 48 ) at the position in 2025 to the 10th-fewest ( four , minimum 49 pass-blocking snaps) during the first month of the 2026 campaign. That sets the stage for a noteworthy battle on the edges of the trenches.

title: Could Chris Goodwin be a fit for Raiders?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders continue to be connected to potential trade fits at the wide receiver position. One name to keep an eye on Chris Godwin of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. They are 0-4 and could be open to trading their longtime standout. If so, the Raiders could be among the team to show interest. […]
full_text: (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders continue to be connected to potential trade fits at the wide receiver position. One name to keep an eye on Chris Godwin of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. They are 0-4 and could be open to trading their longtime standout. If so, the Raiders could be among the team to show interest. Las Vegas general manager John Spytek was in Tampa Bay with Godwin for eight seasons. Plus, Raiders’ minority owner Tom Brady lauded Godwin as a teammate with the Buccaneers. So, a Raiders’ pursuit could make sense. Goodwin is 30 and he has 16 catches for 142 yards in four games this season. He has dealt with injuries recently as he missed a total of 18 games the past two seasons. He had three straight 1,000-plus receiving yards season and had, at least, 83 catches a season spanning 2021-23. While he is getting older, Godwin would give the Raiders a needed veteran presence at wide receiver. Of course, he wouldn’t be a long-term answer, but he would give them needed immediate help. The truth is no wide receiver who could be available before the November 10 trade deadline will be a long-term answer as a No. 1 receiver. So, Godwin could be a solid answer for the this and next season for the Raiders and he likely wouldn’t come at a steep asking price. The biggest issue for the Raiders to acquire Godwin would be his contract. He is in the second of a three-year, $66 million contract. The Raiders would likely need to restructure the contract as part of the deal. So, while this fit may not be perfect, it could be something Spytek looks into in the next month.

title: Dolphins could see defensive reinforcements arriving soon
summary: The Miami Dolphins are the youngest team in the league and they are relying on rookies and second-year players all across the roster. They could see the benefit of the experience gained this year in the future, but they could also be establishing bad habits and failing to learn lessons without veterans in key positions […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 21: Kenneth Grant #90 of the Miami Dolphins is introduced prior to a game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on December 21, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are the youngest team in the league and they are relying on rookies and second-year players all across the roster. They could see the benefit of the experience gained this year in the future, but they could also be establishing bad habits and failing to learn lessons without veterans in key positions on the field. Miami might see some reinforcements returning to the field soon as injured players begin practicing. Last week, the team opened the practice window for cornerback Storm Duck, giving him 21 days to be activated from the Physically Unable to Perform list. Duck sustained a knee injury last year and has had nearly a full year of recovery and rehabilitation to make it to this point. He ended last week as a full participant in practice. Miami also opened the practice window for defensive tackle Kenneth Grant this week. Grant was placed on Injured Reserve as part of the Dolphins’ final roster cuts at the end of the preseason, with the designated to return label applied. Now he begins to work himself into game shape from a toe injury, with the potential that he could return to the roster as early as this weekend. Duck was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice while Grant was limited. Head coach Jeff Hafley was asked on Wednesday about the possibility of Grant playing on Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals. While he did not confirm the defensive tackle would be on the field in Week 5, he also left open the possibility. “I’m excited to see him go through individual, watch him practice. Again, I just think let’s just watch today and see how he does and we’ll progress from there,” Hafley stated. “But he’s attacked his rehab. He’s been such a positive guy and I’m excited that he’s able to come back out for him.” Hafley was also asked about the flexibility a return of Grant could mean for the defensive line. He explained, “Without getting too specific for obvious reasons, it allows us to move some pieces around to help us in some certain situations, whether it’s move other people to other positions on certain downs based on personnel. It just gives us more flexibility, more versatility, and it gives us another good player.” If both players were to return for Sunday’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals, the Dolphins would have to make additional roster moves to create space under the league’s 53-man in-season roster limit. Miami currently has only 52 players on the roster, giving them space for one activation. The presence of one or both of the veteran players could solidify a defense that has been improving over the first four weeks of the season, but could still use some stabilization. The younger players are correcting their mistakes, but if Miami wants to pull off an upset in over the Bengals, adding some experience to the group could go a long way. The Dolphins could also choose to slow their returns, opting to have them sit out this weekend’s schedule, then use Week 6’s bye to further focus on their preparation for a return. Miami visits the New York Jets in Week 7.

title: Miami Dolphins Review: 5 Things I Think I Think After Week 4
summary: Sure, the Miami Dolphins fell to 0-4 on Sunday with a 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. But man, they went into one of the league’s toughest environments and held their own. Here are five things I think I think after Week 4. The kids are growing up fast. There’s young, and then there’s 2026 […]
full_text: Sure, the Miami Dolphins fell to 0-4 on Sunday with a 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. But man, they went into one of the league’s toughest environments and held their own. Here are five things I think I think after Week 4. The kids are growing up fast. There’s young, and then there’s 2026 Dolphins young. Take a look at some of the snap counts from Week 4: Kadyn Proctor: 39/39 snaps Chris Bell: 32/39 snaps Kevin Coleman Jr.: 20/39 snaps Will Kacmarek: 24/39 snaps Jacob Rodriguez: 78/78 snaps Chris Johnson: 78/78 snaps Michael Taaffe: 78/78 snaps That’s seven rookies of a 13-player class either starting or getting meaningful snaps. (And that’s excluding the team’s arguably No. 1 receiver Caleb Douglas, who’s nursing an ankle injury, as well as fourth-round linebackers Kyle Louis and Trey Moore on the injured list.) More importantly, the rookies didn’t look overwhelmed. With 18 tackles, Jacob Rodriguez may have played his best game as a Dolphin . Michael Taaffe and Chris Johnson were solid on a defense that gave up just 15 points to an undefeated Vikings team. Wins be damned, it’s fun to have a team this young play this well. The Dolphins may be building their identity on defense. Coming into the season, most of the attention was on the offense. The big investment in quarterback Malik Willis. Replacing big-time receivers Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle with a trio of high-potential rookies. Bolstering the offensive line and tight end room. Yet four games in, the defense is starting to define this team. The Dolphins finally got to the quarterback, generating four sacks against Minnesota and consistently pressuring Kyler Murray. Chop Robinson delivered his most disruptive performance of the season with a sack and 10 pressures. Zach Sieler looked like the Zach Sieler Dolphins fans have come to expect. Joshua Uche continued his recent surge, and Malik Herring keeps finding ways to make himself noticed. And small sample size, but they’ve only allowed 19.5 points on average over the past two weeks. For the first time this season, you can start to see what this defense wants to become: fast and aggressive. And with Kenny Grant plus Louis and Moore coming back, it might only get more disruptive. We’re losing the hidden yardage game. Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: Opening drive: The Vikings run back the opening kick 47 yards to their 48-yard line. First quarter: After a failed Dolphins’ drive, the Vikings return the ensuing punt 36 yards to the Dolphins’ 38. Second quarter: Malik Willis sacked and fumbled at the Dolphins’ 39, and the Vikings recover at midfield. The Vikings consistently started drives with shorter fields, while Miami’s offense repeatedly had to work its way out of its own territory. In a defensive slugfest where every first down felt significant, those hidden yards became a major factor. I’m not especially worried about Malik Willis … but his lack of production is annoying. The box score is ugly: Less than 100 passing yards usually tells a pretty straightforward story. That said, Brian Flores’ Vikings defense has made plenty of capable quarterbacks look uncomfortable. The Buccaneers passed only for 186 yards in Week 3, and the Bears for only 163 yards in Week 2. And Baker Mayfield and Caleb Williams have a lot more experience under center than Malik Willis. Just the same, the quarterback has not made the same kind of progress that other positions have. The Dolphins are averaging only 163.5 passing yards, the third fewest in the NFL. They’re last in the league in completions and completion percentage, and have thrown only a single touchdown pass. And the team isn’t calling up as many designed runs for Willis – the Vikings game was the second in which Willis had only two rushing attempts. There’s no Achane, of course, and building chemistry with rookie receivers will take time, especially when your top wideout is injured. Still, I’ll be eager to see what this team looks like when its offense has hit its stride. The schedule may hide this team’s progress for a while. The Dolphins entered the season facing one of the league’s hardest schedules, and it’s likely they will be underdogs in every game the rest of the year. That’s fine. But the way this team is growing, especially on defense, and the way it’s competing into the fourth quarter on the road against quality opponents, I think this team will ultimately be better than its record might indicate. There’s still a lot of development that needs to happen, but the amount of growth they’ve already shown is exciting.

title: Miami Dolphins news: Veterans stepping up, Kenneth Grant practices, and more
summary: The Miami Dolphins are the league’s youngest team, fielding a roster full of rookies and second-year players trying to quickly adapt to the speed of the game and the demands of the professional level. They face a steep learning curve as they try to minimize rookie mistakes and learn from the ones they make. The […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler (92) sacks Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) during the first half of the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are the league’s youngest team, fielding a roster full of rookies and second-year players trying to quickly adapt to the speed of the game and the demands of the professional level. They face a steep learning curve as they try to minimize rookie mistakes and learn from the ones they make. The team needs their veteran players to step up and carry the weight of the franchise while the younger players work to reach their potential. Against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4, that is exactly what happened on defense. Suddenly, the Dolphins’ pass rush was disruptive, led by defensive tackle Zach Sieler and edge rushers Chop Robinson and Josh Uche. Sieler recorded two sacks during the game, Uche added another, and Robinson dominated with 10 pressures and a sack on Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray. Those are the performances the Dolphins need from their experienced players. Miami Herald writer Omar Kelly took a closer look at the performances from the veterans and stressed the importance of getting top-tier performances from all their veteran players: We have seen plenty of development from the Dolphins’ first- and second-year players, which is what this 2026 season is about considering the scorched-earth rebuild the franchise began this past offseason. Just imagine what this team could look like, how it might perform, if the Dolphins veterans got their act together… Mistakes happen in football, especially when a team’s adjusting to a new coaching staff, new technique, hasn’t carved out an identity yet, and is working toward creating culture. But the players that should be setting the standard are the veterans… The Dolphins need more from the team’s mature players if the 2026 team plans to produce a win in the second quarter of the season, which is filled with winnable games considering Miami’s next four opponents — the Bengals, New York Jets on the road, and New England and Detroit at home — all struggled in the first quarter of the season. full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 05: Chris Olave #12 of the New Orleans Saints runs after a catch against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on October 5, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings and New Orleans Saints released their second injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at Caesar’s Superdome in New Orleans. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jordan Mason* RB Thumb DNP DNP IR-OUT Jordan Addison* WR Hamstring DNP LP Christian Darrisaw* LT Concussion DNP DNP Charles Demmings CB Hamstring DNP LP Justin Jefferson* WR Ankle LP LP Aaron Jones* RB NIR-Rest LP — Brian O’Neill* RT Knee LP LP Michael Jurgens C Elbow FP FP Brett Thorson* P Hamstring FP FP Ben Yurosek TE Ankle FP FP New Orleans Saints Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Kelvin Banks* OT Ankle DNP DNP IR-OUT Bryan Bresee* DT Knee DNP DNP IR-OUT Travis Etienne* RB Hamstring DNP DNP IR-OUT Julian Blackmon* S Shoulder LP LP Barion Brown WR Thigh DNP LP Kaden Eliss LB Calf DNP DNP Noah Fant TE Abdomen LP LP Jaylan Ford LB Ankle FP FP Davon Godchaux* DT Groin/NIR- Rest FP DNP Carl Granderson LB Ankle LP LP Anfernee Jennings LB Knee DNP DNP Alvin Kamara* RB Back DNP LP Chris Olave* WR NIR-Rest/Foot DNP LP Mike Reid S Ankle LP FP Tyler Shough* QB Left Hand LP FP Lorenzo Styles CB Calf FP FP Jeremiah Wright G Concussion — LP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, Jordan Addison being upgraded to a limited participant in practice on Thursday is a good sign for his availability on Sunday. His injury is thought to be minor. Justin Jefferson continues to be limited in practice and he said yesterday that the plan is for him to play on Sunday but he will take it day to day. It doesn’t sound like his ankle is bothering him anymore but I wouldn’t expect him to play on Sunday unless he has a full practice beforehand. We’ll see what happens tomorrow. Christian Darrisaw is in concussion protocol and missing another day of practice makes it less likely he’ll play on Sunday. I’d be surprised if he played at this point. Charles Demmings being upgraded to limited means he has a shot to be active on Sunday as well. Kevin O’Connell said he expects Brett Thorson to return as punter/holder for the Saints game and his full status for Wednesday’s and now Thursday’s practice would seem to confirm that. The Vikings also released Johnny Hekker from the practice squad, which is another indication that Thorson will be back on Sunday. Michael Jurgens and Ben Yurosek had their 21-day windows to return from injured reserve opened on Wednesday and the fact that both were full participants in practice is a good sign. However, whether they will be activated for Sunday’s game or not make come down to other roster considerations. Lastly, Brian O’Neill is dealing with what appears to be a minor knee injury he is likely to play through. For the Saints, Alvin Kamara being upgraded to limited means he’s on track to play on Sunday. Lorenzo Styles and Jaylan Ford have been designated to return from IR and have their 21-day window opened, but unclear at this point whether they will be activated for Sunday’s game or not. Saints starting QB Tyler Sough being upgraded to full participant also means he’s on track to play Sunday as expected. The one downgrade worth monitoring is to Chris Olave, their best receiver, who was limited with a foot injury. My guess is that he’ll play on Sunday but that could be an injury that limits him on the field. The Saints also have three starters on IR which hurts. Other than that, there is a long list but probably not of great consequence for Sunday’s game. We’ll have the final report and injury designations on Friday. Stay tuned. title: Five Good Questions with Canal Street Chronicles
summary: We haven’t done these all that frequently this season, but this week we got another opportunity to exchange Five Good Questions with the SB Nation site that covers the Minnesota Vikings’ opponent for this week. Yours truly swapped some questions with Nic Jennings of Canal Street Chronicles, SB Nation’s home for everything relating to the […]
full_text: We haven’t done these all that frequently this season, but this week we got another opportunity to exchange Five Good Questions with the SB Nation site that covers the Minnesota Vikings’ opponent for this week. Yours truly swapped some questions with Nic Jennings of Canal Street Chronicles, SB Nation’s home for everything relating to the New Orleans Saints. Once they post my answers to the questions that Nic sent me, I’ll put them up on our page and link them here. For now, here are the questions that I sent over to Nic along with his answers. 1) A year after all four teams in the division finished under .500, it looks like the NFC South could potentially be messy again this year. Nobody is better than 2-2 after the first four weeks, and with a couple of bounces, the Saints could just as easily be looking at a 3-1 mark rather than 1-3. How optimistic are you about the Saints at the quarter pole of this 2026 season? I’m still pretty optimistic about the Saints. I don’t think they’ve lost morale at all, especially because, like you said, they could very easily be 3-1 right now. There have definitely been bright spots, but there have also been some things that need to be cleaned up. The biggest thing for me is they have to find a way to start games faster. If they want to turn this thing around, they can’t keep putting themselves in holes and expecting to fight their way out of them. They also need to clean up the penalties, establish a run game and be more disciplined on the defensive side of the ball. There are still plenty of winnable games left on the schedule, and the NFC South is wide open. I don’t think this season is anywhere close to over. The Saints just have to start playing more consistent football and take advantage of the opportunities they have in front of them. 2) Early last season, the Saints turned to young Tyler Shough at quarterback. Through the first few weeks of this season, he’s put up some very impressive numbers. Do Saints fans really feel that he’s the long-term answer at quarterback in New Orleans? Absolutely. Tyler Shough is the real deal and his teammates rally behind him. He’s been one of the three consistent bright spots for the Saints this season, along with Chris Olave and Chase Young. Shough showed a lot of promise in his limited starts as a rookie, then attacked the offseason and blew expectations out of the water. He’s carried that same momentum into this season. His ball placement, ability to stretch the field with his arm, poise in the pocket and ability to extend plays with his legs give the Saints a dimension offensively that they haven’t really had. And most importantly, he has that clutch gene. He’s shown he can make plays when the Saints need them most. I do think there are still things he can improve on. The offense has developed a habit of starting slowly, and while I’d put more of that on Kellen Moore, Shough still plays a role in getting the offense into a rhythm. But overall, I’ve seen more than enough to believe he can be the long-term answer in New Orleans. 3) For as solid as the Saints’ offense has been, the defense has been. . .not so good, as through the first four weeks they’ve given up more points than any team in the NFL. Given that the Vikings have only scored one offensive touchdown in the last three weeks, what do you think they can do to attack this New Orleans defense effectively? The Vikings need to lean on the run game and get T.J. Hockenson heavily involved. The Saints have not been able to stop the run for the life of them, and the interior of the defensive line has been a major weak point. If Minnesota can establish the run early, I think that could open up some things in the passing game. As for Hockenson, the Saints have consistently had trouble defending vertical-threat tight ends. We saw it in Week 3 when Brock Bowers torched them, and after Hockenson’s big game against Miami last week, there’s no reason to think he can’t do the same thing against New Orleans. I’d expect Minnesota to test that matchup early and often. 4) Give us one “under the radar” player for the Saints who you feel will play a role in any success that they’ll have against the Vikings on Sunday. It has to be Devaughn Vele. After the Saints invested a fourth-round pick in him last year to pry him away from Denver, Vele has come in and become the contested-catch slot receiver the Saints have been searching for since Michael Thomas. He’s quickly become one of Tyler Shough’s favorite targets and has become the go-to guy on third-and-long situations. He and Juwan Johnson have also been quite lethal in the red zone. Vele is a guy I expect to keep garnering more and more attention as the season progresses. For a six-foot-foot receiver to be able to move the way he does and have that type of body control, it’s truly remarkable. 5) How do you see this one playing out? Will the Saints’ offense be able to solve a Vikings’ defense that has terrorized every offense they’ve seen so far this season, or will someone break through in the pillow fight between the Saints’ defense and the Vikings’ offense? The Saints are eager to get the sour taste out of their mouth after Monday night’s beatdown. I think if the defense comes out like it did in the first two weeks and New Orleans can establish its own run game, they have a chance to come out strong and give the Vikings their first loss. If they want any chance of winning this game, however, they have to start fast. They can’t afford to dig themselves into another early hole and expect to fight their way back. Thanks again to Nic for taking the time to answer my questions for this week!

title: Patriots mailbag: Will injuries force an addition at wide receiver?
summary: The New England Patriots are looking to build off of their big win against the Buffalo Bills, and now return home for a matchup against the surprising 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. Hey Brian. Do you think there’s a move made at wide receiver if the team gets […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are looking to build off of their big win against the Buffalo Bills, and now return home for a matchup against the surprising 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. Hey Brian. Do you think there’s a move made at wide receiver if the team gets grim news on Hollins, or do you think they just elevate one of the practice squad guys? – Pat in Agawam With Hollins’ injury not considered long term and the return of A.J. Brown looming, I don’t think an outside addition is needed. If they believed otherwise, that addition would have been in the building early this week. The Patriots can continue to primarily run Romeo Doubs at the X, Efton Chism at the Z in place of Mack Hollins, and DeMario Douglas in the slot with Kyle Williams working in at multiple spots as well. That should be enough to get by in the mean time, with Cameron Dorner or Kyle Dixon potential practice squad elevation options if spots are available. Via chats with other Pulpiteers, I’m curious, what’s up with Kyle Williams lack of “production?” Is he seeing the field? Is he being used primarily as a “Sacrificial X” WR to clear out safety help and open the field for others? Is he doing his job in respects beyond catching the ball?—running good routes, blocking etc. Or, does he just suck? I believe Vrabel and McD have said in the past that doing your job doesn’t always mean you are the guy who gets targeted with the ball, and I’m wondering if that might be the case with Kyle. – Maye The Force Be With You Is there a future for our WR Williams ? With now Chism emerging, Doubs starting to catch and Douglas established in the slot we can imagine Brown and Hollins will come back so Williams could be the odd man Non active on game day …. – 7i165 The effort is not an issue for Kyle Williams. He’s running hard routes, blocking in the run, and continuing to earn praise from the coaching staff behind the scenes. His role simply leads to volatile production, as he’s mainly playing outside in a sacrificial X role, where he’s often running clear-out routes. I did think his third-down catch against Pittsburgh over the middle of the field was a big play, as he fought through contact to convert. At the same time, it’s been disappointing that Drake Maye has not been able to get him the football on two specific instances when he won deep along the outside: the blood-fumble play and a second-down incompletion late against Buffalo. The skill set is still valuable in this wide receiver room, and I would still be in favor of Williams working at different positions and running a more diverse route tree like he did in college. But with the veterans ahead of him, those opportunities simply haven’t presented themselves. He should get more of them this Sunday, however. Why did it take so long to get around to Efton Chism? All we’ve been hearing about is how good this guy is how hard he plays he could become the next Julian Edelman,who wasn’t used much his first couple of years.. he needs to be out there going forward. What’s your take? – PatriotsWay We’re not comparing him to Julian Edelman or any other former Patriots slot receiver, but frequent readers here know we’ve been a fan of Chism since before the draft. While he’s dominated virtually every practice we’ve watched since his arrival, he was an undrafted free agent joining a depth chart that included veterans such as Stefon Diggs, Mack Hollins, and DeMario Douglas. Like Williams, Chism needed an opportunity. He got one late last season and then again Sunday, and he impressed both times. Now, we’d expect to see more of him moving forward. The Right Guard position continues to be a mess. Brown was bad against Buffalo. I believe between Lomu, Bryant, and Crownover one of those could be a better RG than they have on the roster. Will those guys get a shot at that position or does the team view them strictly as Tackles. – Elderly Lothario Ben Brown will be “slated to start at right guard” this week, according to Mike Vrabel. Brown did allow three pressures, failing to pickup a stunt and got pushed back on the strip sack (in part due to an uncalled hands to the face penalty) but was certainly not a train wreck in his first meaningful NFL reps at right guard. I’d continue to roll with Brown. Mike Vrabel has not ruled out Lomu potentially factoring into he mix at some point, but the rookie appears to be behind newly signed Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse at the position. Moses shocked me by having a pretty good pass protection grade but his run blockjng grade is horrible. Do you think he gets replaced at some point by Lomu? – XGhost-PepperX It was definitely a bounce back game for Moses in Buffalo, who allowed one tackle for loss in the run game and just one pressure while drawing the most matchups against Gregory Rousseau. The veteran is battling through a painful foot injury, but don’t think the team has any immediate plans to pull the plug for Caleb Lomu, who did not look ready in a limited sample size against the Jaguars. When is our 2025 Sack Leader Harold Landry expected to make his return? Getting him back as a Pass Rusher and Run Stuffer will help this Defense. – For Pats Sake I haven’t had any expectations for Harold Landry this season after what he played through last season. Anything they get from him would be a bonus in my book, and I’m not sure how impactful he would even be following that knee injury. Considering that the Pats no longer have a 2028 1st round pick, would you target the OL again in the next draft or look at other potentially weak areas like TE, LB? – Arschloch Certainly can never have enough offensive lineman, but with two straight first-round picks invested in Will Campbell and Caleb Lomu I would not use another first on an offensive tackle. I’m also largely against using that capital on an interior offensive lineman. I would still look at some position in the defensive front seven. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

title: Patriots vs. Raiders weather forecast for NFL Week 5
summary: Last year’s meeting between the New England Patriots and the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium was a wet affair. full_text: Last year’s meeting between the New England Patriots and the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium was a wet affair. There is a chance this week’s game between the two clubs is as well, but it does not seem particularly likely. According to NFL Weather , there is a “slight chance of rain showers” throughout the contest on Sunday. That chance, however, has been calculated at a minuscule 2%. More likely, the game will be played under consistent cloud cover and with temperatures in the low 60s; wind should not be a major factor despite gusts of up to 15 mph being possible. The National Weather Service shares a similar projection. According to its models, Sunday will be “mostly cloudy, with a high near 64” and rain showers only expected to happen after 7 p.m. ET. Long story short, as far as October football is concerned those are pretty standard conditions that should not negatively impact the game. For the Patriots, who have struggled with ball security and will be going up against the league leaders in takeaways this week, this can be seen as positive news. The Week 5 game between the Patriots and Raiders at Foxborough’s Gillette Stadium is scheduled for Sunday, Oct. 11 at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots offense looking for consistency after finding its stride in Buffalo
summary: The New England Patriots offense took a major step forward last Sunday in Buffalo. The unit looked different, scoring a season-high 29 points as the four touchdowns it scored doubled the amount they previously had through the first three weeks. According to offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, however, not much changed. “I just think staying consistent. […]
full_text: The New England Patriots offense took a major step forward last Sunday in Buffalo. The unit looked different, scoring a season-high 29 points as the four touchdowns it scored doubled the amount they previously had through the first three weeks. According to offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, however, not much changed. “I just think staying consistent. I know this is hard to believe, but we didn’t really do a whole lot different from week one to two to three to four,” McDaniels said. “We knew we hadn’t played our best brand of football that we could play. And again, I keep saying this, it’s about the group. The group has to play well in order for us to play well as an offense, and believe it or not, we didn’t, that was far from perfect also, so there was much to improve on that we’re going to work hard to try to make better and hopefully we can do that.” Entering the week last in motion rate and 29th in play-action rate, the Patriots increased both in Buffalo. That included running motion on 75.3% of their plays, their highest rate in a single game since Week 15, 2023. But McDaniels noted that it’s not simply about playing fast. The Patriots have to play fast and execute to see results. The results were there for Drake Maye, who played his best game of the season. Maye threw for a season-high 269 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 yards on the ground. “I think his approach being consistent with the things we’re trying to improve on for himself, but also the group as a whole,” McDaniels said. “There are just so many areas where we can do better and make better decisions, use better techniques and fundamentals and produce more offense. And so hopefully we’ll see that again Sunday.” Maye and the Patriots offense will hope to keep building on that performance Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. It’s the next step toward reaching their full potential as a unit. “I think we’re just starting up the mountain,” Maye said. “I think you would like to think that, and we have to go and prove that, but it’s a race for us to improve, knowing that you have to improve throughout the season and throughout the year for these teams. These teams, once you get closer to the end, are going to be at their best at the end, and I think that’s one of the things that you strive to do throughout the year. “Knowing that, you would like to say everybody – especially on offense – you’d like to say that the first three weeks weren’t what we wanted to put out there. You have to try to build off last week, knowing that it’s not just going to do it for you. You have to put the work in and the focus, and hopefully continue to catch a trend and catch a stride.”

title: What signing Mike Brown to the 53-man roster means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots have started filling the openings on their active roster, and Thursday saw them make the first such move. Safety Mike Brown, who began the regular season on the practice squad, was promoted to the 53-man team. Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots heading into their Week 5 game […]
full_text: The New England Patriots have started filling the openings on their active roster, and Thursday saw them make the first such move. Safety Mike Brown, who began the regular season on the practice squad, was promoted to the 53-man team . Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots heading into their Week 5 game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Deliberate timing Brown entered training camp in a competition will Dell Pettus for the No. 3 spot at the safety position behind Craig Woodson and Kevin Byard, and eventually lost out to the former UDFA. With Pettus on IR and not eligible to come back until after Week 6, however, the team has relied on the veteran to provide depth — first as a standard-elevation from the practice squad and now as an official piece of the roster. This begs the question, why they made the move. Brown only having one elevation left likely played a part in the move: elevating him now that there is some roster flexibility effectively allows the Patriots to keep that elevation in their back pocket should they need it later. But also, Brown is a safety in name only: he is mostly a special teamer, meaning that his promotion says less about the Woodson, Byard, Jaylen Reed and Brenden Schooler’s potential return off NFI. Instead, it is a reflection that the team values his kicking game contributions and sees him as a player whose presence might help free other players up to focus on different areas. Special teams impact Brown’s special teams expertise was on display in both of his games so far this season. He played 86% of available kicking game snaps over the last two weeks and was used in a core-four capacity: he saw action on kickoff return, punt return, kickoff coverage and punt coverage. Among his roles was serving as a personal protector in the punt game, a job he filled over the summer as well. The Patriots were forced to use several PPs this season, with Dell Pettus, Craig Woodson and Jaylen Reed all getting an opportunity over the first two weeks. Since Week 3, however, Brown has been the guy and the expectation is that he will continue to fill that job moving forward. Paired with Brenden Schooler’s impending return, the Patriots effectively bought themselves a long-term influx of quality experience into their kicking game operation. One spot left open, theoretically As noted above, Brown was the first player picked to fill an open spot on the Patriots’ 53-man roster. There is a second such spot, and it seems relatively clear at this point in time who it will be going to: Brenden Schooler, who returned to practice after Week 2 while still on the non-football injury list due to a back issue. Schooler is a full practice participant already, and seems ripe to be brought back either this week or next. The team has until Oct. 14 to return him to its active roster or else he would revert to NFI, ending his season. While other players are now also eligible to return off their respective injury lists — OT Marcus Bryant (IR), ED Harold Landry III (PUP), LB Khalil Jacobs (IR), P Bryce Baringer (IR) — Schooler being the only one out of that group currently practicing is a clear sign of what will happen: the 53rd spot will go to him, probably sooner rather than later.

full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 4: Reggie Gilliam #44 of the New England Patriots warms up prior to the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the New England Patriots headed back to practice, four absences became five. Fullback Reggie Gilliam joined the list of non-participants during Thursday’s work on the Las Vegas Raiders after being limited with ankle and knee injuries to begin the week. Alongside the March signing, wide receiver Mack Hollins and cornerbacks Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis III and Karon Prunty all remained sidelined in Foxborough. Here’s the second injury report ahead of Sunday’s 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Gillette Stadium. DID NOT PARTICIPATE Patriots FB Reggie Gilliam (ankle, knee) WR Mack Hollins (calf) CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) CB Carlton Davis III (neck) CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) Gilliam has played 58 snaps on offense and 39 snaps on special teams since arriving at Gillette Stadium on a three-year deal. The former Buffalo Bills fullback, who was dealing with a knee injury heading into last weekend, suffered an ankle injury in the first half. Announced as questionable , he returned as a lead blocker on a touchdown run. Out wide at Highmark Stadium, Hollins did not . The 33-year-old receiver, ranking atop the passing game in targets, catches and yards, a sustained a non-contact calf injury following intermission and hopped to the sideline on one foot. And then there’s the cornerback room’s Rolodex. Gonzalez had been ruled out due to a shoulder injury prior to the trip to Orchard Park and has now missed five consecutive practices. The extended All-Pro’s absence lingers with company. Back-to-back sidelined sessions have been logged by Davis due to a neck injury and Prunty due to a hamstring injury. While the veteran starter stayed in for all 59 defensive downs in the 29-26 AFC East upset, the No. 171 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft handled 18 downs in the kicking game. That would include the starting running back he helped send from the goal line to the end zone last weekend. Stevenson later limped off with a knee injury on the final drive of the divisional meeting. His outing brought 47 rushing yards, 27 receiving yards, a touchdown and a two-point conversion. He has been present for consecutive practices since then. The Patriots’ partial group continues to include two who did not take the field versus Buffalo. At defensive tackle, Barmore missed three practices in the lead-up due to a shoulder injury before being scratched . And at cornerback, an undrafted rookie in Canada had been downgraded on the eve of the 1 p.m. ET kickoff due to a hamstring injury. Woods and Woodson, who combined for five tackles and an interception last Sunday, are also managing ailments in the shorthanded secondary. New England’s quarterback also rushed for a team-high and season-high 54 yards on the way to being named AFC Offensive Player of the Week The Patriots stand with one open spot on the 53-man roster. summary: The New England Patriots stood with two open roster spots. One remains. The organization announced the promotion of safety Mike Brown from the practice squad on Thursday after the vested veteran served as a back-to-back standard elevation. Brown, 27, reverted as the week began. The 6-foot-1, 218-pound safety has played 12 snaps on defense and […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Mike Brown #33 of the New England Patriots looks on after the preseason game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots stood with two open roster spots. One remains. The organization announced the promotion of safety Mike Brown from the practice squad on Thursday after the vested veteran served as a back-to-back standard elevation. Brown, 27, reverted as the week began. The 6-foot-1, 218-pound safety has played 12 snaps on defense and 42 snaps on special teams through matchups against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills. Notching a pair of tackles this fall in a core role, he tied for the team lead with 88 percent of the workload in the kicking game during his latest call-up. Undrafted in 2022, Brown spent time on the practice squads of the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and Cleveland Browns before joining the Tennessee Titans’ 53-man roster late in his rookie season. The Miami of Ohio product remained in the AFC South until being non-tendered as a restricted free agent in March. He signed in Foxborough as the 2026 league year got underway and was retained on the practice squad after being released during August’s cutdown. Now 37 games into his NFL run, including a handful of starts, Brown has recorded 61 tackles and two passes defensed over the course of 515 snaps on defense and 802 snaps on special teams. He steps into an active safety depth chart that currently includes Kevin Byard III, Craig Woodson and Jaylen Reed. A 2025 special teams captain in Brenden Schooler, who resides on the non-football injury list , is also set to rejoin the group after having his 21-day practice clock start in September. A recent departure returned in a corresponding move on Thursday. The Patriots re-signed outside linebacker Jose Ramirez to the 17-man practice squad after he cleared waivers the afternoon prior. Ramirez, 27, first agreed to terms in Foxborough as the calendar turned to September. A promotion from the practice squad to the 53-man roster followed for the 6-foot-2, 252-pound edge rusher as safety Dell Pettus landed on injured reserve last month. From there, Ramirez appeared in two road matchups. He recorded one solo tackle across 30 snaps between defense and special teams before being waived . Entering the NFL in the sixth round of the 2023 draft at No. 196 overall, Ramirez checked into four games while a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and notched one quarterback hit. The former MAC Defensive Player of the Year by way of Arizona, Riverside City College and Eastern Michigan spent last year with the CFL’s Hamilton Tiger-Cats en route to reaching a futures contract with the Philadelphia Eagles in January. Head coach Mike Vrabel’s 2-2 side hosts the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Kickoff at Gillette Stadium is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots vs. Raiders: Who has the edge in Week 5?
summary: After back-to-back road contests, the New England Patriots return home in Week 5 for what will on paper be a marquee matchup. On the one side, you have the reigning AFC champions, who just improved to 2-2 on the year; on the other side, you have the upstart Las Vegas Raiders and their 3-1 record. […]
full_text: After back-to-back road contests, the New England Patriots return home in Week 5 for what will on paper be a marquee matchup. On the one side, you have the reigning AFC champions, who just improved to 2-2 on the year; on the other side, you have the upstart Las Vegas Raiders and their 3-1 record. Both teams have had stretches of very good play this season, but as our head-to-head comparison shows, we are clearly trusting one of the two over the others. Passing game Patriots pass offense vs. Raiders pass defense: Is Drake Maye back? It sure looked like it last week against the Buffalo Bills. Now, the newly-minted AFC Offensive Player of the Week will go up against one of the toughest challenges he has faced this season: a Raiders pass defense ranked fourth in the league in EPA per dropback (-0.078). From solely that statistical perspective, the visitors should have an edge this week. However, if Maye plays like he did in Week 4 and can keep mistakes at a minimum, and New England stays in manageable down-and-distance situations, he and his receiving corps should be able to put pressure on an opportunistic but somewhat inexperienced secondary. The big question is how the offensive line will hold up versus a ferocious pass rush led by Maxx Crosby, but Maye’s ability to escape a collapsing pocket should still allow him to find success even when pressured. | Edge: Patriots Patriots pass defense vs. Raiders pass offense: Five of the six cornerbacks on the Patriots’ active roster are on the injury report, and neither Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) nor Carlton Davis (neck) were at practice on Wednesday or Thursday. The uncertain state at the position might be putting immense pressure on New England’s pass defense this week. We do feel confident in the team’s outlook if at least one of Gonzalez or Davis two suits up — Buffalo’s Josh Allen did find some success last week, but Kirk Cousins is no Josh Allen despite ranking 10th in the league in EPA per play among quarterbacks (0.214) — but both being out could be problematic. That said, the Raiders offense does not run through its wide receivers and the Patriots did a fantastic job against the Bills’ tight ends last week; a repeat performance would force the Raiders out of their comfort zone regardless of who lines up at CB. | Edge: Patriots Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! Follow every snap and discuss every decision with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Connect through our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Running game Patriots rushing offense vs. Raiders run defense: The uncertainty surrounding Rhamondre Stevenson, who exited Sunday’s game late and is a limited practice participant to start the week due to an ankle injury, puts a question mark over New England’s ability to consistently run the ball against the Raiders. That said, even if he is available this week and at a 100% physically, Las Vegas should have a slight edge in this category. Outside of Drake Maye scrambles, which are pass plays, New England has struggled moving the ball on the ground at consistent rate, which is why the team is ranked only 23rd in EPA per run. Now going up against what is still the sixth-ranked run defense despite giving 177 yards to Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker this past week, it needs improvement across the board. There is little to suggest it will come this week against this particular opponent and considering the circumstances. | Edge: Raiders Patriots run defense vs. Raiders rushing offense: Asthon Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. are a pretty good 1-2 punch at running back, but so far this season Las Vegas has not been able to get consistent production out of them. This could change on Sunday given that the Patriots have had their issues stopping the run. From that perspective, this can be seen as a classic weakness-versus-weakness matchup. Why do we still like New England? Because the Raiders’ problems appear to be more diverse and harder to work around on a week-to-week basis: the blocking has not been up to par, while Jeanty himself does not look entirely comfortable coming off an ankle injury. New England’s main issue has been controlling the interior line, but more reps for DaQuan Jones and getting Christian Barmore back from injury might help fix that. | Edge: Patriots Special teams The Raiders have been pretty good in the kicking game so far, with one player in particular standing out: third-year kickoff returner Dylan Laube, who leads the NFL with 33.4 yards per runback. For as good as Laube has been, he is only the tip of the special teams iceberg: Matt Gay has made all 19 of his combined field goals and extra points so far, Malik Benson is averaging 13.6 yards per punt return, and the kickoff coverage team — going against an uneven Patriots unit in that regard — has also been rock-solid. The only real problem has been covering punts but Marcus Jones has not been getting going in the game’s third phase so far either. | Edge: Raiders Coaching Not only are the Patriots players coming off their most complete collective game of the season, the coaching staff is as well. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels and defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr were both excellent against one of the NFL’s best teams last Sunday. Whether it was the former instilling some life into his unit and much-needed confidence into his quarterback through good play designs and sequencing, or the latter keeping Josh Allen in check while also taking away Buffalo’s two-headed tight end monster of Dalton Kincaid and Dawson, New England’s coaches are entering Week 5 with momentum. The Raiders’ rather inexperienced staff, meanwhile, will have to prove itself coming off its first loss together. | Edge: Patriots Verdict The Raiders are a solid team and have impressed so far under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak. However, even more so than the Patriots they are a work in progress and have yet to show that they can compete against playoff-caliber teams; they couldn’t last week versus Kansas City. Even though the Patriots are dealing with some significant injury questions especially at wide receiver and in the secondary, they seem better equipped overall to find an edge and use it to their advantage.

title: Gabe Jacas keeps eyes forward as big plays start piling up for the Patriots rookie
summary: Former New England Patriots research director Ernie Adams once compared a good football team to a racehorse with its blinders on, not being distracted by anything in its surroundings and remaining focused on what lies ahead. That description also can be applied to one of the current Patriots’ most promising players. Four games into his […]
full_text: Former New England Patriots research director Ernie Adams once compared a good football team to a racehorse with its blinders on, not being distracted by anything in its surroundings and remaining focused on what lies ahead. That description also can be applied to one of the current Patriots’ most promising players. Four games into his NFL career, Gabe Jacas has had his fair share of impactful moments. The second-round draft pick has registered 1.5 sacks, 10 total quarterback pressures, and an interception. But as he keeps putting out highlight-reel plays — including running over Pro Bowl left tackle Dion Dawkins last week versus the Buffalo Bills to force a near-safety — he is making sure not to stray from course. His blinders are staying on. “I feel like a lot of people always like to go back and talk about something I did last week. The main thing for me is just focus on this week ahead,” he said at his Gillette Stadium locker on Wednesday. “No one cares what you did last week. This league will sting upon you if you get comfortable and complacent. That’s not something I want to be, complacent or comfortable. I just want to continue to get better and improve.” Since joining the Patriots, Jacas has done just that. knocked a lineman right over 👀 pic.twitter.com/aJTSyTpiLx — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Arriving as the 55th overall selection out of Illinois this spring, Jacas’ tenure started slowly. He made his lone public appearance in the offseason watching rookie minicamp from the sideline while recovering from hamstring and knee issues. Along the way, contract negotiations also took their time. When he finally signed his deal — a pact that includes multiple protections for the team — training camp was already underway. Jacas did start on the back burner, and even when he did take the field was not particularly convincing. Looking like the rookie he very much was, his preseason tape was rough and he seemed destined for a minor role early in his career. And then, he turned it on and has not looked back since. For the 22-year-old, that development was not surprising; he remained confident in his abilities throughout his ups and downs over the summer. “I always have confidence,” he said. “It’s not just that one play. I’ve always had confidence even coming into this league.” Jacas’ confidence, and by extension his play on the field, has been an asset for the Patriots this season. He and second-year edge Elijah Ponder have been vital to New England’s defensive success in light of both projected starting edges, Harold Landry and Dre’Mont Jones, missing time due to injury. But even as the big plays are piling up, Jacas’ main focus is on how he can ensure they keep coming. “I just continue to improve and that’s what I’m trying to do each week — just improving;” he said. “Not really worried about plays here and there, just improving and try to continue to do what I can to win games for this team.”
