title: Saints draft position: Entering Week 5
summary: Another loss means the New Orleans Saints’ draft position keeps improving, which is at least one positve you can take from Monday. With needs across the roster, moving up will give New Orleans some great options. Here are two of those prospects that the Saints can select at their new draft position, the 7th pick: […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA AUGUST 31: South Carolina linebacker Dylan Stewart (6) reacts during the AFLAC Kickoff Game between the South Carolina Gamecocks and the Virginia Tech Hokies on August 31st, 2025, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Another loss means the New Orleans Saints’ draft position keeps improving, which is at least one positve you can take from Monday. With needs across the roster, moving up will give New Orleans some great options. Here are two of those prospects that the Saints can select at their new draft position, the 7th pick: South Carolina EDGE Dylan Stewart Let’s have the Dylan Stewart conversation. This probably isn’t the best way to introduce the prospect, but we need to address it before we get to what he would bring to the Saints. South Carolina has had a bad season, and the team has suspended Stewart. At times, he yelled at coaches and refused to get off the field. Before the season, this didn’t seem like an issue (though it could have been happening behind closed doors). This team has been a mess, so several factors could have led to the outburst. Because of this suspension, nobody really knows whether Stewart will go to the draft or even get selected in his projected range, but for now, let’s consider him a top-10 pick because that’s his talent. Stewart is one of the most athletic pass rushers in CFB. He is so quick off the line, can go right past offensive tackles, and few players can run away from him. He has clear potential to be the best edge rusher in the NFL, and his floor is solid, too. That should scare people who hear it, but the potential is extremely enticing. For the Saints, the character concerns may take Stewart out of their draft research, but his talent could make the team reconsider. Adding Stewart across from Chase Young would instantly make the Saints’ pass rush 10x better than it was in 2026. Ole Miss DT Will Echoles Sticking with the defensive line, we are going to the interior. Going into the season, Echoles wasn’t expected to be the best DT in the draft, but this season has shown he should at least be considered. Echoles is a game changer in both pass rush and run defense, can use his strenght to push offensive linemen into the QB’s lap, and has a slew of rush moves that allow him to go right past blockers. This is the definition of a top-10 DT, and for the Saints, they need it. Against the Falcons, we saw what this interior looks like right now. Vernon Broughton is a good pass rusher, but can struggle against the run; Davon Godchaux’s time in New Orleans should be over after this season, and they do not have a starter for the other 3-4 DE spot. Hopefully the Saints can start playing Christen Miller in Godchaux’s spot because they need to develop the young DT, and maybe Bryan Bresee can come back healthy and ready, but they need to add a high-level player to this group. Echoles would be a game changer on this defensive line, and if the Saints can’t get a top-tier EDGE in this class, go with the DT, then go with a pass rusher later.

title: Is it time to have the Kellen Moore conversation?
summary: I wanted to start this with one question: What has Kellen Moore done to make you feel good about him as the New Orleans Saints’ head coach? For me, I can think of Tyler Shough’s development, but that could also be attributed to the rest of the staff, or maybe the team chemistry that’s been […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - SEPTEMBER 27: New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore on the field during the second half of a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Caesars Superdome on September 27, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I wanted to start this with one question: What has Kellen Moore done to make you feel good about him as the New Orleans Saints’ head coach? For me, I can think of Tyler Shough’s development, but that could also be attributed to the rest of the staff, or maybe the team chemistry that’s been built. But everything he is supposed to be doing as a head coach has been underwhelming to this point. Let’s just start with Monday’s night game against the Atlanta Falcons and why it exposed everything that has gone wrong so far. The Saints looked unprepared, which is insane to think about with the extra day of preparation; the lack of defensive investment showed; the decision to keep the tackles on an island when your best offensive lineman is out was horrible; not playing CJ Donaldson was confusing, the entire run game makes no sense; the 2025 draft class has taken a step back; and playing your starters at the end of the game was malpractice. It was overall just a bad game, but these coaching issues have been here since Moore was hired. The slow starts have been the most glaring issue with this team. There was one game vs the New York Jets last year, that felt like the Saints were going to win from start to finish. New Orleans is consistently behind in games and sometimes gets lucky at the end to make a comeback. There’s been no evidence yet that this coaching staff can figure out how to start fast, and although I understand Travis Etienne’s injury isn’t helping, they couldn’t do it with him. Sticking with the offense, this group looks excellent on paper, but it still looks all over the place at times. Not utilizing Donaldson, the best blocker in the RB room and potentially the best rusher at this point, to at least help your struggling backup LT makes no sense. On the topic of the run game, there’s absolutely zero reason it should be as bad as it is. With this offensive line, most RBs should have success, or at least some decent runs, but the Saints can’t even get that. It just feels like the Saints are going out there to run the ball, choosing a random play, and seeing what happens. This offseason, New Orleans put nearly all of their effort into making the offense a juggernaut, and the defense was an afterthought. The offense has had some success this season, but not at the level we expected, and the defense has had its moments, but it’s struggling like we thought it would. Offensively, this team should be better, especially with an offensive head coach leading the team, and the lack of investment on defense made little sense for a team that wanted to take that next step forward. Don’t get me wrong, it’s always important for an offense-minded head coach to get the right personnel, but not paying more attention to an unproven defense is why we get games like the one against the Falcons. The Saints can easily turn this season around, and I do like some things Moore has done as a play caller in the passing game, but it’s impossible to not notice that his seat is getting a bit warm. Entering the unknown after letting a head coach go is scary, but the Saints aren’t the same job they were two offseasons ago. New Orleans will be one of the most coveted jobs available if things continue and they part ways with Moore, and top candidates like Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle will be interested. I’m not saying that Moore will be fired, and I still want to mention that he can turn this around, but this loss to the Falcons and any other game to come that are similar to it should at least open the conversation about a new head coach in 2027.

title: NFL Picks Week 5: Celebrating the Past
summary: The New Orleans Saints remain at home to face the Minnesota Vikings, to continue their disappointing season so far. After getting completely embarrassed by Atlanta last Monday Night, the Saints hope to stop the hemorrhaging against the undefeated Vikings. Despite not being a division rival, Minnesota may be the next most hated team for many Saints fans […]
full_text: Dec 25, 2020; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18) is tackled by New Orleans Saints cornerback Marshon Lattimore (23) in the first quarter at the Mercedes-Benz Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Chuck Cook-USA TODAY Sports The New Orleans Saints remain at home to face the Minnesota Vikings, to continue their disappointing season so far. After getting completely embarrassed by Atlanta last Monday Night, the Saints hope to stop the hemorrhaging against the undefeated Vikings. Despite not being a division rival, Minnesota may be the next most hated team for many Saints fans outside of the NFC South. Following the Falcons march through the city, New Orleans simply doesn’t need the Vikings to do the same. Once again, the Saints will celebrate the past in the midst of lamenting the present. Drew Brees, who will be in the booth to call the game, will also be honored at halftime, the Hall of Famer’s second-consecutive game in attendance. The fans will have another opportunity to honor what came before, while wishing those times never had to pass. The Saints as an organization desperately needs to find a way to keep the fans and the region invested in the current-day franchise without leaning on days long past. That opportunity starts now, with another hated team coming into New Orleans. Win, and the chance to reinvigorate the fanbase grows larger. Lose, and the chance to lose the fanbase grows larger as well. Let’s take a look at this and every matchup in Week 5. Last week I went 9-7 I told you so: Panthers over Lions! What do I know: Saints over Falcons? *** WEEK 5 Thursday, October 8th – Thursday Night Football Buccaneers(0-4) at Cowboys(2-2) Dallas’ roller coaster season will finally give them a break against the beleaguered Bucs. Dallas wins 35-20. Pick: Cowboys *** Sunday, October 11th – Very Early Game Eagles(2-2) at* Jaguars(3-1) – London, England This tight contest will come down to a late field goal by Philly on the final play. Philadelphia wins 27-25. Pick: Eagles *** Sunday, October 11th – Early Games Bengals(2-2) at Dolphins(0-4) Cincy gets themselves back on track against the lowly Dolphins in Miami. Cincinnati wins 35-17. Pick: Bengals *** Raiders(3-1) at Patriots(2-2) This will be a tight contest throughout, but trailing by a point, Klint Kubiak schemes a touchdown to win the game in the closing moments. Las Vegas wins 23-17. Pick: Raiders *** Browns(3-1) at Jets(1-3) This will be a far more entertaining game than the names attached to it would suggest. Cleveland wins 37-27. Pick: Browns *** Colts(2-2) at Steelers(2-2) This is a surprisingly crucial game for both teams as they look to keep pace in their respective divisions. Indianapolis wins 24-20. Pick: Colts *** Texans(0-4) at Titans(0-4) The Texans have not bottommed-out yet, until now, and heads might roll in Houston after this one. Tennessee wins 21-7. Pick: Titans *** Giants(3-1) at Commanders(1-3) Jameis Winston will lead one of the NFL’s most improved teams to another win. New York wins 29-13. Pick: Giants *** Bears(3-1) at Packers(2-2) At this point, Ben Johnson could suit up a 46-year-old Rex Grossman at QB and still lead Chicago to another routine victory. Chicago wins 27-16. Pick: Bears *** Vikings(4-0) at Saints(1-3) No defense in the NFL has given up fewer points than the Minnesota Vikings squad, led by Brian Flores. Conversely, no defense in the NFL has given up more points than the New Orleans Saints squad, led by Brandon Staley. One might see where this is a problem. It looks as though the Vikings will score quite a bit in this game, while the Saints won’t. It’s a shame honestly, considering where the Saints have fallen since their win in Baltimore in Week 2. Not just a fall in the standings, but the fall in confidence and faith of the fans. Despite it all, the Dome should be loud, even with the amount of purple that will be in attendance, but like the last two home games, there will simply be too many obstacles for Kellen Moore’s team to overcome. Minnesota wins 31-19. Pick: Vikings *** Sunday, October 11th – Late Games Broncos(2-2) at Chargers(0-4) Denver rebounds from last week’s loss, with a dominant win over the sad-sack Chargers in Los Angeles. Denver wins 21-7. Pick: Broncos *** Lions(2-2) at Cardinals(1-3) Arizona is better than their record shows, and Detroit is worse, much worse. Arizona wins 14-10. Pick: Cardinals *** 49ers(4-0) at Seahawks(3-1) These bitter NFC West rivals will show us all what a huge rivalry game is supposed to look like. This slugfest will go back and forth, but the Niners find a way to win on the road. San Francisco wins 20-13. Pick: 49ers *** Sunday Night Football Ravens(3-1) at Falcons(2-2) No Lamar Jackson? No chance against the red-hot Falcons in Atlanta. It’s just another dominant primetime win for the birds. Atlanta wins 34-21. Pick: Falcons *** Monday, October 12th – Monday Night Football Bills(3-1) at Rams(2-2) – Game of the Week This highly-anticipated Monday Night showdown should be infinitely more competitive and entertaining than last Monday Night’s debacle. Many consider this a Super Bowl preview, we’ll see about that, but even without those lofty expectations, this game will be phenomenal. It will be razor-close, but the home team finds a way to win in the end. Los Angeles wins 37-34. Pick: Rams *** There we go, Week 5 is shaping up to be pretty interesting. Leave us your picks, comments, and insight below!

title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 5 preview vs. the Vikings
summary: It’s clear the New Orleans Saints must invest in their young talent, and it’s time to see some of these players start over the veterans in front of them. DT Christen Miller Somehow, Miller was a healthy scratch against the Falcons. A poor decision that made little sense then. Miller could have helped defend Bijan […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - SEPTEMBER 27: CJ Donaldson #43 of the New Orleans Saints warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Cesars Superdome on September 27, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s clear the New Orleans Saints must invest in their young talent, and it’s time to see some of these players start over the veterans in front of them. DT Christen Miller Somehow, Miller was a healthy scratch against the Falcons. A poor decision that made little sense then. Miller could have helped defend Bijan Robinson (and apparently Brian Robinson Jr.), and Davon Godchaux was injured at the end of the game. It feels like the writing is on the wall with Godchaux, and with Miller’s impressive preseason, he needs to start. At least the Saints need to see what they have with Miller, and even if he struggles (which wouldn’t be shocking because he’s still a ROOKIE), it’s important that he gets reps. TE Oscar Delp Delp continues to be a big part of the offense, but with the entire offensive line’s struggles during the Falcons game, his job to try and help block was way too much for a young player, or really any player. Delp’s blocking issues have removed him as a passing option, which is unfortunate, and I hope they can elevate him over Fant as a receiver soon. His blocking is just too important right now. OG Jeremiah Wright Hot take (or maybe not), the Saints should just start Wright. I’m not saying it’ll be better in the short term, but if it’s already pretty bad, you can’t go lower. The Saints selected Wright for a reason, and seeing what he can do as a starter is extremely important before the season ends. Also, with the team being 1-3, it’s time to start considering loading up on draft picks, and Cesar Ruiz can be a trade piece. WR Bryce Lance It’s sadly clear that Bryce Lance is not ready to be that WR3 yet. He makes some plays and blocks well, but he is making rookie mistakes the Saints can’t afford. Also, Tyler Shough has not been able to connect with Lance on the deep ball, but the Saints want to make that happen, which is positive. WR Barion Brown Brown’s return game has not been good enough, which is a surprise. That was the one area we felt that Brown could make an impact right away, but it’s been too inconsistent. Maybe with Lance’s struggles last game, Brown may get into the offense more, but also, I wouldn’t push it. RB CJ Donaldson This is the first time I’m adding Donaldson to the list, and it’s long overdue. Donaldson has been the best blocker in the RB room, but for some reason he wasn’t utilized in that role against the Falcons, eventhough the offensive line was struggling. Also, Donaldson’s strong running style is something the Saints currently lack, and I believe he fits better with what Kellen Moore is trying to do in the run game. The Kendre Miller project is over, and it’s time for Donaldson to take over. OT Mason Murphy Asim Richards’ struggles showed that the Saints need to go in another direction, and Mason Murphy is the clear choice. It’s time to make some changes. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson DB Lorenzo Styles Jr.

On top of that, he’s probably one of the most competitive. You morph those together and you have somebody that sometimes that may happen. Don’t ever take that away from a player. Arvell Reese, LB/Edge, New York Giants. Reeseis a very scary player. He has been on the field for over 99% of the defensive snaps for the Giants, opening the year in what has primarily been an off-ball linebacker role while leading the league in solo tackles (27). With Brian Burns suffering a season-ending torn ACL, though, the Giants moved Reese onto the line of scrimmage more often against the Cardinals in Week 4, with their first-round pick playing more than 46% of his defensive snaps as an edge defender, up from 34% over the first three weeks. Reese isn’t the Micah Parsons-esque pass rusher Giants fans might have hoped they were landing when he fell to the fifth pick of this year’s draft, but New York probably doesn’t beat Arizona on Sunday without him being the best player on the field. title: NFL predictions: Will underdog Giants keep first place in NFC East?
summary: The New York Giants are alone in first place in the NFC East. Will they still be sitting on that perch as day turns to evening on Sunday? That depends on the outcome of their game against the Washington Commanders. Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game and the rest of […]
full_text: The New York Giants are alone in first place in the NFC East. Will they still be sitting on that perch as day turns to evening on Sunday? That depends on the outcome of their game against the Washington Commanders. Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game and the rest of the NFL Week 5 action. Chris Pflum I think this game comes down to two questions: Can the Giants play a complete game, and how much difference does Jayden Daniels make? I won’t be surprised if we see a less aggressive brand of defense this week than we saw against the Cardinals. The Giants need to play to their strengths, but also limit the opportunities for Daniels to hurt them out of structure. I don’t think we can expect the defense to shut the Commanders’ offense down, so the offense will need to step up with more down-to-down consistency. I’m just not sure if that’s in Jameis Winston’s uh… Uhhh… ( idiom, sir? ) Idiom! Still, I think the Giants are the more complete whe healthier team. I’m going to bet on the Giants’ newfound resilience, and the fact that this is a team built to win ugly. Pick: Giants Tony DelGenio To me, this game is a coin flip. Both teams are better than they generally have been in the last few years (although the Commanders made a nice run in 2024). Both have been decimated by injuries to key players. Both have a rookie Ohio State linebacker playing really well. And both have a potentially elite quarterback who has missed significant time with injuries in two consecutive seasons. That last point is where the game hinges. Only one team has that QB back on Sunday. The Giants were the Commanders’ daddies until Jayden Daniels came along. Since then, Washington is 4-0 against them, even though Daniels missed one of those games, and Daniels was a big reason for each of the three wins when he played. Lost in the euphoria of the Giants’ rally and goal line stand to beat Arizona is that when their defense was playing the Cardinals’ offense straight up, Jacoby Brissett was shredding it. Dennard Wilson started blitzing – a lot – and that turned things in the Giants’ favor. Will Wilson risk doing the same against the uber-mobile Daniels? If not, then unless Wilson can figure out how to get pressure without blitzing, it will be up to the Giants’ secondary to slow down Stefon Diggs, Terry McLaurin, and rookie Antonio Williams without help. I could imagine Wilson using Arvell Reese as a spy to keep Daniels from wreaking havoc when he flees the pocket. If so, then although Washington has a good running game, I have (some) more confidence in the Giants DLs and LBs to limit it than in previous games when the Commanders just ran it down the Giants’ throats. On offense, I expect the Giants to try to move the ball on the ground against the Commanders, but their run defense has been good to date. The key will be whether the Giants’ offensive line, which has been leakier than I’d like in pass protection, can give Jameis Winston and the Giants’ receivers enough time to exploit the Commanders’ suspect secondary, and whether we’ll get more Famous Jameis or Shameful Jameis. In the end, my coin flip comes up Daniels, and the Giants come back to Earth a little. Pick : Commanders Nick Falato Jayden Daniels is returning from injury for the 1-3 Washington Commanders, who are traveling back from their 30-13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London. Washington’s lone home game was a 33-31 upset against the Seattle Seahawks, led by Marcus Mariota in Week 3. The Commanders defense is good against the run, ranking sixth in overall yards allowed on the ground, but their pass defense has struggled this season. The Giants will look to test the base defense with their heavier personnel, but the Giants can gain an edge with the matchups outside with Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields, and Isaiah Likely; scheming Fields against the 5’8 Amik Robertson, who has played well this season, will give the Giants the opportunity on vertical balls in one-on-one matchups against middle-of-the-field closed defenses. Jameis Winston will have opportunities to attack Washington’s defense through the air, but the Giants must take better care of the football. I expect the Giants defense to remain aggressive against Jayden Daniels. I can see this going either way, and believe the Giants will have a good game plan against Washington, but it should be a hard-fought game. I’m going with the Giants, though. Pick: Giants David Hartman Remember last season, when week after week the Giants faced a powerhouse? What a difference a year makes. The Giants are halfway through a four-game stretch against opponents who, like them, had a Top-10 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Three of those four games are at home. It’s the easiest stretch of the Giants’ 2026 schedule and so far, they’re taking advantage, albeit by the proverbial skin of their teeth. Still, wins are wins, and after seeing devastating injuries quickly burst the bubble after the opening win over Dallas, the Giants are alone in first place and look to keep the good mojo going at Washington this Sunday. The Commanders return from a trip to London that not only saw them lose, but they also lost their backup quarterback in the process. It’s been a rough start to the season for Dan Quinn’s team. The good news (for them) is a return to the lineup for Jayden Daniels. Whether he and his bum elbow can stay in the game for 60 minutes could be the biggest factor in the outcome. Daniels has unique dual-threat abilities that could give the Giants’ front seven fits — assuming he’s playing with no limitations. Washington is a slight favorite, and on paper this is a tough game to handicap. Recent history suggests a close game, and mistakes (turnovers, penalties, special teams gaffes, etc.) will probably be what decides it. That’s where Jameis Winston makes me a little nervous. I’m sure the coaching staff doesn’t want to see 33 dropbacks again, but Washington is tough to run on and easy to throw on (their defense ranks sixth against the run and 24th against the pass), and with Daniels at the helm they can score points, so I expect plenty of passing. I really want to pick the G-Men here, but I think the return of Daniels (and potentially, Terry McLaurin) will give Washington just enough of a lift to get past New York. Pick: Commanders by 4 Valentine’s View The 3-1 first-place Giants are 3.5-point underdogs to the 1-3 last-place Washington Commanders on Sunday. That tells you a lot about the muddled NFC East. Few seem convinced the Giants are the best team in the division. The Philadelphia Eagles are reeling. The Dallas Cowboys might be the best team, and maybe someday they will play like it. The Commanders are pinning their hopes on the health of star quarterback Jayden Daniels. The Giants have earned all three of their victories in the can’t-quite-believe-what-they-are-seeing confines of MetLife Stadium. They have won the last two in dramatic, last-second fashion thanks to great defensive work. They can get better, and need to get better. Offensively, they need to take better care of the ball and get more production from the run game. Defensive, a consistent pass rush would be nice. I want to believe the Giants can go into Landover, Md. and win. I do think they are capable. The Commanders are not a juggernaut. The return of Jayden Daniels and the fact that this game is away from home, though, make it hard for me to ride with the Giants. Pick: Commanders Giants fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! title: 4 takeaways from Giants DC Dennard Wilson: Touching Tae Banks’ heart
summary: Deonte Banks’ resurgence at cornerback has been a major story for the New York Giants so far this season. Banks looked like a lost cause at the end of last season, his second straight terrible year after a promising 2023 rookie season. Head coach John Harbaugh and his staff, including defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, offered […]
full_text: Tae Banks | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Deonte Banks’ resurgence at cornerback has been a major story for the New York Giants so far this season. Banks looked like a lost cause at the end of last season, his second straight terrible year after a promising 2023 rookie season. Head coach John Harbaugh and his staff, including defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, offered no judgment of the past. They simply started over, and Banks has responded. ‘I believe in the kid’ "This goes with teaching and coaching – you can't ask for the hand until you touch the heart." – Dennard Wilson pic.twitter.com/fqwwrTw9BH — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 8, 2026 Banks is a Baltimore kid, so Harbaugh and much of his coaching staff have known about him for a long time. Wilson said part of his job was to reach Banks and make him believe that the staff believed in him. “It goes back from when I took the job. And it goes back to me knowing the kid. Like, I believe in the kid. And I’ve always believed in the kid,” Wilson said on Thursday. “And this goes with teaching and coaching. You can’t ask for the hand until you touch the heart. And that was the objective, to touch the heart, to understand that he has people that care about him, that won’t throw him away. If he has a bad moment, if he has a good moment, we’re going to stay consistent. We’re going to have tough love with him. And that’s what he needed. “We do too much of throwing guys away when they’re not having success right now. Sometimes it takes them time to fight through it. Sometimes they need that teacher, that motivator, that person that inspires them to go out and be the best version of themselves. And that was the thing that we wanted to do with him. And that’s all the players. It’s every guy that we have, man, we treat them with love and respect, but we have tough love. And we coach them hard.” Wilson said it is about more than telling them what to do. “We preach discipline and detail,” Wilson said. “But it’s not about just telling them what to do from an X’s and O’s standpoint. It’s also getting to know them as a person, to know how they operate, to know how they tick, to be able to push them without telling them all the time. So, that’s the impact. That’s what this coaching staff has done with the players. We’ve fused positivity. We’ve learned our players on and off the field. We support our players on and off the field. And we show love when love is needed.” Here are more takeaways from Wilson’s media availability. Handling ‘unscouted runs’ Wilson said Arizona sprung some “unscouted runs” on the Giants in their first two drives on Sunday as they went up 14-3, rushing nine times for 81 yards. After that, the Giants held the Cardinals to 42 yards on 17 carries. “They came out with some unscouted runs that we didn’t see or predict that they were going to do. So, they hurt us on a few of them,” Wilson said. “A couple of plays was leveraging, getting down closer to the line of scrimmage, boxing a ball back, and then we made some adjustments on the sideline to kind of surround their formations after that second series, and guys came out there and executed. We stopped the run, forced them to pass, and we were able to get after them when they were passing.” Defending Kayvon Kayvon Thibodeaux has been quiet this season, with just five tackles, one quarterback hit, and no sacks or tackles for loss so far this season. Wilson still seems excited about what Thibodeaux can do as a pass rusher. “Kayvon has done an excellent job pass rushing. More so when he’s on the edge, he’s forcing the ball back, he’s using his long arm. He’s been around the quarterback, but at times we have to convert a little bit better, and he will. It’s coming. It’s coming for him.,” Wilson said. “His speed is still there. I love his power. I think early on we had him playing inside a little bit too much. I think he’s just better off the edge right now. I can’t wait to see him go out there and perform this week. The numbers are still – they’re going to come, just like I said last week. He’s ready to turn it on. He’s excited about the pass rush plan this week, and I can’t wait to see him go out there and execute.” Greg Newsome’s impact The Giants signed the former first-round pick to a one-year “prove it” contract in free agency. Newsome has played well. “He’s been a great impact. I love him. Man, I believe so wholeheartedly in him and his ability,” Wilson said. “He has cultivated the room with his energy, with his effort, his attention to detail, his willingness to learn, his willingness to go the extra mile to bring guys in with – him and (safety) Jevón (Holland) bring the DBs in the group, watch extra film together. They spend a lot of time together. If you see them, like I say, their energy is infectious. I mean, they dance and do all their little corny moves every day. The DBs were able to pick the music this week and, man, it’s terrible (laughs). But they love it. They love it. “So, as long as they love it and they are in a good place, I’m happy. But we’re happy to have him. He’s been an outstanding addition to this defense and to this organization.”

title: NY Giants’ Arvell Reese named NFL Rookie of the Week
summary: New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese has been named NFL Rookie of the Week for his play on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. It is the first of what might be many honors for Reese, the fifth overall pick in the draft, who appears to have a bright future. Reese helped the Giants to a […]
full_text: Arvell Reese | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese has been named NFL Rookie of the Week for his play on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. It is the first of what might be many honors for Reese, the fifth overall pick in the draft, who appears to have a bright future. Reese helped the Giants to a 36-24 victory over the Cardinals as they improved to 3-1 on the season with nine solo tackles, three passes defensed, one tackle for loss and his first career interception. He leads the NFL with 26 solo tackles. After Sunday’s game, he called his performance “decent.” “One thing you look for is called ‘no-hesitation tackling,'” coach John Harbaugh recalled this week about scouting Reese in the draft. “In other words, guys who get there quick and don’t give the ball carrier much chance to make him miss, they aren’t really too hesitant. But you’ve got to be good to do that because if you’re going that way and the ball carrier is coming the other way, you can miss when you do that too. So, he’s got that unique kind of just talent to get there quickly and still hit his target. And you see it. He’s doing it now. He’s doing a great job.” Many analysts saw Reese as an edge defender in the NFL. The Giants did not, drafting him to be an inside linebacker. Why? “I would answer it this way. That’s what he played. So, it was easy,” Harbaugh said. “You watched him on tape and he played it really well. And I could see where they might have said, ‘Well, he’s young, he hasn’t played a lot. He’s 20 years old,’ and all that, but he played it really well at Ohio State against the best teams in the country in a pretty complicated defensive system that they have over there. So, yeah, it was, to me, the evidence was right there.” Cornerback Deonte Banks won NFL Defensive Player of the Week honors this week for his game-clinching interception against the Cardinals.

title: Fantasy Football 2026: Week 5 preview — Start/sit and more
summary: Welcome to Week 5! The NFL season is almost at the quarter pole, and the fantasy football regular season will be more than a third of the way done once Week 5 is in the books. That was fast. Unfortunately, the injuries continue to mount, and this week the Byes start. Fielding a decent fantasy […]
full_text: The Dirty Birds are back | Getty Images Welcome to Week 5! The NFL season is almost at the quarter pole, and the fantasy football regular season will be more than a third of the way done once Week 5 is in the books. That was fast. Unfortunately, the injuries continue to mount, and this week the Byes start. Fielding a decent fantasy lineup is getting harder and harder. As for the NFL, it’s been a somewhat surprising (and confusing) first month of the season. Figuring out which teams look like playoff squads and which ones are in real trouble isn’t so easy. Look at the Falcons – they scored 16 points combined in Weeks 1-2 (fewest in the league) and then 80 points combined the last two weeks (most in the league). Only three teams are undefeated after four weeks (KC, SF, MIN), while five teams sit at 0-4 (MIA, TB, LAC, TEN, HOU). That total is tied with 1976 for the most winless teams at the four-week mark. Two of those teams (HOU, LAC) made the playoffs last season. The Bucs, who in 1976 were an expansion team that finished 0-14 and had the worst point differential in NFL history (-287), have the unique distinction of being on both lists. We’ll get to see them Thursday night, battling the 2-2 Cowboys, who once again have a high-flying offense paired with a defense that can’t stop anyone. Maybe a UDFA rookie QB making his second career start is just what the doctor ordered. If you want to hold your nose and stream the Cowboys’ D/ST this week, have at it. Stats of the Week : Go Big Blue! The Giants are alone in first place in the NFC East for the first time since 2015 (when Eli Manning was their QB). 2. The 4-0 Vikings are last in the NFL in yards and failed to score a touchdown in two of their four games. 3. Kenneth Walker, Jr. has 537 rushing yards on the young season, the most through Week 4 since Arian Foster’s 539 in 2010. 4. The Bears ran 57 more plays than the Jets and had more first downs (34) than the Jets had plays (32). 5. Offensive ineptitude, Part 1: Denver’s first half points on the season: 13, with just one touchdown. 6. Offensive ineptitude, Part 2: The Eagles were 0-for-12 on third down against the Rams and going back to Week 3 they’ve failed to convert their last 17 third downs. 7. LAC@SEA was the first game in NFL history where each team’s first offensive snap resulted in an interception. OK, Week 5, here we go! Note: The PHI@JAC game is in London – set those lineups early! Bye Weeks: CAR, KC Week 5 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start Bijan Robinson . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade, and Sleeper of the Week. The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers cooked, thank you very much. Tet McMillan was my Ride of the Week and he finished as the WR1, with over 200 yards and two TDs. Ka-Ching! Emeka Egbuka was my Fade of the Week and he had a whopping two catches for 13 yards. Wham! Hopefully, he wasn’t in your lineup. I guaranteed that Tucker Kraft would score, and he did. I also had misses, of course, but overall it was a solid week. I’ll try to repeat that success. You can check my work here. *** Rides of the Week: Jacoby Brisssett (vs. DET) and Jared Goff (@ARI). I’m feeling generous at the moment so I’ll give you two QBs, who happen to be facing each other’s decrepit defense this week. There are only a few QBs that I’m starting over either of these guys this week. This game is going to be fun, unless you don’t have anyone playing in it. The Vegas total is 54.5, which is among the highest we’ve seen all season. The Lions have allowed 127 points which is just one point behind the Saints for worst in the league, and the Cardinals are close behind them (117). Play what you can in this one. The QBs should feast. The Lions are allowing the most passing yards and fantasy points per game (FPPG) to opposing QBs, while the Cardinals are again close behind them (fifth most FPPG allowed). Both defenses have already given up 11 TD passes, tied for most in the league. Fade of the Week: Jalen Hurts (@JAC). I hate the term “MASH unit”, but I think it applies here. Philly is probably going to be without three opening day starting offensive linemen, its #1 and #2 running backs, its #1 receiver, and its #1 tight end. That’s a lot to overcome, and going back to last season, the offense isn’t exactly a juggernaut to begin with. Do you really want to get up early on Sunday to spend three hours waiting for the Iggles to convert a third down, or get into the red zone? Trust me, it’s misery. Maybe Hurts will run enough to save his day, but he failed to clear 100 passing yards against the Rams and it gets harder this week against an underrated Jaguars’ defense. They’re allowing the sixth fewest FPPG to opposing QBs and are tied for the league lead with six picks. Hurts is a great fantasy QB, but not this week. I’m sitting him in my main league. Fire him up again when he gets some weapons back and the schedule gets easier. Sleeper of the Week: Jameis Winston (@WAS). I’ll stick with the QB theme and go with the 17 th -ranked QB on the board for the week. Last week we got the full Jameis, and I had forgotten how much joy we were missing – three TDs, two picks, four sacks, a heart-stopping finish, and his usual hilarity before and after the game. This week’s road matchup against a division rival is another tasty one where the script might call for a lot of passing, and with J.J. McCarthy on the roster there’s pressure on Jameis to keep producing and winning. Only the Lions are allowing more FPPG to opposing QBs than the Commanders, and they’re another team that’s allowed a league-worst 11 passing TDs. If you need a second QB in a Superflex, or a streamer to replace Lamar Jackson, Patrick Mahomes, or someone else, Jameis is a fun flier who could easily finish inside the Top-10 QBs. Just take some Pepcid before the game and have your favorite alcohol handy. Lots of it. Quarterback: Elite option this week – Josh Allen and Matt Stafford (playing against each other); the analysis starts below them. I already discussed four QBs in detail, so let’s breeze through this section. Rides: Dak Prescott (vs. TB) is humming, and Tampa is falling apart. I like Dak for a solid and productive game on Thursday night, even though it’s not a great matchup and he might not have to throw a ton. I think Dallas will control the game. Others ranked in the Top-15 this week who I think will outperform their ranking: Jordan Love (vs. CHI), Drake Maye (vs. LV), and Jayden Daniels (vs. NYG, assuming he plays). Daniels is not without risk of re-injury, but it’s a pretty good matchup. Sleepers: Aaron Rodgers (@IND) is coming off back-to-back games with at least 290 passing yards and three TD passes. He’s on a heater and is finding his weapons. The Colts are allowing the sixth most FPPG to opposing QBs. If you need a second QB in a Superflex, or a streamer for someone who is hurt or on a Bye, there are some OK options (in addition to Winston and Rodgers), including Tyson Bagent (@GB), Sam Darnold (vs. SF), and if you want to give him one more shot (I get it if you can’t and especially if Justin Jefferson is out again), Kyler Murray (@NO,…

title: NY Giants ‘just not good enough yet’ in the run game, says John Harbaugh
summary: The New York Giants’ offense is built upon a run game that has helped them to a 3-1 start by grinding out first downs and controlling the clock. A closer look at the numbers, though, shows that the Giants have not actually run the ball well. They have simply run the ball a lot. And […]
full_text: Cam Skattebo | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants’ offense is built upon a run game that has helped them to a 3-1 start by grinding out first downs and controlling the clock. A closer look at the numbers, though, shows that the Giants have not actually run the ball well. They have simply run the ball a lot. And ground the play clock down to the nub as much as they can. Through four games, the Giants have run the ball 49.17% of the time, sixth-most in the NFL. They are fifth in the league with 29.8 rushing attempts per game. They are second in the NFL in time of possession at 32:41 per game. They are also second in the NFL in seconds used per play at 32.4. The Giants, though, are 23rd in the league at 3.7 yards per rush. The Giants’ rushing Expected Points Added (EPA) is -15.6, 26th, per NextGenStats. Their 37.8% success rate is 22nd. The Giants are at -45 in rushing yards over expected, 26th in the league. The Giants have eight runs of 10 yards or more. Only five teams have fewer. Over their last three games, without Jaxson Dart’s ability to energize the offense with his running ability, the Giants’ average of 3.4 yards per carry is 28th. The Giants have just one run of more than 20 yards, a 22-yard run by Dart. Their second-longest run? A 15-yard scramble by Jameis Winston. The longest run they have from a running back is a 13-yarder from Cam Skattebo. Head coach John Harbaugh was blunt on Wednesday when I asked him about the state of the running game. “We’re just not good enough yet,” Harbaugh said. “Defenses are playing us pretty well. As we get better, we’ll probably have more longer runs. Also, if we make them pay a little more with play action, I think that’ll loosen them up a little bit, probably. But we just got to keep getting better. I think the guys are working hard at it. We’re playing very hard. We’re trying to play very physically. So, all the elements are there. We just have to get better, keep getting better.” How can the Giants get better? It is fair to ask how much more explosive the Giants can get running the ball with the personnel they have in the backfield. Skattebo is a bulldozer with 4.65 40-yard dash speed, slow for a running back. In 169 rushing attempts over two seasons, he has one run of 20 yards or more, a 24-yarder. Still, he did average 4.1 yards per carry last season and 50.5% of his runs were considered successful. Those numbers through four games this year are 3.5 yards and 44.1%. Najee Harris had 1,000-yard rushing seasons in each of his first four seasons in the NFL with the Pittsburgh Steelers, but he has just 4.57-second 40-yard dash speed and a 3.9 yards-per-carry average for his career. In 1,134 carries, his longest run is 37 yards. Perhaps more rushing opportunities for Tyrone Tracy could be part of the solution. Tracy has just four carries for 16 yards this season. In 372 career rushing attempts, Tracy has nine runs of 20 yards or more. Mostly, though, the Giants are going to have to get better at executing their run game. Fullback Patrick Ricard, a central figure in run games with Harbaugh and the Baltimore Ravens since 2017, knows what Harbaugh is talking about when he says the Giants are “not good enough” in their run game. “I think he’s talking about how we can fit it up as an offense better in terms of how to execute the run play. It’s not the scheme. It’s not the coaching,” Ricard said. “I feel like it’s just us executing the play correctly with the fronts. Like ID’ing it correctly. All of us being on the same page in terms of who we’re going to [block]. And then just applying our techniques and letting it go.” Ricard said one mistake in a “very detailed” running attack designed by senior offensive assistant Greg Roman can impact the success of a play. “We’ve had instances where maybe the tackle/guard on the play side went to the wrong guy. And if they went to the right guy, then the play would have had more yards,” Ricard said. “Or, it’s like one person didn’t hear the play call correctly. Because we have a lot of check-with-me’s. Maybe one guy didn’t hear it correctly. “So it’s just communication with all of us being on the same page. It’s like those growing pains you have when you have a bunch of new coaches. A new offense. A running game that’s very detailed with Greg Roman.” Ricard said he sees it as “growing pains of just learning together.” “If you’re having 5 yards, 4 yards of carry, I think that’s a pretty good run game,” Ricard said. “But we’re striving for explosive runs. So if you’re not having those explosive runs, it’s just going to be you can’t have negative plays. “But we’re striving; we’re working every day at trying to all play together to where we can get those explosive plays.” Let’s see if they can get it figured out by Sunday against the Washington Commanders.

title: Giants-Commanders ‘5 questions’: Jayden Daniels, Sonny Styles, more
summary: The New York Giants face a Washington Commanders team on Sunday that has gotten off to a rocky start to the season. In an NFC East where no team appears to be dominant, though, that isn’t a death-knell. Let’s learn more about the Commanders in our ‘5 questions’ segment, with Andrew York of Hogs Haven […]
full_text: Sonny Styles | Getty Images The New York Giants face a Washington Commanders team on Sunday that has gotten off to a rocky start to the season. In an NFC East where no team appears to be dominant, though, that isn’t a death-knell. Let’s learn more about the Commanders in our ‘5 questions’ segment, with Andrew York of Hogs Haven as our huckleberry. Ed: How disappointing is the 1-3 start? Is there still belief that if Jayden Daniels can come back and stay healthy the Commanders can make noise in an up-for-grabs NFC East? Andrew: It’s terribly disappointing, but it’s not just the fact that the team is losing games, it’s that they’re constantly losing players to injury too. A loss can be overcome with a win next week, but losing core players makes even a win next week harder. It’s also tough for fans that it feels like we’re re-living the injury-plagued 2025 season again, when we were hoping for something closer to 2024. That being said, the team has looked better and deeper than they did at this same point in 2025. Last year, an injury to Terry McLaurin was enough to collapse the entire passing game. This year, players like Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams can pick up the slack. The same is true for several other position groups, but it’s only possible to have so much depth, so I hope the pace of injuries can become more normal. Even without the two best starters on the OL (Laremy Tunsil and Sam Cosmi), the team was able to protect and score against the Seahawks’ elite defense in Week 3. That said, fans are anxiously awaiting the return of Jayden Daniels. He had a strong training camp and looked really effective and efficient in Week 2 vs the Cowboys right up until he was injured. Despite the injuries, I think the overall roster now is better than it was in 2024, so there’s absolutely a belief that a healthy Jayden Daniels could reverse the team’s fortunes.and get them back into a winning record. As you said, it’s still early in the season and the division is up for grabs. Ed: What are your impressions thus far of Sonny Styles? I thought the Giants might select him if the draft had fallen a different way. No one in New York is unhappy with Arvell Reese, I know that much. Andrew: Sonny Styles has been amazing and already looks like he’ll be a star on defense for many years to come. At first in the preseason, he seemed a bit hesitant and afraid to trust his first read, but quickly improved his reaction time and his tremendous athletic measurables have really shown up. He’s been a very strong tackler showing sideline-to-sideline speed and can limit runs anywhere on the field. He’s also shown to be very good in coverage, like this play where he ran step-for-step with Seahawks RB Jadarian Price to break up a pass. He’s also shown to be a dangerous blitzer, like in this play where he ran straight through Saquon Barkley to sack Jalen Hurts. He’s good at everything you’d want a linebacker to do and hasn’t shown any obvious weaknesses. In addition to his presence in games, I’ve also been impressed by how he carries and presents himself off the field. He seems very humble, serious, hard-working, and simply eager to be a good teammate and improve himself. He has a mindset that I think will age extremely well in the NFL. He actually reminds me of how Bobby Wagner spoke and acted when he was here, though without Wagner’s aura of accomplishment. Ed: If you could take one player off the Giants’ roster and put him in Washington’s lineup, who would it be? Why? Andrew: If we’re taking into account contract, age, etc, probably Arvell Reese. Linebacker isn’t exactly a need on the Commanders right now, but you can never have too many playmakers and he seems to already look like a star in the making. Most Commanders fans would probably say Malik Nabers and he would probably be a bigger long-term upgrade over the wide receiver group, but I’d be a bit worried about his injury history on a team that already has quite the problem with injuries. Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Ed: Who are a couple of players on the Commanders’ roster we may not know a lot about, but that we should be familiar with for Sunday? Andrew: On offense, rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams was taken in the third round of this year’s draft. He’s a great route runner and seems to already understand a lot of the nuance of the WR position. As a result, he’s been getting more and more time on the field and it’s clear the staff trust him. Williams went from a 28.9% route share in Week 1 to leading the team in routes run in Week 4, so his role keeps increasing in the offense. On defense, I’ll go with cornerback Amik Robertson. He’s a 5-foot-9 stick of dynamite who flies all over the field making plays and plays much bigger than his size. He’s sticky in coverage, but also a physical and sure tackler and a decent blitzer. He’s also got a swagger and energy that seems infectious. He signed as a free agent from the Lions this offseason and is our most playmaking CB. Ed: I see this as a 50-50 game, whatever the oddsmakers say. If the Giants are going to win it, how should they plan on attacking the Commanders? Andrew: To attack the defense, I would plan to go passing heavy to exploit the defensive back group, which is probably the weakest position group on the Commanders roster. Play 3- or even 4-wide receiver sets (forcing Washington’s worst personnel on the field) and layer their routes to hit all areas of the field, expecting a coverage bust somewhere. The trick here is to protect your quarterback well enough to enable him to have time to throw. Dallas and Seattle had good enough pass protection that they could air out the ball to the tune of 279 passing yards and 379 passing yards against us respectively. In weeks 1-3, the Commanders run defense had been stout, as seems to be a hallmark of this Brian Flores-style Daronte Jones defense. The defense allowed a lot more rushing in Week 4, but I think that’s only because they were on the field all of the time once Mariota got injured and the defensive players got gassed. To attack the offense (and assuming Jayden Daniels is starting for Washington), I would use a QB spy to limit Jayden’s rushing and only rush four, dropping the rest back in coverage. Jayden has been very good at reading the blitz and throwing quickly or using his legs to avoid it, so dropping more back in coverage and shifting coverages has generally been more effective at preventing him from making a play.

Giants coach John Harbaugh says that’s not good enough. The Giants now have fumbled seven times in four games, although they’ve only lost two to the opposing defense (Tyrone Tracy Jr. in Week 1). Harbaugh looked like he was going to Harris (nine carries, 30 yards, two-point conversion) as Sunday’s second half finisher ahead of Cam Skattebo until Harris coughed it up. The veteran didn’t play another snap after that. Skattebo played his first game without a fumble but gained only 3.2 yards per carry (20 rushes for 58 yards). He also has the most rush attempts in the NFL (68) without a 15-plus yard gain, per Ian Hartitz of RotoWire. Tracy had one carry for -1 yard. Veteran Devin Singletary has gone from 25 snaps in the opener to 15 in Week 2 to being inactive in Weeks 3 and 4. Harbaugh said Singletary wants to play and the team still values him, but the three active backs have defined roles in the gameplans right now. That could change. 2026 NFL offensive line rankings: Lions rise, Eagles fall without Lane Johnson | PFF 20. New York Giants (up 2). The Giants made a switch to their starting lineup in Week 4, with Bryan Hudson replacing John Michael Schmitz Jr. Hudson proceeded to deliver a really eye-opening performance, securing a 73.8 PFF grade and not allowing a single pressure from 37 pass-blocking snaps. Both tackles have been effective in pass protection, with Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor combining to allow 11 pressures from 133 pass-blocking snaps. B/R 99: Ranking the 99 Best NFL Rookies After Week 4 | Bleacher Report Linebackers Sonny Styles (1) and Arvell Reese (4), who were collegiate teammates and top-seven draft selections, have created instant impacts for the Washington Commanders and New York Giants, respectively. Styles has been particularly good using his length and athleticism in coverage, while creating multiple pressures when asked to blitz. Plus, his run fits are improving each week. Meanwhile, Reese’s versatility has translated to the pro game, with 22 tackles, two tackles for loss, four pass breakups and an interception during the Giants’ last two games. This week’s backup QB? McCarthy today at Giants practice pic.twitter.com/VJzpAPihtH — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 7, 2026 Khalil Mack trade rumors: Landing spots for the Chargers pass rusher | SB Nation New York Giants. We could see a Harbaugh brother trade. Mack is the type of player teams want to do right by and if the Chargers have to punt on this season and the Giants remain a playoff contender, Jim Harbaugh would probably feel good about sending Mack to his brother John’s team. With Brian Burns out, Mack would be a nice fit for New York. The two words that don’t need to define this Giants season | New York Post There is so much about these Giants to get everyone excited. summary: Where the hell is Adonai Mitchell? Seriously, have you seen him? His family must be worried sick! We definitely saw him through the first two weeks of the season, but he has been MIA since. ESPN’s Rich Cimini said on the “Jets Collective” podcast that he heard Mitchell’s finger is “broken.” Head coach Aaron Glenn […]
full_text: Aug 21, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; New York Jets wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (15) warms up before the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Where the hell is Adonai Mitchell? Seriously, have you seen him? His family must be worried sick! We definitely saw him through the first two weeks of the season, but he has been MIA since. ESPN’s Rich Cimini said on the “Jets Collective” podcast that he heard Mitchell’s finger is “broken.” Head coach Aaron Glenn denied that. We’ve got a good old-fashioned western standoff. “Well, the Jets have been pretty tight-lipped on this one, but clearly it’s not your run-of-the-mill sprained finger. I mean, if it were a sprained finger or something of that nature, he would have been out there taped up. We all saw the giant cast on his hand,” Cimini explained. “It would not shock me if we find out that he had surgery. I have not seen him at all in the locker room. Usually you see a guy you know wandering through the locker room. I haven’t seen AD Mitchell in a couple of weeks since that injury.” Glenn said AD Mitchell’s finger got caught in a jersey. I’m not a doctor or anything, but did it get amputated? Caught in a meat slicer? Did he slam it in a car door? I mean, good lord! He hasn’t practiced in the first two practices ahead of the Cleveland Browns game, which means he’s likely out another week. However, next week the door opens. The Jets didn’t place him on injured reserve before Week 3. The thought process has to be that they expected him back before four weeks, which would be next week. Something to monitor. For now, the Jets will have to try to figure it out on offense without him *shoulder shrug*. J-E-T-S! Take the game-day conversation with you! title: New York Jets News: Eli Manning Endorses QB Arch Manning to Jets
summary: Normally, when we’re talking about mock drafts for the New York Jets in October, it’s for an obvious bad reason. However, today’s discussion will destroy a stupid narrative that people have been peddling for months, if not years. Arch Manning is a talented quarterback prospect who could be available in the 2027 NFL Draft. With […]
full_text: Sep 26, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates after a college football game between Tennessee and Texas at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn. on Sept. 26, 2026. Mandatory Credit: Brianna Paciorka-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Normally, when we’re talking about mock drafts for the New York Jets in October, it’s for an obvious bad reason. However, today’s discussion will destroy a stupid narrative that people have been peddling for months, if not years. Arch Manning is a talented quarterback prospect who could be available in the 2027 NFL Draft. With the Jets being recently terrible and having multiple first-round picks, there has been a chance for a while that these two could join forces. Whenever that conversation has been brought up, a swarm of people has been quick to say that would never happen because the Manning family wouldn’t allow it. Interesting. Well, when Uncle Eli Manning was asked where he’d prefer his nephew to play football at the NFL level, he brought up the green and white. “There’s two ways I look at this,” Manning said via Grace McCarron of the New York Post. “For purely selfish reasons, I wouldn’t mind if he went to the [New York] Jets, just because I live right there, I could go to games, I could have dinner with him during the week a little bit. I think it’d be great for him to have some family nearby, so I wouldn’t mind him going to the Jets, being up in New York…that’s just my selfish reasons, and I think he could help them.” Well, well, well, isn’t that a fun plot twist. So it sounds like if the Jets were in a position to select the young Manning, there wouldn’t be any roadblocks to making that a reality. I’m not sure how the LOL Jets crowd is going to take this one, but… Full stop. The New York Jets are one of, if not the best, landing spots for a young quarterback next year. Their roster is overflowing with offensive talent, talented pieces on the offensive line, pass catchers, running backs, and all the rest. If Manning or any other QB prospect lands with the green and white, they have a path to immediate success. We haven’t been able to say that for a long time. J-E-T-S! summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their second official injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Drew Kendall, Jonathan Greenard, Marcus Epps, and Hollywood Brown. Barkley is reportedly “week-to-week” with a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Rams defeated the Eagles 24-20. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their second official injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Drew Kendall, Jonathan Greenard, Marcus Epps, and Hollywood Brown. Barkley is reportedly “week-to-week” with a hamstring injury. He’s on track to miss Sunday’s game. In his absence, the Eagles have Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce at running back. To be determined if they’ll ride with two RBs or use a temporary practice squad elevation on either Carson Steele or Jaydon Blue to give them a third backfield option. Smitty is tracking to miss a second straight game due to a hamstring injury. Not ideal. Seems like he might be able to suit up in Week 6, though. Kendall missing two straight practices points to him not playing against the Jags. Nick Sirianni has an obsession with “competitive advantage” (and that’s definitely really helping the team this year!), so, maybe the following observation from practice is just a red herring. But practice squad interior offensive lineman Jake Majors was getting first-team center looks during the media-attended portion of Thursday’s session. If we take this development to be indicative of who’s actually starting, the Eagles’ offensive line could look like this from left to right: Jordan Mailata, Willie Lampkin, Jake Majors, Tyler Steen, Markel Bell. Fred Johnson and Micah Morris are currently the only backup offensive linemen on the roster. Majors is one of four practice squad blockers with the others being John Ojukwu, Kiran Amegadjie, and the recently added James Brockermeyer. Center Drew Kendall (knee) appears to be absent for a second straight day at Eagles practice. In this look, Jake Majors is at center and Willie Lampkin at left guard. pic.twitter.com/Cl3nKcGEg1 — Tim McManus (@Tim_McManus) October 8, 2026 Greenard is on track to miss his third game this season. He might be able to return next week. Until then, the Eagles will roll with Nolan Smith, Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa as their top four edge rushers. Epps is probably going to miss his second straight start. Look for Michael Carter II to play safety next to Andrew Mukuba in nickel packages with Cooper DeJean next to Mukuba in base defense. Brown is set to miss his third game in a row. And he didn’t actually play in Week 1 despite being active. So, he’ll have zero snaps in four out of five games so far. The Eagles listed five players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Dontayvion Wicks, Zack Baun, Jihaad Campbell, Dallas Goedert, and Fred Johnson. Wicks is a new addition to the report with a hamstring injury; he apparently got hurt during Thursday’s practice. Not a good development. Normally the No. 2 WR, Wicks was WR1 with DeVonta out . If Smith, Brown, and Wicks all can’t play, the Eagles will be down to these four wide receivers on the roster: Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Britain Covey, and Elijah Moore. They also have Xavier Gipson and the recently re-signed Erik Ezukanma on the practice squad. Outside of Cooper (the official Eagles wide receiver of Bleeding Green Nation), not exactly the most imposing group. Baun was limited for the second day in a row. Guessing he’ll be upgraded to full on Friday but we’ll see if that’s the case. Campbell was upgraded from DNP on Wednesday to limited on Thursday. If he can’t play, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. figures to start in his place. I wonder if Campbell’s struggles might lead to Trot Jr. getting some more rotational snaps anyway. Goedert told reporters that he feels “ really good .” Seems like he’s going to give it a go. Will be interested to see how the Eagles distribute their tight end snaps among Goedert, Zach Ertz, Johnny Mundt, and E.J. Jenkins. Assuming he can play, Fred Johnson figures to be the swing tackle behind Jordan Mailata and Markel Bell. He might also be the top backup option at guard, unless the Eagles trust Micah Morris in that capacity instead. The Eagles listed one player under FULL PARTICIPATION: Quinyon Mitchell. Mitchell was upgraded to full after being limited on Wednesday. He’s going to play this week, which is an important development for the Eagles’ defense. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. BLG’S WEEK 5 NFL POWER RANKINGS 1 – Kansas City Chiefs (Last Week: 1) – The Chiefs are the only remaining undefeated team in the AFC and just one of three teams yet to lose a game this season. With the Chargers up next, they’re probably going to reach 5-0. 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 3) – The Niners have a strong case as the NFL’s top team. They have played an easier schedule than the Chiefs have, though. Interested to see how they fare against Seattle in Week 5. Should be a great game. 3 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 4) – The Seahawks rebounded from a bad Week 3 loss. Now we’ll see if the reigning Super Bowl champs can claim the top spot in the NFC West away from the 49ers. 4 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 5) – Lamar Jackson’s injury raises concerns but this offense looks pretty good when he’s available. It remains to be seen if the Cam Jurgens trade will be worth it for the Ravens, who were desperate to find a solution at center. 5 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 2) – The Bills are pretty good while also being slightly unserious. Losing to the Pats at home for the second year in a row? 6 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 6) – They’re probably not going to be able to count on their defense to keep carrying them to wins all season long. The offense being bad will eventually catch up to them. For now, though, being undefeated is fun. 7 – Chicago Bears (LW: 7) – Ben Johnson won a game with his third-string quarterback in Week 3 and his second-string quarterback in Week 4. The Bears are a real power in the NFC with him at the helm. 8 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 8) – They came dangerously close to dropping to 1-3 with a loss to the undermanned Eagles. But they ultimately got the win to keep their season afloat. And Myles Garrett could be back as soon as next week. 9 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 12) – The Cowboys’ offense is capable of lifting their defense. See: Dallas scoring 28 second half points to prove they’re the superior NFL team in Texas. 10 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 14) – The Jags rank second in point differential and second in DVOA this season. They lost to the Chiefs, yes, but they gave the top team in the league a run for their money. They deserve credit for that. 12 – Detroit Lions (LW: 9) – Detroit’s defense is a major problem that could prevent them from seriously contending for a championship. Their ceiling might be a wild card team. 13 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 10) – Two straight losses after starting 2-0 but the Bengals should bounce back against the Dolphins. 14 – New England Patriots (LW: 17) – Big win in Buffalo to keep them alive for the AFC East crown. 15 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 11) – One on hand, this placement feels too high. And now they’re without Lane Johnson as they deal with a bunch of injury absences. More losing is likely on the way. The Eagles are keeping company with … the 0-4 Miami Dolphins. Not great! Not sure why you’d ever go away from Sean Payton running things. 17 – New York Giants (LW: 19) – For the first time since the prehistoric era, the Giants are first in the NFC East! It probably won’t last for too long. But they do have some more winnable games coming up. 18 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 24) – Bryce Young is balling. He leads the NFL in passing yards and has a 100.0 passer rating so far. 19 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 25) – Turns out that there’s a difference between starting Cooper Rush and starting Michael Penix. The Falcons are alive. 20 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 16) – After an exciting start to the season, the Saints have cooled off. Maybe not a team on the rise after all. 21 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 20) – Not sure we learned much from the Colts beating Athan Kaliakmanis. 22 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 26) – Todd Monken sure isn’t tanking. 23 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 23) – The Packers beat a team starting an undrafted rookie free agent quarterback … by three points. Or maybe not. 25 – Washington Commanders (LW: 21) – Washington was down to their third-string rookie quarterback, who actually didn’t even play all that poorly relative to expectation, in a Week 4 loss. We’ll see if Jayden Daniels’ return can give this team a spark in Week 5.
