full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers are set to do battle with their NFC West rival Seattle Seahawks on Sunday at Lumen Field. The 49ers are sporting a 4-0 record, with Seattle coming in at 3-1. The Seahawks won two of the three matchups last season, including the season finale at Levi’s and the divisional round before finishing the job against the New England Patriots at Levi’s Stadium. After celebrating twice in the 49ers building, the team has some work to do to inflict the same pain on their rivals. So, how do the 49ers do that? In the final two matchups, the 49ers offense had to scratch and claw for every inch. Yes, the offense was depleted, but Seattle’s defense was incredible. After spending an offseason looking to add separators at the receiver position, the 49ers aren’t at the level of threat they would like to be, but are far more equipped to handle Seattle’s defense, especially with Brock Purdy’s play in 2026. Here are three things to watch for Sunday: Beating Seattle’s pass rush The 49ers offensive line has kept Purdy clean through four weeks. That’s a feat not easily dismissed regardless of the opponents, but they will face their biggest test of the season against a Seattle pass rush that ranks number one in pass rush win rate, according to ESPN, and sits at the bottom of the league in blitz rate. Straight drop-back and obvious passing situations aren’t where the 49ers want to live against Seattle. Through four weeks, Seattle’s defense is 2nd in EPA/play allowed but is 19th in EPA/play allowed on throws happening quicker than 2.5 seconds, according to SumerSports. The Seahawks are also 28th in EPA/play allowed on short throws. The quick game will need to be on display; look for the 49ers to target Deebo Samuel on these plays, but Mike Evans will need to get past the sticks quickly for Purdy. Breaking through against Mike MacDonald Purdy and Shanahan have beaten MacDonald-led defenses before. However, that was before the defense gelled and the organization got its personnel together. According to SumerSports, in the first three meetings between Mike Macdonald and Brock Purdy, Purdy had 87th, 65th, and 87th percentile performances by EPA/dropback. In the last two, Macdonald’s swarming Seahawks held Purdy to a 10th and 5th-percentile EPA/dropback. For those keeping score at home, the first three performances are good. The last two aren’t, and the 49ers offense hasn’t scored a touchdown against Seattle through eight quarters. The deck is set more fairly for Purdy, but Shanahan and Purdy have their work cut out for them on Sunday. The 49ers offense against base, nickel, and light boxes So far, the 49ers have torched base defenses to the tune of a league-leading 0.29 EPA and have faced base defenses at a league-high rate of 48.6%. Against nickel, the 49ers have faced the second-to-last percentage of 41.4%, but lead the league with a 0.24 EPA. While against light boxes, the 49ers lead the league with 0.52 EPA, but have faced light boxes at the lowest rate in the NFL at 29.7%. Seattle under MacDonald hasn’t been known to play much base defense, and the same is true in 2026. With a 15.5% base percentage, Seattle ranks 29th in the NFL, but sports the third-best EPA allowed at -0.37. The jump from base to nickel is striking, with Seattle in nickel for 68.2% of their snaps, which is tenth, and has allowed the third-best EPA at -0.23. Where things get interesting is that Seattle defends the run well without loading the box, and the proof is in the numbers. Their light box percentage sits at 51.4%, the eighth-highest in the NFL, and they allow the fifth-best EPA at -0.16. Can the 49ers punish their light boxes with throws in the middle and running the football? That is where the game will be decided.
author: Jason Aponte

title: The 4 biggest surprises about the 49ers a month into the season
summary: The San Francisco 49ers beginning the season undefeated isn’t surprising. The Rams looked like a team that had just gotten off a 16-hour flight. The Dolphins and Cardinals were feisty at best. And Bo Nix was gunshy. All eyes will be focused on the Seattle Seahawks, but let’s look at the biggest surprises during the […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers beginning the season undefeated isn’t surprising. The Rams looked like a team that had just gotten off a 16-hour flight. The Dolphins and Cardinals were feisty at best. And Bo Nix was gunshy. All eyes will be focused on the Seattle Seahawks, but let’s look at the biggest surprises during the first month of the season that led to the Niners entering Week 5 undefeated. Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense not being sacked through 4 games Zero sacks — Random Guy (@gocrysomemore22) October 6, 2026 We just watched how the Denver Broncos operate offensively. They’ve allowed five sacks all year. The biggest difference is Bo Nix hasn’t had to scramble the same way Brock Purdy has. The 49ers have the eighth-highest scramble percentage in the NFL. That matches the eye test. Credit to the offensive line, but Purdy could’ve easily been sacked 5-6 times this season. The fact that he hasn’t is a Christmas miracle and easily the biggest surprise this season. Only 13 more games to tie Dan Marino. The offensive line is a strength The OLine who I didn’t trust other than Williams and Puni — Brian Staples (@bpstaples20) October 6, 2026 A lot of love for the offensive line, and rightfully so. A healthy Puni looks like a borderline All-Pro. According to Sports Info Solution’s total points earned metric, Puni has been the best lineman on the Niners and the 12th-best in the NFL. Seven spots behind him isn’t Trent Williams; it’s Jake Brendel, who has one of the lowest blown-block rates in the league. Brendel is the third-best center. After Brendel is Connor Colby, who looks like a completely different player from a season ago, Colby is more assertive, and it’s paying off. Next is Colton McKivitz, who hasn’t really had the “lookout” blocks in pass protection that we’ve seen in years past. Puni has earned 10 points, Brendel has 9, and the other two have 8. Williams sits at 6. We know his job is harder because the 49ers leave Trent on an island and put more on his plate. Despite being isolated, Williams has the lowest pressure rate allowed this season at 3.5% among any left tackle. His blown blocks have come against some funky defensive looks, where slants and stunts have crossed his face. Still, the offensive line is more than holding its own. They’ve been a weapon late in games. Raheem Morris has been an upgrade over Robert Saleh The upgrade that Raheem Morris has been over Saleh. — NJ (@NTPJ_) October 6, 2026 In Week 4, Raheem Morris used 6-man pressures 13.6% of the time. In 2025, Brian Flores used 6-man pressures 13.9% of the time. So, for a game, Morris was effectively Flores. Some fans have been concerned about the lack of sacks, but the illusion of pressure has worked in Morris’s favor. The two-minute drill to end the first half is a great example. He blitzed Nix on four consecutive plays last week. There were no sacks, but there were four incompletions in a row. We’re seeing free rushers, which shows the scheme is working. Some of the differences in the 49ers' defense under Raheem Morris: Base personnel has doubled. 35.7% (13th-highest), up from 18.5% last year. Corners switching sides. Deommodore Lenoir is the boundary CB on 72.8% of the snaps. They've already used 6+ DBs on more snaps (19)… — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) October 8, 2026 Above all, we’re not seeing some of the defense’s weak links exposed the way they were a season ago. A month into the season, Morris feels like an upgrade. The feather in Morris’s cap has been erasing deep passes. The 49ers have allowed a league-low 33% completion percentage on downfield passes this season. The only other team to allow a rate below 40% is the Niners’ opponent this Sunday. We’ve also seen Morris adapt to his personnel. Keion White lines up everywhere. Literally. He’s the only player in the NFL to play at least 10% of his snaps at four different spots. Morris has also logged more Dime snaps (19) already this season than Saleh did all last year (17). Base personnel is up, too. Morris is using it 35.7% of the time, compared to Saleh’s 18.5%. Above all, we’re not seeing some of the defense’s weak links exposed the way they were a season ago. A month into the season, Morris feels like an upgrade. Injuries haven’t slowed the 49ers Still playing strong after injuries .. next man up mentality 💪🏾 — Killa (@Killa_Keem_Doe) October 6, 2026 The 49ers offense was expected to be potent. De’Zhaun Stribling and Ricky Pearsall would complement Mike Evans. We’ve seen early and often why they brought in Evans, but it’s been a one-man band. The 49ers dwarf the rest of the league in EPA per pass. But they’re not relying on the speed of Pearsall and Stribling. Shanahan’s scheme has gotten the best of everybody. Evans is a big reason why. George Kittle’s screen pass to end Week 4 highlights how Shanahan is always two steps ahead of his competition. What’s getting swept under the rug is that the 49ers sit sixth in rushing success rate. It’s a metric they were abysmal at a season ago. When the Niners suffered all their injuries last year, they were bottom three in every meaningful statistic. This year they are anywhere between 17th and 19th. Hovering around average has been good enough. As they get healthier, they should start to creep closer to 10th, but kudos to Raheem Morris for bending, not breaking, on that side of the ball.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Revisiting the 49ers schedule after 4 weeks: Does the back half look easier or harder now?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are 4-0 through four weeks, as they’ve navigated the early part of their schedule well with notable wins over the Los Angeles Rams and Denver Broncos. Now, in Week 5, they get the Seattle Seahawks on the road in their most difficult matchup yet, and one that has given San Francisco […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are 4-0 through four weeks, as they’ve navigated the early part of their schedule well with notable wins over the Los Angeles Rams and Denver Broncos. Now, in Week 5, they get the Seattle Seahawks on the road in their most difficult matchup yet, and one that has given San Francisco fits in recent years. Through four weeks, we’ve learned a lot in the NFL, with some teams exceeding expectations, while others have struggled. While there’s definitely room for change over the course of the season, we’re starting to see what teams look like in 2026. So, it’s a good time to revisit San Francisco’s schedule, which was perceived to be especially hard over the final weeks of the year. Let’s go week-by-week and assess the matchup for the rest of the season. Week 5: @ Seattle Seahawks (3-1) Despite dealing with an injury to Sam Darnold for a few weeks, the Seahawks are 3-1, with their lone loss coming to the Washington Commanders in a 33-31 road loss with Darnold healthy. The Seahawks defense has been quite good, as expected under Mike McDaniel, and the main question stemming from last year is their run game without Kenneth Walker. This will be a challenge, and one that will be telling for the 49ers offense after their hot start. Week 6: vs. Washington Commanders (1-3) The Commanders have lost to the Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys, and Indianapolis Colts, while beating the Seahawks in a close game with Marcus Mariota. They’ve been all over the place. Washington’s offensive line was hit with injuries, and Jayden Daniels has missed two games now and could be back for Week 6. They played the Eagles very close, but Philly doesn’t look good. They were blown out, though, by the Cowboys and Colts, and are probably trending down compared to preseason expectations. Still, there’s a bit of unknown with this team, as we haven’t seen Daniels healthy for enough time to get a sense of their offense. Week 7: @ Atlanta Falcons (2-2) The Falcons are 2-2, with both wins coming after Michael Penix was inserted into the starting lineup. They’ve blown out the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints and are definitely trending up heading into Week 3. Atlanta’s defense, especially against the run, where they’re No. 1 in EPA allowed per play, has impressed, despite missing some key edge rushers. Kevin Stefanski has done a really good job of making things easy for Penix by getting the ball out quickly, and Bijan Robinson is just a different runner. This game could sneakily give the 49ers some problems on the ground with their run defense, making it a tougher matchup than expected. But I do think this could be a good matchup for the 49ers defense, which has done well keeping the ball in front of them when quarterbacks get it out quickly this season. Week 8: BYE WEEK Week 9: vs. Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) Talk about improvements. The Raiders have been one of the NFL’s pleasant surprises behind Klint Kubiak and Kirk Cousins. Now, they’ve beaten the Miami Dolphins, New Orleans Saints, and Los Angeles Chargers. But they did come back late to play the Kansas City Chiefs close in Week 4 in a 30-27 loss. The Raiders defense has done quite well against both the run and the pass, ranking second in EPA allowed per play behind only the Minnesota Vikings. Their passing offense has looked solid as well, especially with Brock Bowers in the lineup, although Ashton Jeanty and the run game have struggled with efficiency. Vegas plays the Patriots, Bills, and Rams over the next three weeks ahead of their matchup with the 49ers, so we’ll get a clearer picture of how they are against tough opponents, but they’ve looked better than expected so far this season. Week 10: @ Dallas Cowboys (2-2) It’s a very similar story with the Cowboys, who have the second-most points in the NFL and a defense that ranks dead last (by a considerable margin) in EPA allowed per dropback and 31st, behind only the Detroit Lions in EPA allowed per play. Dallas’s offense has really been clicking, with Dak Prescott looking like a dark-horse MVP candidate once again, and the Cowboys just beat the Houston Texans on the road 34-30. Dallas had a close 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio as well. This will be a big test for Raheem Morris and could be a fun midseason shootout. So far, the Cowboys look just as expected. Week 11: @ Minnesota Vikings (4-0) The 49ers will face the Vikings on the road in Week 11, taking on one of the other two currently undefeated teams in the NFL. Minnesota’s offense has not looked pretty under Kyler Murray, and they had to go to Carson Wentz briefly when Murray suffered a concussion. Their offense is 28th in EPA per play, as they’ve been a bottom-half rush and pass offense. But Murray is still figuring things out, and the Vikings have had the best defense in the league through four games with a lot of ascending young talent. They’ve also yet to be really tested. They’ve faced the Packers, Bears (in a storm game), Buccaneers, and Dolphins. So, we’re in wait-and-see mode on whether this team will be well-rounded come midseason or if they waver off. Week 12: vs. Seattle Seahawks (3-1) This one could be one of the tougher matchups of the year for the 49ers, even at home. The Seahawks will be in midseason form and should have Jadarian Price back as they try to figure out their run game issues on offense. These three games also start a grueling stretch for the 49ers to end the year. Week 13: @ New York Giants The Giants were expected to be a sneaky good team in 2026 under John Harbaugh, and showed some of that life in Week 1 with a 28-20 upset over the Dallas Cowboys. New York is still 3-1 through four weeks, but they’ve since beaten the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals, while losing 28-6 to the Los Angeles Rams. They’re also without Jaxson Dart and could be on to J.J. McCarthy by this point. The Giants are 22nd in EPA per play offensively and 20th in EPA allowed per play defensively. Now, they still have a ton of winnable matchups between Weeks 5 and 13, so they could very well still be a playoff contender come this time. But their quarterback situation isn’t desirable after Dart’s injury. Week 14: vs. Los Angeles Rams (2-2) This one will also be more indicative of a playoff environment, just like Week 12 against the Seahawks in a crucial division game. The Rams have looked good offensively since their subpar Week 1 performance, ranking 10th in EPA per play over the last three weeks. They blew out the Giants in Week 2, lost to the Broncos 30-26 in Week 3, and just came back to beat the Eagles 24-20 on the road. They’ve ranked second in EPA allowed per play defensively since Week 2 as well, and will be a tough out. That could also be a time when their veterans on defense are all settled in, making it a tougher matchup. Week 15: @ Los Angeles Chargers (0-4) Talk about disappointment. The Chargers have really struggled through four weeks. They look broken on offense with a bad offensive line. And while their defense is eighth in EPA allowed per play, they’ve lost by at least a touchdown in all four of their games. And things don’t get any easier for the Chargers coming up with their brutal schedule. This team could look a lot different come Week 15. They’re definitely on the worse-than-expected side. Week 16: @ Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) The Chiefs are the only other undefeated team. They were expected to bounce back after Patrick Mahomes’s ACL tear, but have even exceeded expectations on that front so far. Kenneth Walker has invigorated their offense. The Chiefs are fourth in EPA per play and third in rushing success rate. They’ve beaten the Broncos, Colts, Dolphins, and Raiders. Mahomes has looked good. And the Chiefs are always a tough out. This will be a tough challenge in Arrowhead Stadium. Week 17: vs. Philadelphia Eagles (2-2) Things are falling apart in Philly. They’ve had questionable quarterback play. A…
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: The 49ers proved that good teams can win ugly
summary: As we approach a big Week 5 showdown against the Seattle Seahawks, let’s take a final look at the San Francisco 49ers’ 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos. It took a bit, but the 49ers finally took control after a special teams play and then put things away with a big play from George Kittle. […]
full_text: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we approach a big Week 5 showdown against the Seattle Seahawks, let’s take a final look at the San Francisco 49ers’ 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos. It took a bit, but the 49ers finally took control after a special teams play and then put things away with a big play from George Kittle. Denver’s defense was as advertised, but the game turned with a couple of injuries in the Denver secondary that aided a big fourth quarter from the San Francisco offense. But the good news is, we learned something important from the 49ers: Good teams can win ugly If we were to rank the 49ers’ wins from best-looking win to ugliest, I think the obvious order is: at Rams versus Dolphins versus Cardinals versus Broncos But we learned the most about the 2026 49ers on Sunday against Denver. You don’t learn much with a blowout against a team like Miami, but against a team like the Broncos, there’s plenty to learn, and on Sunday we learned the 49ers can win ugly. For three weeks, everything has worked perfectly for the 49ers. The offense scored at least 27 points in each of the first three games of the season, and was held without a touchdown in just three of the 12 quarters. The defense held their end of the bargain as well, allowing 13 or fewer points in two of those games. On Sunday, the defense held Denver to only 14 points, but the offense was held without a touchdown the first two quarters, and was 4:15 away from a third. It wasn’t the type of game we’ve gotten used to so far this season from the offense and it felt like there was real struggle. Maybe it was the lack of receivers with Mike Evans leading the charge nowhere near 100 percent health. Maybe it was a sign of just how good the Broncos defense is (and maybe not coincidentally the offense started to work with Patrick Surtain and Riley Moss out). But not every win is going to walk in the park like Weeks 1 and 2. Good teams like Denver will make you earn wins, and in what was the 49ers first real test of 2026, San Francisco proved they can win ugly. An all-time revenge game Revenge games have lost a little bit of meaning in recent years with how much player movement there is now. But every so often there’s a revenge game that has a personal aspect to it so there’s a little more juice to it. That’s exactly what Dre Greenlaw went through on Sunday and he backed up his talk with his performance against his former team. It wasn’t exactly a secret that Greenlaw didn’t enjoy his time with Denver with Sean Payton being the main reason. If you didn’t know about that beef, Greenlaw made it known pretty quickly. With Denver facing a first-and-15 inside its own 10-yard-line, Bo Nix checked down to RJ Harvey, with Greenlaw making the tackle. After the play, Greenlaw pointed at the Denver head coach and the two exchanged words. But Greenlaw put that emotion into his play, leading the 49ers with 12 total tackles and seven solo tackles. If PFF grades are your thing, Greenlaw finished with the fourth-highest defensive grade at 68.2 with a team-high six stops. Greenlaw then closed his day by politely telling Payton to leave his field. Sunday was an emotional game for Greenlaw, and he more than came through for the 49ers defense. Play of the week With limited options, one play stands out as this week’s play of the week and surprisingly enough, it comes from Siran Neal: SIRAN NEAL WITH THE RECOVERY‼️ 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/WFqXRfNQB6 — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) October 4, 2026 I mean, what a play from Neal. For a blink, it looked like Marvin Mims shook off Neal but a second effort from the specialist was just enough for Neal to grab Mims’ ankle. The 49ers benefitted from a technicality in the rule book where the wrist counts as the hand and Mims’ wrist hitting the ground was just enough to free the ball and allow Neal to recover. The 49ers’ longest offensive drive by time up to that point was its opening drive that lasted 4:38 but resulted in a punt. On the drive following Neal’s forced fumble, the offense took 5:25 off the clock, and most importantly scored its first touchdown of the game. 21 of San Francisco’s 24 points came after the fumble. After so many times of seeing the 49ers suffer from a game-changing special teams play, it’s nice to see the Niners be the beneficiary of one.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: ‘As good as it gets’ – 49ers’ ascending position group faces its toughest test
summary: One of the most exciting developments of the 49ers’ 4-0 start to the 2026 season has been the play of the offensive line. A much, and often unfairly, maligned position group for the Niners, Chris Foerster’s group have excelled through the opening four weeks. They have not allowed a sack through the first four games, […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 17: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers drops back to pass during the first quarter of an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the most exciting developments of the 49ers’ 4-0 start to the 2026 season has been the play of the offensive line. A much, and often unfairly, maligned position group for the Niners, Chris Foerster’s group have excelled through the opening four weeks. They have not allowed a sack through the first four games, with the 49ers the first team to achieve that feat since the 2005 Indianapolis Colts. Per Pro Football Reference , the 49ers have allowed a pressure rate of just 13 percent, the best in the NFL. San Francisco was 10th in the league (19.5%) last year The Niners’ O-Line was on an upward trajectory last season, and it is obviously no surprise that future Hall of Fame left tackle Trent Williams is playing at a high level. Right tackle Colton McKivitz enjoyed the best season of his career last term and has established himself as one of the better starters at that spot in the NFL. Brock Purdy’s pocket presence and mobility have also contributed to the Niners’ success in keeping him clean to this point. However, the biggest surprise surrounding the play of the 49ers’ O-Line so far is the performance of the players on the interior. Center Jake Brendel is a player who has previously received more criticism than his play on the field merited, but the big questions up front going into the season concerned the two guard spots. With right guard Dominick Puni having played through the lingering effects of a knee injury in 2025 and the 49ers seemingly lacking a convincing option on the left side next to Williams. Connor Colby has been doing some excellent work at the second level in the run game. pic.twitter.com/q7Wyxn9Erb — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 8, 2026 But left guard Connor Colby has made that role his own through the first four games. While he can still be considered the weak link from a pass protection perspective, Colby has more than held his own and has shown considerable prowess as a run blocker, particularly when climbing to the second level blocking for zone runs. Superb pass pro from Colby helps Purdy get to his third read. Eight-yard gain gets 49ers into third-and-short on the Kittle TD drive. pic.twitter.com/9OxJwwMXz1 — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 8, 2026 Puni, meanwhile, has delivered performances that have served as a reminder of why the 49ers were so excited about him coming off his rookie season in 2024. He has given up four pressures in 231 pass-blocking snaps, per Pro Football Focus ( h/t Al Sacco ), with his resurgence and the emergence of Colby fortifying what was seen as one of the most significant weaknesses on the 49er roster. But the interior offensive line will receive its sternest test of the season so far when San Francisco travels north to face the Seattle Seahawks and their ferocious defensive front. Dominick Puni! And Brock Purdy, obviously. pic.twitter.com/B7hWbhPSjV — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 8, 2026 The Seahawks are fifth in the league in pressure rate (30.9%), per PFR, with their imposing starting three-man front of Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II and Jarran Reed supplemented by the likes of Uchenna Nwosu, Demarcus Lawrence and Derick Hall rushing off the edge. That group has once again played a critical role in the defending Super Bowl champions maintaining their dominant defensive form of last season. The Seahawks rank fourth in the NFL on defense in by EPA per play and second by success rate. For as much as they are fearsome unit to throw the ball against, they arguably make life even tougher for the ground game. Indeed, the Seahawks have allowed a rushing success rate of just 30% this season, the third-best in the league. In short, Puni and Colby will have their work cut out for them to maintain their stellar play in pass protection and open holes in the run game. Speaking at his press conference on Wednesday, head coach Kyle Shanahan detailed the challenge facing his O-Line. Asked about the task of taking on the Seahawks’ interior D-Line, Shanahan said: “They’re as good as it gets. Just individually, I think [Seattle Seahawks DL] Leonard Williams is second to none just in how good of a player he’s been here over the last few years and still is. Then just how deep they are. There’s not one guy out there who’s not a good player. They roll them, so they play like overachievers because of how hard they go. They play with their hair on fire, but they’re definitely more than that because they’re very talented. It starts with Leonard, but down the line, even outside with [Seattle Seahawks LB DeMarcus] Lawrence, who’s been good for so long. They’ve got a real good group.” Getting through the win over the Denver Broncos and their formidable defense with the clean sheet of sacks allowed still intact was a huge feather in the cap for the 49ers and their O-Line. But the difficulty level ratchets up against the Seahawks in the toughest road environment in football, in what will be the first ‘true’ road game the 49ers have played this season. It’s unrealistic to expect the 49ers to prevent Seattle from getting to Purdy at all on Sunday, but, if they can limit the damage and lay the foundation for an offensive performance that delivers a victory, it will send a message that the Niners have rectified a chink in their armor as they push to contend for the Super Bowl in 2026.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Kyle Shanahan shares interesting perspective on 49ers unique drafting strategy for their OL
summary: When it comes to the NFL Draft, the San Francisco 49ers are often a team in many conversations during the offseason, with this year being no different after they took wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling at No. 33 and running back Kaelon Black at No. 90 overall. San Francisco has seen its wide range of successes […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Colton McKivitz #68 and Dominick Puni #77 of the San Francisco 49ers block during the game against the Miami Dolphins at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Dolphins 35-13. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images When it comes to the NFL Draft, the San Francisco 49ers are often a team in many conversations during the offseason, with this year being no different after they took wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling at No. 33 and running back Kaelon Black at No. 90 overall. San Francisco has seen its wide range of successes and misses in the draft under head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch, finding hits with some of their mid-round and late-round targets, while sometimes struggling with their early-round picks. The 49ers have been scrutinized in the draft ever since they took quarterback Trey Lance with the No. 3 overall pick in 2021. Their draft classes in 2022 and 2023 were quite poor, set aside the massive hit of Brock Purdy, while their 2024 and 2025 classes are yet to be determined. One position the 49ers haven’t prioritized as much in the early rounds of the draft is the offensive line. The 49ers have taken an offensive lineman just once in the first round under Shanahan: Mike McGlinchey back in 2018. Other than that, they’ve rarely spent a first or second-round pick on an offensive lineman, with Aaron Banks being the only other guy. Instead, they’ve acquired or developed their linemen in a different way. Just look at their current starters. Trent Williams was acquired via trade. Connor Colby was a seventh-round pick in 2025. Jake Brendel signed a reserve/future contract with San Francisco back in 2020 after being cut and developed into the starting center. Dominick Puni was a third-round pick. And Colton McKivitz was a fifth-round pick who got cut after his rookie year. However, the 49ers are currently seeing some of the best offensive line play in the NFL this year after sporting a top-10 unit in 2025. Why have they embarked on this path with their offensive line selection in the draft, and why has it worked? Head coach Kyle Shanahan shared some perspective with NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco last week, and it starts with offensive line coach Chris Foerster. “I definitely do [have a lot of confidence in Chris Foerster developing players for our scheme], ” Shanahan said. “Chris is as good a coach as there is, as good a coach as I’ve been around. He was one of the most important guys even when I came here. I tried to get him right away and couldn’t. But Chris, he’s a stud, and I trust him with so many people. However, the biggest part of the puzzle is actually finding scheme fits for the 49ers offense, which is where a lot of the team’s draft strategy for offensive linemen come into play. “But it doesn’t just mean that, hey, give him whatever and he’s going to turn them into stuff. You got to get the right guys. He’s really good at helping us find those right guys. Our personnel department is really good at helping us find those right guys. You don’t just say, ‘hey, we like the later-round guys.’ There’s got to be a certain type of guy that you believe in who can do it. But also, I want to say we have a philosophy that, hey, we’re not going to draft guys early. We just try to take who we think the best player is for our team. “And I think it’s really hard with O-linemen because last year there was an O-lineman I loved [in the 2026 NFL Draft]. He wasn’t there at 27. And a lot of guys you love at O-Line rarely get past 15 if they’re really legit, that guy. And then when you get to a certain draft pick, yeah, this might be the best guy available at 27, but how different is he than the guy that you know will be available in the third round? And yeah, if we had to pick now, we’ll take that take that guy at 27. But man, Chris, myself, some personnel guys, we think that guy in the third round might be this close to being as good as them. So why would we do that when we can go get a guy who can rush the quarterback, a guy who can touch the football? But if you can find that guy in the third round, then that guy might be the best pick then.” Interestingly, Shanahan believes that’s where a lot of the NFL can fail, as they choose to go the safer route in the draft and draft offensive linemen unnecessarily. “So by no means do we go into it and say, hey, it’s just our philosophy not to take those guys. But we don’t just take them to take them. And I do think one thing I’ve noticed a lot in this league: I think a lot of people just take O-linemen to take them. It’s one of the safest things to do. You take an O-lineman, and very rarely are you going to get questioned. Very rarely do they turn and bust, even if they’re just an average guy. A guy who’s in the first round who plays like a 4th-round guy but still plays like a starter, there’s not that much difference. “Now, it’s hard to find a starter, 1st-round, 4th-round, whatever, but there’s not that big of a difference level until you find like a Pro Bowl type dude. And if it’s a Pro Bowl type dude, hell yeah, that guy’s so worth it. That guy’s going to be so much different than a guy later, but that’s not always the case. And so you don’t want to just stockpile these O-linemen when you feel like you can find people later. I also think that’s why we’ve gotten a lot of players and not always just in the first round or anything like that, but that’s what allows you to add pass rushers. That’s what allows you to get some guys that I think can touch the ball and score touchdowns.” After years of scrutiny and warranted criticism for their strategy, San Francisco’s offensive line is currently playing at a very high level, as they’ve had continuity everywhere but at left guard from 2025. But it’s interesting to see Shanahan’s perspective on offensive linemen and why the 49ers differ from a lot of other teams on strategy.

title: Buccaneers Week 5 Top Performers at Dallas Cowboys
summary: The Buccaneers came into Thursday Night Football facing long odds on the road and improbably secured their first victory of 2026 with a 24-16 win over the Dallas Cowboys. It almost crumbled into disaster late, with the Bucs forgoing a chance at a 3-score lead that nearly bit them you-know-where, but they benefitted from just […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 08: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys during the third quarter of the game at AT&T Stadium on October 08, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buccaneers came into Thursday Night Football facing long odds on the road and improbably secured their first victory of 2026 with a 24-16 win over the Dallas Cowboys. It almost crumbled into disaster late, with the Bucs forgoing a chance at a 3-score lead that nearly bit them you-know-where, but they benefitted from just enough luck to hold on. The defense showed it might indeed be above average after weeks of stifling lesser offenses, which was encouraging outside of the near-collapse toward the end. The offense took advantage of a horrific Dallas defense, as Jalon Daniels played clean and Bucky Irving wrecked house with a career high in yardage. There were still far too many coaching miscues and self-inflicted mistakes, but a win is a win. Now the team has a mini-bye to rest up and continue making tweaks. We’ll see where it goes from here, but let’s do some victory shoutouts. Offensive Top Performer: RB Bucky Irving Bucky Irving recorded his best game in more than a year and his highest yardage total ever, as he carried the rock 21 times for 165 yards and a score. That total included an electrifying 72-yard jaunt that sparked the Bucs’ offense in the second half as well as the game-clinching 22-yard run. He also added 2 catches for 10 yards an additional touchdown to lead the offense to its best output since Week 1. Nasty jump cut and vision by Bucky Irving pic.twitter.com/fWUxwEQLtt — Billy M (@BillyM_91) October 9, 2026 If the Bucs can run the ball more effectively like they did Thursday, their offense should be in a better place moving forward. Jalon Daniels played much more confidently and poised in his second start, on a short week no less, starting the game 8-for-8 and finishing 19-of-25 for 189 yards and a touchdown to go along with 7 rushes for 23 yards. He almost threw a back-breaking pick six that Dallas’s Daron Bland inexcusably dropped, but that was the only major blemish on an otherwise rock-solid night. Jalon Daniels was CUTTING UP against the Cowboys defense ALL NIGHT LONG: • 19/25 (76% completion percentage) • 189 passing yards • 23 rushing yards • 1 passing TD • 110.2 passer rating The Buccaneers rookie QB PUT ON A SHOW vs the Cowboys in a primetime upset 😳🔥 pic.twitter.com/xv4fn0a473 — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) October 9, 2026 The offense did a better job of getting the ball to its premier targets as well, as Emeka Egbuka recorded 6 catches for 38 yards and one carry for 14 yards and a touchdown. Incremental improvements, I suppose. Defensive Top Performer: CB Jacob Parrish The defense faced a daunting task against a top-5 offense that just dismantled a vaunted Houston defense last week, and it did a mostly standup job of taking the punches. It looked dicey after an opening-drive touchdown, and again with a 99-yard march in the fourth quarter, but the in-between was encouraging. The secondary capped CeeDee Lamb, who just went off for 17 catches and nearly 175 yards on Sunday, by holding him to just 2 catches for 9 yards. The man to lead that charge? Jacob Parrish once again. He recorded a game-high four pass breakups, constantly harassing Cowboys pass catchers despite consistently getting put in disadvantageous positions with Todd Bowles’s zone-heavy scheme. He’s been a stud all season, now currently sitting at top 3 in the NFL for passes defensed. The pass rush actually looked alive, consistently pressuring Dak Prescott and getting him uncomfortable despite failing to record a sack. Per SumerSports, the Bucs recorded a 2.31-second average time-to-pressure, which was top 5 for any team this season. Tykee Smith thrived all night, converting 5 of his 7 blitzing opportunities into pressures — along with 2 quarterback hits — to lead the team. David Walker also cooked with his opportunities to run as the looper on multiple blitzes, and he even tipped a pass that led to a Yaya Diaby interception. A lot happening here but David Walker gets the main credit for this interception happening, Watch him tip that ball. pic.twitter.com/GI445DcdL8 — Logan B. Robinson (@LogansTwitty) October 9, 2026 And of course, we need to give Alex Anzalone some credit for actually holding onto the game-clinching interception that caromed off tight end Jake Ferguson. Anzalone was not very good overall but credit where credit is due on killing Dallas’s final drive. Alex Anzalone seals an improbable win for the #Bucs , one they absolutely had to have. Their first one. pic.twitter.com/rx7vy83kMT — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 9, 2026 Special Teams Top Performer: ST Miles Killebrew Hey, someone who isn’t Chase McLaughlin. The Buccaneers stared down one of the most dangerous return men in the league in KaVontae Turpin and needed to keep him contained, and special teams ace Miles Killebrew delivered with a massive forced fumble to set the offense up in position to secure an additional 3 points off the leg of McLaughlin. Killebrew was signed exclusively for this purpose so it’s nice to see that investment pay off. That was Turpin’s first fumble on a kick return ever, great time! Miles Killebrew forces a fumble for the first time since 2017 to give Tampa Bay the ball right back 👀 @TBvsDAL on Prime Video Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Jgo3rC0WSV — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) October 9, 2026

title: Week 5 Game Recap: Buccaneers shock Cowboys in upset
summary: First Quarter: The 0-4 Bucs, the 2-2 Dallas Cowboys, the Thursday night spotlight. Centerstage and ready to let up a score Tampa’s defense took the field. Dallas didn’t find last week’s 17-catch superstar, Ceedee Lamb, on their opening drive but they did find the end zone. Following two Buccaneer penalties inside of 10-yard line, Dallas […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 08: Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrates a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys during the second quarter of the game at AT&T Stadium on October 08, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images First Quarter: The 0-4 Bucs, the 2-2 Dallas Cowboys, the Thursday night spotlight. Centerstage and ready to let up a score Tampa’s defense took the field. Dallas didn’t find last week’s 17-catch superstar, Ceedee Lamb, on their opening drive but they did find the end zone. Following two Buccaneer penalties inside of 10-yard line, Dallas finally converted, handing the ball off and pushing Tampa’s front back across the goal line. 7-0, Dallas. Jalon Daniels, off of his first career start, took the field with a confident swagger. That boisterous posture flashed on the team’s first third down attempt when Daniels pulled the ball down and ran through a Dallas defender at the first down to move the chains. In a drive that was only the second of opening quarter and lasted for the entirety of that quarter, Daniels found a way to do what this team’s offense has consistently struggled to do all year— Spread the ball around. Second Quarter: Tampa’s first drive saw multiple receptions by both Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka, while still finding Cade Otton for his customary underneath completions. The Bucs also held the ball for 15 plays and over 10 minutes before finding six points and a tie game. In what was their longest drive since 2007, the Buccaneers reminded fans and maybe even themselves that they have playmakers, they have a good offensive line, and that they are capable of playing high level offensive football when all of those facets are working in harmony. Jalon Daniels started Thursday’s game 8-8, however, his second drive kicked off backed up, began with an incompletion and ended with punt. Dallas’ second punt of the game would follow, once again pinning Tampa inside of their own 10-yard line. The half ticked past its halfway point and the Bucs scooted across midfield briefly before an ugly penalty-laden sequence bounced them backwards. Tristan Wirfs got it underway with a false start on third and one which backed the Bucs up to a third and must pass. Their third and must pass led its way to a field goal— 61 yards away, but a field goal. Chase McLaughlin, groin hindrance or not, nailed the kick from 61. Bucs’ fans would soon see yellow on the field and find out the kick didn’t count. The Buccaneers were late in their decision making, forcing the special teams unit to take a delay of game— In turn, losing five yards and having to punt. The Buccaneers’ defense had shutout Dak Prescott and co., post their debut drive. The Cowboys’ final drive of the first half featured their first true down the field completion, a play where even though he had respectable positioning, Alex Anzalone wound up on a poster. Still, chunk play or not, Dallas only managed three points. 10-7, Cowboys. Third Quarter: With the ball first, lightening struck. The storm’s name— Bucky Irving. Irving ripped off an ankle breaking detonation. Tampa Bay segued what might be Irving’s greatest career highlight thus far into an Emeka Egbuka rushing touchdown to cap off a 90-yard touchdown drive. 14-10, Buccaneers. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are not a team that has not played anything close to complimentary football in 2026, but they gave the Cowboys a small dose of what that might look like. Dallas’ ensuing possession was thwarted by an unlikely foe— Yaya Diaby’s hands. Dropping into coverage, Diaby found a ball bouncing across the hands of defenders and receivers alike, until the pitter patter of the ball in flight landed softly in the waiting arms of Tampa Bay’s edge-rusher for his first career interception. Working in some of that complimentary football again, the Buccaneers’ offense took that turnover and turned it into points— Immediately, with the help of a Tez Johnson deep ball. Johnson’s defender was sat down as he lost his footing trying to run with Johnson down field. The Daniels—Johnson connection was the setup for another Bucky Irving splash, his second trip across the goal line in the game. Five plays, 75 yards, and a Bucky Irving touchdown run put the Bucs out in front by 11. 21-10, Tampa Bay. After touchdowns come kickoffs— A Kavonte Turpin fumble in this case, the first of his career. Miles Killebrew’s playmaking would give Tampa another drive and more points, by way of a Chase McLaughlin field goal. 24-10, Buccaneers. While the Cowboys’ would get to play offense after Chase McLaughlin’s next kickoff, it wouldn’t be for long— A quick four out. Fourth Quarter: The fourth quarter (and much of the second half) belonged to Tampa’s offensive line. Once again, Dallas’ front was mauled into a 10+ play drive that moved the Bucs all the way down to the one-yard line where Tampa’s historically conservative head coach made a decision that was definitely a decision — Turning away a chip shot field goal and a three-score lead for a fourth down conversion attempt. That attempt would be a failed one and directly transitioned into a 99-yard touchdown drive for the Cowboys, no two-point conversion though. 24-18, Buccaneers. Two-minute warning, 34 yards from the game-evening two-point conversion attempt, and Dak Prescott found his second Tampa Bay defender. Perhaps an even more unlikely set of hands, as Prescott found Alex Anzalone—Tampa Bay’s most embattled defender through the first month of the 2026 season. Bucs win— A shocking upset, a performance to be proud of.

full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans gestures during the first quarter of the game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images On paper, it appears the Tennessee Titans have a winnable game versus the Houston Texans in Week 5 . Both AFC South teams are 0-4. Despite that, the Texans are considered heavy favorites despite the showdown being contested at Nissan Stadium. Both organizations found themselves in familiar territory last season. They entered their first matchup (Week 4) sharing 0-3 records. This was the first game then-Titans HC Brian Callahan lost play-calling duties. The Texans enjoyed a dominant 26-0 win. Hopefully Sunday doesn’t repeat that result. That victory jumpstarted a Texans turnaround. They finished 12-5 and qualified for the playoffs. The Texans hope this is another get-right game versus the Titans. The Texans lost two high-scoring affairs with the Buffalo Bills and Dallas Cowboys. They were disappointing in losses to the Cincinnati Bengals and Indianapolis Colts. It’s worth noting star receiver Nico Collins missed the Bengals and Colts games. They are averaging 30 PPG with Collins in the lineup. The Texans lost two shootouts with the high-octane Bills and Cowboys. The Bengals are another postseason contender. They’ve faced a pretty tough schedule so far. The Titans are unfortunately nowhere near as difficult of a matchup on paper. The Texans have had a surprising amount of issues on defense. Head coach DeMeco Ryans recently announced he’s taking defensive play-calling duties back from coordinator Matt Burke. That’s probably bad news for this Titans offense. Nobody knows the Texans defense better than Coach Ryans does. Brian Daboll’s offense found something between Cam Ward and Carnell Tate in Week 4. CeeDee Lamb torched this Texans secondary on that same afternoon. The Titans need to move Tate around the formation, and target him 10+ times on Sunday. The Titans-Texans rivalry lives on, especially after the rebranding followed Oilers themes. Owner Amy Adams Strunk will be paying close attention to Sunday’s result. Hopefully the Titans make it a competitive game.

title: Commanders Q+A: Five questions needing answers before Giants clash
summary: It’s only Week 5, but the Commanders are encroaching on must-win territory. Yeah, that sounds a bit extreme for October, but Washington simply can’t afford to fall to 1-4 on the season and 0-3 within the NFC East so early.   There are fair complaints to be made about the early-season schedule and a buzzard’s […]
full_text: It’s only Week 5, but the Commanders are encroaching on must-win territory. Yeah, that sounds a bit extreme for October, but Washington simply can’t afford to fall to 1-4 on the season and 0-3 within the NFC East so early. There are fair complaints to be made about the early-season schedule and a buzzard’s luck when it comes to injuries , but this is the hand Washington was dealt. While the injury report is a million miles long and features some star power, franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels is expected back for Sunday’s game against the New York Giants, sporting a brace to protect his left elbow following a Week 2 dislocation that kept him out the last two games. That’s a real plus, especially after Athan Kaliakmanis was forced into action versus Indianapolis following Marcus Mariota’s sprained MCL . They’ll need a big performance from Daniels and a few others to best the resurgent Giants, who have started this season with a 3-1 record. The Commanders won their last (and only) contest at Northwest Stadium. Can they do it again? The answers to these five questions will be key in deciding the outcome. As we do each week, I’ll ask the questions and you all provide the answers in the comments section below. Then we’ll post the best responses in the article itself on Friday morning. Let us know what you think: Question 1 : Do you think Jayden Daniels will be impacted by the elbow brace? If so, how will it affect him? If not, why not? Question 2: Who needs to step up in the passing game if WRs Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs can’t go? Question 3: Who scares you on the Giants defense? Which guy simply must get shut down for the offense to have a productive day? Question 4: Who should be taking most of the Commanders carries on Sunday and how many should he get? Question 5: Asked this one last week but I like it, so here it goes again. Who will be the Commanders unsung hero if they win? Which guys needs to step up on a big way on Sunday?

full_text: Commanders right guard Sam Cosmi didn’t make the trip to London for that Week 4 contest against the Indianapolis Colts. He was in the concussion protocol and ruled out early in the week while recovering from a vicious hit delivered by his own teammate, when running back Kaytron Allen inadvertently ran into him. Missing one of the NFL’s best guards was an issue in the running game especially, with rookie Matt Gulbin struggling as his replacement. Cosmi was a full participant in Thursday’s practice and spoke to the media afterward, signaling what should be considered a high probability that he’ll play. That would be a huge boon for the Commanders, who need stability and quality working for them up front. Cosmi talked about the scary concussion this season in an interview with 7News reporter Scott Abraham, especially after he suffered one last year . Sam Cosmi is back and ready to go. title: Commanders roster moves: Sixth-round NFL draft pick Kaytron Allen waived
summary: The Commanders have waived rookie running back Kaytron Allen.   That was a surprise move even with Jeremy McNichols practicing again (while on IR) and Austin Ekeler now on the roster, considering how much the Commanders liked the Penn State product.   The team announced the transaction on Thursday afternoon.   The Commanders drafted Allen […]
full_text: The Commanders have waived rookie running back Kaytron Allen . That was a surprise move even with Jeremy McNichols practicing again (while on IR) and Austin Ekeler now on the roster , considering how much the Commanders liked the Penn State product. The team announced the transaction on Thursday afternoon. The Commanders drafted Allen in the sixth-round out of Penn State, where he set school rushing records . He was a popular player among the fan base, with a preferred nickname of ‘Fatman,’ and a physical rushing style that was thought to play well in short-yardage situations. The running game hasn’t been productive to this point, which isn’t all on the backs. Jacory Croskey-Merritt hasn’t been efficient running the ball. Rachaad White was running well before suffering a shoulder injury. Ekeler’s back in the mix and McNichols just had his 21-day practice window opened this week. Allen was expected to make an immediate impact and looked good during the summer and was thought to have an active role in the rushing game, though that outlook has changed with the personnel available. The running back room was getting crowded and Allen was an odd man out, though the Commanders will probably try to sign him to the practice squad, but there’s no guarantee that he’ll clear waivers. Seattle signed Robert Henry Jr. off the practice squad, where Craig Reynolds still resides. It’s hard to imagine the Commanders giving up on Allen, even as a lower-round draft pick. Time will tell if he’s able to get to the practice squad. All it takes is one team that liked him in the draft to sign him to their active roster. Please check back for updates on this developing story.

summary: The Washington Commanders are preparing to host the New York Giants and their coordinators spoke with reporters before Thursday’s practice. full_text: The Washington Commanders are preparing to host the New York Giants and their coordinators spoke with reporters before Thursday’s practice. David Blough was up first, and he was asked about the failed 4th down play vs the Colts. He mentioned execution from the coaches to the players, and he said they didn’t play winning football on offense. Blough was also asked about Nick Allegretti getting replaced by free agent signing Lucas Patrick at center, then by rookie Matt Gulbin at right guard. He said the coaching staff is transparent with all the players, but didn’t actually answer the question about the apparent demotions. Dan Quinn mentioned injuries, and Allegretti did miss most of training camp, and was limited last week with a hip injury, but it’s clear that Allegretti isn’t one of the best 5 on the offensive line right now. Jayden Daniels is returning this week and Blough said he’s ready to go, and they’re happy to have him back. There are no limitations, and if you need more confirmation that Jayden Daniels is starting this week, Adam Schefter tweeted it out! Blough said that 7th-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis will continue to develop as he remains QB2, this week backing up Daniels. AK16 got more playing time than most people outside of his immediate circle of friends and family wanted to see him get as a rookie, but he showed enough to not force the team to bring in another QB. Blough and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones were both asked about Dan Quinn’s leadership and dealing with losing games and players to injury. They both praised Quinn’s leadership, and ability to stay consistent through wins and losses. Jones implied that previous coaches he’s worked with weren’t as even keel when dealing with adversity. title: Commanders News: The demise of the Nick Sirianni era may be exaggerated
summary: The Daily Slop – 8 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Post (paywall) […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 8 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Post (paywall) An offensive line in flux and more X-factors for Commanders vs. Giants Losing right guard Sam Cosmi to a concussion in Week 2 created a domino effect for Washington’s offensive line. Nick Allegretti, who started the first two games at center, slid over to right guard to replace Cosmi. In his place, Lucas Patrick — who only signed with the team three weeks ago — started at center. Then Allegretti was benched and replaced by Matt Gulbin at right guard. Quinn said that wasn’t a permanent decision — and highlighted that Allegretti had been nursing a hip injury — but it was performance-based, nonetheless. Cosmi returned to practice Wednesday wearing a noncontact jersey. If he plays Sunday, that still leaves the Commanders with a decision at center. There are three options: Stick with Patrick, go back to Allegretti or give Gulbin a shot. Given how poorly Gulbin played last week, he feels like the least likely option. Patrick, meanwhile, has outplayed Allegretti — particularly in pass protection. Allegretti has allowed a pressure rate of 7.8 percent (146th among offensive linemen with at least 50 pass blocking snaps according to the analytics platform TruMedia). In comparison, Patrick has given up a pressure rate of just 2.7 percent (36th). To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) The 5 NFL teams most impacted by injuries in 2026, with the New York Giants at the top We are not simply looking at which team has been hit with the most injuries; positions factor in greatly, as does the expected timeline of the absence. How expectations have changed is also a big part of it. For example, De’Von Achane is a great player, but he plays running back on a Miami Dolphins team that was one of the worst in the NFL with him, and remains one of the worst without him. 5. Washington Commanders: We aren’t just going by quantity for this list but the Commanders’ Wednesday injury report had 23 players on it , [ BiB : To be fair, only 17 were limited or DNP; the other 6 practiced in full but were listed because they’d been on the Week 4 report ] with 11 limited participants and six players who did not participate. They lost Daniels (again) for the short term in Week 2, then lost backup quarterback Marcus Mariota a couple of weeks later. For a team that was in the conference championship game a couple of years ago and is breaking in two new coordinators, injuries to this extent are a big hurdle. 1. New York Giants: The Giants are the only team that has lost their starting quarterback for the season, which almost automatically puts them in the top spot. New York is 3-1, which is a pretty place to be heading into Week 5, but the team’s ceiling in 2026 is greatly reduced with Jameis Winston or J.J. McCarthy compared to what it would [have been] with Jaxson Dart. Dart’s season-ending knee injury could also have residual effects on the franchise beyond this season. Losing Brian Burns for the season just cements the Giants in the top spot. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN Commanders’ Jayden Daniels fully practices; expected to play on Sunday Daniels will wear a brace that will keep his left elbow slightly bent, with the idea that it can prevent another dislocation. During the portion of practice open to the media, Daniels took snaps from center Lucas Patrick in warmups and threw with more zip than last week. In other drills, a coach, kneeling, would hand the ball to Daniels, who took it with both hands and would pitch it to a running back. Quinn said they would incorporate drills in practice to help him roll to the ground the way a running back would when clasping the ball. But when asked if he’d run the same as in the past, [Daniels] responded, “Is it the fourth quarter? If it’s the fourth quarter, we’ve got to do something to win, right?” He later said, “There’s ways you could talk about different ways of protecting myself. But I don’t, I don’t get hit in practice, so I wouldn’t know till Sunday.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable 3 key matchups to watch when Giants visit Commanders on Sunday Washington’s Secondary vs. a Giants Offense Sorting Out Its QB Room After weeks of getting torched through the air — surrendering a league-high seven touchdown passes in the first two games — the Commanders’ secondary had its best showing of the season in London. The defense held the Colts to 257 total yards and forced two turnovers. It wasn’t dominant, but the improvement was real, and the timing matters heading into a matchup where Washington’s back end should have every advantage. Jameis Winston will be New York’s starter, and he’s everything you’d expect: experienced, capable of making smart throws, and prone to the kind of turnover-generating decision that keeps defensive coordinators up at night. Meanwhile, John Harbaugh has officially listed J.J. McCarthy as the backup, with the coaching staff noting his promotion is “definitely on the table.” Neither quarterback inspires fear heading into this game, even after getting blown out by McCarthy last season. Washington’s corners need to carry the momentum from London into this one. title: Washington Commanders versus Giants Week 5: Inside the Matchup
summary: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates […]
full_text: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026. From John Portis: The Washington Commanders have returned from London for a Week 5 matchup at home versus the New York Giants. New Giants head coach John Harbaugh and the Giants come into the game with a 3-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East, while the Commanders are carrying a 1-3 record after their loss to the Colts. New York has only played one road game so far and drew easy matchups the last two weeks, yet only narrowly defeated both the Titans ( 12-7) and the Cardinals ( 36-24 ), with Deonte Banks securing a pick-six on the Giants’ own 5-yard line to ensure the win in Arizona, and earn NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors . PICK SIX TO SEAL THE GAME! 🤯 Deonte Banks intercepts Jacoby Brissett and takes it to the house to secure the win for the Giants pic.twitter.com/xlEssRkJcq — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 4, 2026 Through the first four weeks of the season, the Washington Commanders haven’t looked the same for two games in a row, owing in large part to injuries and lineup changes. Three different quarterbacks have finished the first four games. The result has been a team that is rated fair to terrible in most statistical categories . The team will look for more consistency and improved play with the expected return of franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels, who will wear a brace on his left elbow moving forward. What impact, if any, this will have on Jayden’s performance remains to be seen. For what it is worth, the quarterback does not expect it to be an issue. The Commanders also hope to get Sam Cosmi back from a concussion he sustained in Week 2, and his presence could solidify an offensive line that has had a number of issues. Currently, the Commanders offensive line ranks dead last in run-block win rate but a solid 9th in composite pass protection. An ineffective run game has limited what David Blough wants to do on offense, but improved play in the trenches could give the team something to build upon. Terry McLaurin’s status for Sunday is one of the biggest unknowns, as the star wide receiver continues to work his way back from a hamstring injury he sustained in practice last week, and Stefon Diggs was also a surprise addition to the report Wednesday, dealing with a hamstring injury of his own. Bill-in-Bangkok was prescient in his July preview, correctly predicting that Jaxson Dart’s health would be a key concern for New York in 2026. Unfortunately, the Giants’ quarterback sustained a knee injury in Week 2 versus the Rams and has already been placed on season-ending injured reserve. Backup quarterback Jameis Winston looked uncomfortable in Matt Nagy’s offense in Week 3 throwing for just 118 passing yards and no TDS , but heated up in Arizona, with 250 passing yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions. Daronte Jones’ blitz-heavy scheme should match up well against Winston’s past performance in the face of pressure. #Commanders blitz 2nd most on passing plays at just under 50% Jameis Winston has a less than 30% success rate vs the blitz. He pushes the ball downfield when blitz but only averages 4.3 air yards per completion. He's only completed two passes 10+ yards downfield against the… pic.twitter.com/EXkc9iw7tP — Deuce_Redzone (@redzoneinthelab) October 7, 2026 The Giants’ 2024 first-round draft pick, and key wide receiver, Malik Nabers got off to a slow start after his delayed recovery from a torn ACL suffered last season, but had a breakout game versus the Cardinals in Week 4, hauling in six catches for 112 yards and a touchdown . He did not practice Wednesday, due to knee soreness. Playing alongside Nabers is tight end Isaiah Likely, who currently leads all tight ends in catches for first downs this season with 13. After an impressive start to the season, Greg Roman’s rushing attack has stalled out after losing Jaxson Dart, and current leading Giants rusher Cam Skattebo has averaged 3.1 yards per carry over the last three games. Currently, one of New York’s greatest assets on offense is time of possession , where the Giants rank 2nd overall. Part of their ranking comes from defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson’s ball-hawking secondary . The Giants defense is currently tied for first place in the league for interceptions with six. It also ranks second in pass breakups, and is tied for 3rd in overall turnovers. The defense lost edge defender Brian Burns in Week 2, but Wilson leaned into the blitz more in Week 4 with a 51.3% blitz rate, and first-round selections Abdul Carter and rookie Avrell Reese responded with some big plays. Arvell Reese is no longer fighting for DROY, he’s fighting for DPOY after today: • 66 total defensive snaps (led team) • 9 total tackles (led team) • 3 PD’s (led team) • 5 STOPS (led team) • 6 receptions allowed (36 total yards) • 1 INT (led team) The Giants rookie LB’s… pic.twitter.com/elheLdUxRS — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) October 4, 2026 Time of possession is a concern for a Commanders defense which has been prone to wearing down over the course of a game. Per ESPN’s John Keim , Washington’s defense is tied for last in second-half scoring, allowing 17.8 ppg after halftime, while ranking 22nd in the first half at 12.8 points per game. The defense will be looking to limit the Giants scoring after surrendering 30 or more points to each of their last three opponents. Cornerback Trey Amos has been designated to return from injured reserve, but it would be hard to imagine that he’s available after practicing just once since suffering a fractured fibula last season. Safety Nick Cross should be back, which would be a boost for a secondary that played better with a revamped lineup in Week 4. Fans will have to wait and see about defensive lineman Charles Omenihu’s availability for Sunday’s game. Along with Javon Kinlaw and Tim Settle, Omenihu has been a force in the interior of the defense, while edge Odafe Oweh is having a strong start to the season with eight pressures, two sacks, a forced fumble and one fumble recovery over the first four games. For the first time this season, Washington is the favorite in a matchup and will have several key players returning to the lineup, including Jayden Daniels. The timing couldn’t be better, as the Commanders desperately need to win this divisional matchup in order to keep their season from veering further off course. Betting Lines Oddsmakers have established the home team as the favorite for this matchup. They played the Titans and Cardinals (who were ranked 27th & 29th in ESPN’s latest Football Power Index ) at Met Life Stadium in the two weeks immediately prior to the game in Washington, so Big Blue could enter this game feeling pretty good about themselves and their new coaching staff. The All-Time Series Numbers This rivalry is the oldest that Washington has in the NFL ( beating the Cardinals by a week; the Bears by 3 weeks; and the Packers by 5 weeks ), and it has survived one relocation and a total of 4 different team monikers on the part of the Washington franchise. The birth of the rivalry The Giants have been playing football since 1925, and they were the second team to play against the Boston…
